```md
  (`hm_apu_read`) runs the chip about 4 cycles a turn; when the waiting
  adds up to a whole frame, the frame ends right there and the NMI
  interrupts the wait, as on the console (the start-up upload of the sound
  program takes about 160 frames, almost 3 seconds, like the real thing).
- **The chips.** The picture chip (PPU), the DMA unit and the sound chip
  (its SPC700 and DSP) are the recompilation runner's, compiled unchanged;
  `native/hw.c` is the memory map (LoROM: the ROM, the WRAM, the battery
  RAM) and the CPU's registers (NMI, multiplier and divider, pads, DMA).
- **What differs from the console.** The C takes no time, so a frame
  whose work would not fit in 1/60 s on the console (loading a map,
  the night) does not drop frames here; the NMI comes only at the waits.
  The NMI draws a random number every frame (`UpdateGraphics` calls
  `GetRNG`), so the random numbers drift from the console's after the
  first slow frame; everything else follows. Measured against the
  recompilation at the same points of the title screen (the start of each
  stage), the whole WRAM matches except the random numbers, the bytes they
  decide and the stack.
- **Around the game.** `launcher.c` (the ROM the first time, Options, Controls,
  Improvements, Save states) and `pause.c` (the pause menu) are drawn on a
  256x224 canvas (`ui.c`) and run inside `g_hm_frame_hook`: the game stands
  still at a frame's end while the sound chip goes on playing. `mods.c` is
  the recompilation's improvements; they touch the WRAM between frames,
  only with values the game itself writes, plus three hooks in the C
  (`g_hm_oam_right/left` in PrepareOAMData for widescreen, `g_hm_no_ending`
  in MapEvent_PlayerHouse for the endless game, `g_hm_year_suffix` in DrawSaveFileLine
  for "4th", "5th"...) whose defaults are the ROM's, so the checker sees no
  difference.
- **The clean point.** At the start of every GameLoop frame (`main` is
  about to call `hm_GameLoop`) no routine is half done, only the WRAM, the
  registers and the chips: save states are made there (`hw.c`,
  `native_state_save`) and loaded back with a `longjmp` from anywhere (a
  frame inside a wait, the launcher). The endless game uses the same: it
  keeps the machine on the evening of Summer 29, Year 3, lets the ending
  play, and goes back there with `$0973 = 2` (on to the next day, as when
  sleeping) and the ending's date check off once.

---

## 6. Bugs and quirks of the original game

Things the game does wrong or oddly, found while decompiling:

1. **A hidden `BRK`** in the cows' night ($83:BDE1). If a cow was left
   outside and there was also a broken-fence night, the X register is left
   in 8 bits. Then an instruction is read one byte short and the processor
   executes a `BRK` (an error interrupt).
2. **The ending's score counts wrong**:
   - Hearts and shipped crops are **cut off** instead of capped: 512
     turnips shipped are worth 0 points and 600 hearts count as 88.
   - Only the low 16 bits of the money count: with 655,360 G your money
     is worth 0.
3. **Hang with 10 effects.** If the 10 effect places are in use and
   another is needed, the game gets stuck in a jump to itself ($81:A528).
4. **The die is not fair** (see 5.1).
5. **"21th", "22th", "23th"** in the date.
6. **Any unknown item "works"** as a tool.
7. **The gold axe** skips the "no finds today" check.
8. **The gold sickle in winter** does not advance its step when it lands on
   a tile it could cut.
9. **The horse** uses a different "is it on this map?" rule from the other
   animals.
10. **The grown-grass counter** only goes down in the first 4 rows of the
    field.
11. **`ChangeStamina`** decides the sign from the caller's N flag.
12. **`ChangeMoney` reads the amount twice:** it keeps the second, and the
    argument's first 3 bytes are ignored. And if the result would be
    negative, it sets the money to 0 instead of refusing.
13. **Unused commands:** the command table points three times at
    `ResetFlag`, so `ResetFlagD` and `ResetFlagDD` are never reached;
    `Event_ReturnToolsToShed` (puts the tools back in the shed) is not in the table
    either.
14. **`RemoveProgrammedDMA` uses the whole A as an index.** In 8-bit mode,
    `TAX` copies the hidden high byte of A too, so the channel table is
    read at (high byte : channel). It works only because every caller has
    0 there.
15. **The width of the letters is ignored.** The printer passes "wide
    letter: yes / no" to `DrawLetter` and `AdvanceLetterCursor`, but both
    start by setting it to 0. Every letter is 8 pixels wide. (Probably a
    leftover of the Japanese version, whose characters were 16 wide.)
16. **After a number or a name the printer skips two codes in 8 bits**
    (only the low byte of the position), so in a text of more than 256
    codes it would jump backwards (no text seen so far is that long).
17. **The cow that goes from the farm to the barn gets a wrong position.**
    The table of barn places has x and y for each cow, but this code reads
    the same word twice (it forgets to move to the next one), so the
    position written for the cow is (x, x).
18. **The flag "a save was reset"** ($7F1F60 bit $0800) is only set when
    *both* slots fail the check, not when one does (the code looks at slot
    1's result only on slot 2's failure path).
19. **The camera's speed cap looks at the wrong side.** Going down (or
    right), the speed is capped by the camera's position, that is, the
    distance from the *top*, not what is left to the bottom; going up (or
    left) it is capped by the distance to the *bottom* limit. Since the
    camera moves one or two pixels per frame, it only shows in the first
    pixel or two of a map.
20. **A signed division nobody uses.** `DivisionSigned` ($83:80D0) divides
    with signs (the quotient negative when one of the two is; the remainder
    always positive), but nothing in the game calls it. It is rewritten all
    the same.
21. **Pad 2, read with pad 1.** `ReadJoypad` works out pad 2's "let go"
    buttons ($0136) from pad 1's register ($4218) instead of pad 2's: a typo.
    It does not matter, pad 2 is never used. The same routine also has a
    branch that never runs (when $00 is not 0) that would read only the low
    bytes of the pads.

22. **A sum thrown away.** The flower shop's shelf loops do `TYA; CLC;
    ADC #5` and then `TYA` again, so the sum is lost and the item is just
    Y + 1. Maybe the shelves were meant to start at item 5 at first.
23. **A loop that never ends.** When a piece gives its graphics slot back,
    the game waits while the slot's counter is 0 before lowering it (`LDA;
    BEQ` to itself, `ReleaseSpriteSlot`). At 0 it would hang forever; it never
    happens because a slot being given back is always in use.
24. **A flag that is never cleared.** On entering the town with
    `$7F1F60` bit 10 set, `MapEvent_Town` starts a script and means to
    clear the bit: `LDA.L $7F1F60; AND #$FBFF; STA.B $60`. The store goes
    to the direct page ($60) instead of $7F1F60, so the bit stays set and
    the script starts every time the town is entered (until something else
    clears it).
25. **The wrong bit.** On the farm, a fall event (group $18, on the
    visitor days) checks `$7F1F6A` bit 8 to know whether it was seen, but
    marks bit 7. So it comes back on every such day until something else
    sets bit 8.
26. **A text read with the wrong width.** In the shipper's visit (player
    action $46), when the low word of the day's shipping money is not 0
    the branch to the text keeps A in 16 bits, so `LDA #$00; STA $0191`
    is read as `LDA #$8D00; STA ($01),Y`: $8D00 is written wherever
    `($01),Y` points and `$0191` keeps its old value.
27. **A search with no end.** Picking an egg from the coop (action $53)
    looks for the nest in the column of the tile in front among 13; if
    none is there it jumps to itself for ever (`$81:F856`).
28. **Three places to spin for ever.** The piece loader (`LoadQueuedSpritePieces`)
    jumps to itself when no graphics slot is free, when a slot number is
    $2000 or more, and on the 32nd piece of a frame (its copy list has room
    for 31). Like 23, they are dead ends the game's own limits keep away
    from: the budget lets fewer pieces through per frame.
29. **HDMA switched off every frame.** In the NMI, after the sprite pieces
    (`CopySpritePiecesToVRAM` returns with a 16-bit A), `UpdateGraphics`
    clears `$9A` and `$420B` with 16-bit stores: they also clear `$9B` and
    `$420C`, HDMAEN, so every frame with work to do ends with HDMA off.
30. **A JSL to a routine that ends with RTS.** The names screen
    (`NamesScreen`, `$82:E8E7`) calls `DrawScreenBar` with JSL, but it
    returns with RTS: the bank byte the JSL pushed stays on the stack. The
    names screen never returns, so it does no harm.
31. **A loop of one instruction.** `UnusedEndlessLoop` is a BRA to itself. Nothing
    calls it.
32. **Unreachable code in the title screen.** After the parents' scene's
    loop (`$82:D99A`-`$82:D9B2`), a count of `$168` frames and a fade out
    that no jump reaches.
33. **The last day by hand.** Holding L, R and Select (`$0124` =
    `$2030`) when the night ends sets the date to summer 30 of the third
    year: the next morning is the ending.
34. **A name with nowhere to go.** If `$099F` is not 0-6 when a name is
    done, the names screen goes round for ever looking for its routine.

## 7. Differences found in the recompilation

- **Wider sprites on screen (on purpose).** For widescreen, the
  recompilation changes `PrepareOAMData`'s on-screen test: instead of X in
  -16..255 it asks `hm_ws_oam_left_limit()` / `hm_ws_oam_right_limit()`
  (the "oam left / oam right" overrides of the build). The rewrite keeps
  the original's 256 pixels, so it is checked against the interpreter
  (HM_INTERP), which runs the original code. The interpreter itself also
  clears X's and Y's high byte when the indexes go 8-bit and back, as the
  console does, while the compiled game keeps it (next point): preparations
  of routines checked that way set that byte to 0.

- **`SEP #$10` does not clear the high byte of X and Y.** On the real
  SNES, switching the indexes to 8 bits clears their high byte; in the
  recompilation it is kept. It does not seem to change anything visible
  in the game, but the checker notices it. The rewrites imitate the
  recompilation, which is the reference.
- **A 16-bit read at the last byte of bank $7E.** On the SNES, reading two
  bytes at `$7E:FFFF` takes the second from `$7F:0000`; in the
  recompilation it comes from `$7E:0000`. The game never does it (it was
  found only by random tests of the scroll routines, which then avoid it).
- **The interpreter gives up quietly.** Routines with no compiled body run
  in the recompiler's interpreter, which stops a routine after 2 million
  steps (to escape endless loops) and still reports it as finished. The
  sound uploads take far more while the chip answers, so the checker now
  counts a run as finished only if the routine really returned, and the
  fuzzer raises that limit. The log of the sound chip's traffic was also
  made 64 times bigger (4 million reads and writes): every wait reads the
  port thousands of times.

## 8. Glossary

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ROM | the contents of the cartridge |
| WRAM | the console's working memory |
| SRAM | the cartridge's memory where the game is saved |
| register | internal box of the processor (A, X, Y...) |
| flag | bit left by operations (C, Z, N) |
| bank | 64 KB block of memory; `$7F:1F19` = bank $7F |
| stack | memory area where return addresses are kept |
| JSL / JSR | call a routine (long / short) |
| direct page | 256 bytes of fast variables (`$72`, `$CC`...) |
| long pointer | 3-byte address kept in memory |
| frame | each picture; the game runs at 60 per second |
| NMI | the hardware's signal at the end of each frame |
| DMA | a memory copy done by the hardware |
| sprite | a figure that moves over the background |
| slot (CC) | structure where an event script runs |
| fuzzing | testing a routine with random inputs |
| interpreter | the part of the recompilation that runs, instruction by instruction, what is not compiled |
| open bus | reading an address where nothing answers: you get the last value seen on the bus |
| BG3 | the third background layer; the game uses it for text |
| port | a byte shared by two processors (the CPU and the sound chip) |
| handshake | the "ready / here it is / done" exchange over the ports |
| palette | the 256 colours the screen can use at a time |
| CGRAM | the console's memory where the palette is kept |
| LZSS | a way to compress: "copy this byte" or "copy that many bytes from what you already wrote" |
```

`HOW_TO_PLAY.txt`:

```txt
Harvest Moon (SNES) - native build, v0.2.0 beta
===============================================

The game runs on its code rewritten in C. No ROM and nothing taken from
it is included: you need your own legal copy of Harvest Moon (USA). The
first time, the program asks for it (.sfc or .smc), checks it and
remembers it.

WINDOWS 10/11
    Open HarvestMoonNative.exe. If Windows says "Windows protected your
    PC" (the program is not signed with a paid certificate): More info >
    Run anyway.

MAC (Apple Silicon or Intel, macOS 11+)
    Double-click "Harvest Moon.command". If macOS says it is from an
    unidentified developer: right-click it > Open > Open (or, in
    Terminal: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine on this folder).

ANDROID (phones, tablets, the AYN Thor)
    Open the .apk on the device to install it. If Android says it cannot
    install unknown apps from this source: Settings > allow it, then
    Install (and Install anyway if Play Protect asks). Choose your ROM with
    Android's file picker. On the AYN Thor launch the app on the top
    screen: the pause menu stays on the lower one while you play.

LINUX
    ./HarvestMoonNative  (or ./HarvestMoonNative /path/to/your/rom.sfc)

Everything starts OFF: the game is the console's. Turn on what you like
in the launcher (Esc): Improvements (widescreen, the Harvest Moon 64-style
pause menu, the crop bag, your wife's help, fast text, longer days...),
Cheats and Options.

MODS: put each mod (a folder with .ips or .bps patches and a mod.ini) in
the mods folder, then turn it on in the launcher's Mods page. How to make
one: mods/MODS.md.

Keys: arrows, X = A, Z = B, S = X, A = Y, C = L, V = R, Enter = Start,
Right Shift = Select. Esc launcher, M pause menu, Tab fast forward,
F11 full screen, F1-F10 load a state, Shift+F1-F10 save one.
A gamepad works too. Everything can be changed in Controls.

The source, and scripts to build it yourself:
https://github.com/RodoLy/HarvestMoonSnesDecomp
This is a beta: please report problems in the repository's Issues.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
```

`README.es.md`:

```md
# HarvestMoonSnesDecomp — Harvest Moon (SNES) reescrito en C

[English](README.md) · **Español**

<!-- progress -->
![Reescrito en C: 100.00%](https://img.shields.io/badge/reescrito%20en%20C-100.00%25-2f855a)

**100.00%** del código del juego reescrito en C y verificado: 45176 de 45176 instrucciones, 778 de 778 rutinas (100.0%).
Se calcula con `python3 tools/progress.py --decomp ../HM-Decomp` sobre el desensamblado de HM-Decomp.
<!-- /progress -->
![plataforma: Windows / macOS / Linux / Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64%20%7C%20Windows%20ARM64%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20Android-blue)
![ROM: no incluida](https://img.shields.io/badge/ROM-no%20incluida-red)

Todo el juego reescrito, rutina por rutina, en C que una persona puede leer
y modificar, y **jugable solo sobre ese C**. Cada rutina se comprobó contra
la original byte por byte (toda la memoria, los registros del procesador y
los del DMA deben quedar idénticos). En sentido estricto es una
*reimplementación* en C: el juego se escribió en ensamblador 65816, así que
no había C original que recuperar. Parte del desensamblado de la comunidad
[HM-Decomp](https://github.com/ElisaS-Codes/HM-Decomp) (ElisaS-Codes y
DasK) y es proyecto hermano de
[HarvestMoonSNESRecomp](https://github.com/RodriLoy/HarvestMoonSNESRecomp).

## Jugarlo

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Necesitas tu propia copia legal de Harvest Moon (USA).** No se incluye
> la ROM ni nada sacado de ella: la primera vez el programa te pide tu
> copia, la revisa y la recuerda. Por favor no pidas ROMs.

**[⬇ Descargar la última versión](https://github.com/RodoLy/HarvestMoonSnesDecomp/releases/latest)** · Novedades: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)

| | Descarga | O compílalo tú |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows** 10/11 | `…-Windows.zip`: descomprime y abre `HarvestMoonNative.exe` | `build.bat` |
| **Mac** (macOS 11+) | `…-Mac.zip`: descomprime y doble clic en `Harvest Moon.command` | `build_mac.command` |
| **Android** 8+ | `…-Android.apk`: ábrelo en el equipo para instalarlo | `build_android.bat` (en Windows) |
| **Linux** (x86_64) | `…-Linux.tar.gz`: descomprime y ejecuta `./HarvestMoonNative` | [ver abajo](#compilar-y-comprobar) |

> [!NOTE]
> **La primera vez tu computadora o teléfono te va a advertir: es normal.**
> Los programas no están firmados con un certificado de pago y el APK no
> viene de la Play Store. Windows: **Más información → Ejecutar de todas
> formas**. Mac: clic derecho → **Abrir**. Android: permite instalar apps

**En Android** los controles se dibujan en la pantalla con el aspecto de
los menús del juego (se ocultan cuando usas un mando o los botones del
equipo). En un equipo de dos pantallas como la **AYN Thor**, el menú de
pausa queda en vivo en la pantalla de abajo y se usa tocándolo (abre la

## El código

Las 778 rutinas del juego están en `src/`, un archivo por sistema (el
clima, la granja, los animales, los eventos, los menús…), con nombres que
se leen: `src/hm_vars.h` nombra una sola vez cada variable que comparten
los archivos, con una nota de para qué sirve, y `src/hm_regs.h` los
registros de la consola. **[GUIDE.es.md](GUIDE.es.md)** explica cómo
funciona el juego por dentro, para quien no sabe nada de esto, con todo lo
descubierto en el camino (las probabilidades del clima, los errores del
juego original…). En inglés: [GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md).

- `src/` — las rutinas, y el comprobador que las compara con las
  originales (`hm_decomp.c`).
- `native/` — la versión jugable: la ventana, el sonido y los controles
  (`main.c`), el launcher, las mejoras, y los chips de imagen y sonido de
  la consola (`native/chips/`, de snesrecomp, sin cambios).
- `tools/`, `scripts/` — las pruebas y sus recorridos.
- `DECOMPILATION.md` (el método) y `STATUS.md` (notas).

### Compilar y comprobar

```
cmake -S native -B build/native && cmake --build build/native
build/native/HarvestMoonNative /ruta/a/tu/rom.sfc
```

Para Windows desde Linux agrega `-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=native/mingw-w64.cmake`.
Para comparar las rutinas con las originales, con
[HarvestMoonSNESRecomp](https://github.com/RodriLoy/HarvestMoonSNESRecomp)
y HM-Decomp junto a esta carpeta:

```
tools/build.sh --rom /ruta/a/tu/rom.sfc
HM_ROM=/ruta/a/tu/rom.sfc tools/check.sh 2000 10
```

## Por qué existe

Harvest Moon es uno de mis juegos favoritos. Después de la recompilación
quise ir más lejos: entender el juego rutina por rutina y que se jugara
solo sobre ese código.

**Este proyecto se hizo con ayuda de IA.** Yo lo dirigí y supervisé cada
paso: qué hacer, cómo debía comportarse, probarlo en mi propia PC y decidir
qué se queda. Si no te gusta que se haya hecho con ayuda de IA, está bien:
simplemente no lo uses.

## Aviso legal

Este repositorio y sus versiones **no contienen la ROM ni nada generado a
partir de ella** (ni código, gráficos, textos o música del juego): los
programas leen tu copia al iniciar. Necesitas tu propia copia legal de
*Harvest Moon (USA)*: SHA-256
`73a3aa87ddd5ce5df5ba51292316f42b6e128280179b0a1b11b4dcddc17d4163`.

## Licencia

[PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](LICENSE), la misma que HarvestMoonSNESRecomp:
libre para uso no comercial. Cubre solo el código de este repositorio, no
el juego ni sus datos.
```

`README.md`:

```md
# HarvestMoonSnesDecomp — Harvest Moon (SNES) rewritten in C

**English** · [Español](README.es.md)

<!-- progress -->
![Rewritten in C: 100.00%](https://img.shields.io/badge/rewritten%20in%20C-100.00%25-2f855a)

**100.00%** of the game's code rewritten in C and verified: 45176 of 45176 instructions, 778 of 778 routines (100.0%).
Computed with `python3 tools/progress.py --decomp ../HM-Decomp` over the HM-Decomp disassembly.
<!-- /progress -->
![platform: Windows / macOS / Linux / Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20x64%20%7C%20Windows%20ARM64%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20Android-blue)
![ROM: not included](https://img.shields.io/badge/ROM-not%20included-red)

The whole game rewritten, routine by routine, as C a person can read and
change, and **playable on that C alone**. Every routine was checked against
the original byte for byte (the whole memory, the CPU registers and the DMA
registers must come out identical). Strictly speaking it is a C
*reimplementation*: the game was written in 65816 assembly, so there was no
original C to recover. It builds on the community disassembly
[HM-Decomp](https://github.com/ElisaS-Codes/HM-Decomp) (ElisaS-Codes and
DasK) and is a sister project of
[HarvestMoonSNESRecomp](https://github.com/RodriLoy/HarvestMoonSNESRecomp).

## Play it

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **You need your own, legally obtained copy of Harvest Moon (USA).** No
> ROM and nothing taken from it is included: the first time, the program
> asks for your copy, checks it and remembers it. Please don't ask for ROMs.

**[⬇ Download the latest version](https://github.com/RodoLy/HarvestMoonSnesDecomp/releases/latest)** · What's new: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)

| | Download | Or build it yourself |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows** 10/11 | `…-Windows.zip`: unzip, open `HarvestMoonNative.exe` | `build.bat` |
| **Mac** (macOS 11+) | `…-Mac.zip`: unzip, double-click `Harvest Moon.command` | `build_mac.command` |
| **Android** 8+ | `…-Android.apk`: open it on the device to install it | `build_android.bat` (on Windows) |
| **Linux** (x86_64) | `…-Linux.tar.gz`: unpack, run `./HarvestMoonNative` | [see below](#building-and-checking) |

> [!NOTE]
> **The first time, your computer or phone will warn you: that is
> expected.** The programs are not signed with a paid certificate and the
> APK is not from the Play Store. Windows: **More info → Run anyway**. Mac:
> right-click → **Open**. Android: allow installing apps from your browser
> or file manager. The downloads are built by GitHub from this public
> source (the **Actions** tab) and each release lists their SHA-256.

**On Android** the controls are drawn on the screen in the look of the
game's menus (they hide when you use a gamepad or the device's buttons).
On a two-screen device like the **AYN Thor**, the pause menu stays live on
the lower screen, used by touch (launch the app on the top screen).

| Touch controls | The AYN Thor's two screens |
|---|---|
| ![Touch controls](docs/screenshots/android_touch.png) | ![Two screens](docs/screenshots/android_two_screens.png) |

## What it brings

**Everything starts off**, so the game is exactly the console's: turn on
what you like in the launcher.

### A launcher in the look of the game

The program's first screen, drawn at the SNES's resolution with the game's
wooden frames; in the game it opens with **Esc** (or L3 / Guide), with the
game paused. In English, Spanish and Italian.

- **Options**: full screen, window size, sharp or exact pixels, vsync,
  widescreen, sprites without flicker, volume, fast-forward speed, language.
- **Controls**: **gamepads are mapped automatically** (Xbox, PlayStation,
  Switch Pro, 8BitDo… USB or Bluetooth): plug one in and play. Every
  button and key can still be changed.
- **Save states**: 10 slots (F1–F10 load, Shift+F1–F10 save).

| Launcher | Options | Controls | Gamepad |
|---|---|---|---|
| ![Launcher](docs/screenshots/launcher.png) | ![Options](docs/screenshots/options.png) | ![Controls](docs/screenshots/controls.png) | ![Gamepad](docs/screenshots/gamepad.png) |

### Widescreen

More of the map at the sides instead of black bars, as wide as your screen
(16:9 or 16:10), the start screens included.

| Original (4:3) | Widescreen |
|---|---|
| ![4:3](docs/screenshots/widescreen_off.png) | ![16:9](docs/screenshots/widescreen.png) |

### Harvest Moon 64-style pause menu *(M or R3)*

Date, money and stamina; your tools and the tool shed; each girl's hearts;
the farm's status; and every cow and chicken with its own sprite, hearts
and today's care. All pictures are the game's own, read from your ROM.

| Inventory | Hearts | Farm | Animals |
|---|---|---|---|
| ![Inventory](docs/screenshots/pause_tools.png) | ![Hearts](docs/screenshots/pause_hearts.png) | ![Farm](docs/screenshots/pause_farm.png) | ![Animals](docs/screenshots/pause_animals.png) |

### More improvements

- **Crop bag** (with the pause menu): Q keeps what you carry, up to 9;
  held at the shipping box, it ships them all.
- **Your wife helps**: married, with her ten hearts, she offers to help
  for a day, three or a week; mornings she feeds the animals and waters
  (half of the work at most, each plant as long as you would).
- **Her old clothes some days**: one day in two she wears the clothes from
  before the wedding.
- **Walk through crops** (they sway as you pass) and **one seed at a time**.
- **Mouse controls**: click to use a tool, walk or talk.
- **Endless game**, **fast text**, **longer days**, **OPTIONS on the title
  screen**, **fast forward** (Tab) and **cheats**.

| Crop bag | Your wife offers to help | Her old clothes |
|---|---|---|
| ![Crop bag](docs/screenshots/crop_bag.png) | ![Your wife helps](docs/screenshots/wife_help.png) | ![Her old clothes](docs/screenshots/wife_clothes.png) |

| Improvements | Cheats | OPTIONS on the title |
|---|---|---|
| ![Improvements](docs/screenshots/improvements.png) | ![Cheats](docs/screenshots/cheats.png) | ![OPTIONS](docs/screenshots/title_options.png) |

### Mods from the community

New pictures, text, maps or music as IPS / BPS patches, in a folder inside
`mods/`; the launcher's **Mods** page turns each one on or off. Your ROM
file is never changed. How to make one: [docs/MODS.md](docs/MODS.md).

![The Mods page](docs/screenshots/mods.png)

### Keys

| Key | SNES / action |
|---|---|
| Arrows · X Z S A · C V | D-pad · A B X Y · L R |
| Enter · Right Shift | Start · Select |
| Esc · M · Tab (held) | Launcher · pause menu · fast forward |
| F1…F10 · Shift+F1…F10 · F11 | Load · save a state · full screen |

## The code

All 778 routines of the game are in `src/`, one file per system (the
weather, the farm, the animals, the events, the menus…), with readable
names: `src/hm_vars.h` names once every variable the files share, with a
note on what it is for, and `src/hm_regs.h` the console's registers.
**[GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md)** explains how the game works inside, for someone
new to it, with everything found along the way (the weather's odds, the
original game's bugs…). Spanish: [GUIDE.es.md](GUIDE.es.md).

- `src/` — the routines, and the checker that compares them with the
  original (`hm_decomp.c`).
- `native/` — the playable build: the window, sound and pads (`main.c`),
  the launcher, the improvements, and the console's picture and sound chips
  (`native/chips/`, from snesrecomp, unmodified).
- `tools/`, `scripts/` — the checks and their playthroughs.
- `DECOMPILATION.md` (the method) and `STATUS.md` (notes), in Spanish.

### Building and checking

```
cmake -S native -B build/native && cmake --build build/native
build/native/HarvestMoonNative /path/to/your/rom.sfc
```

For Windows from Linux add `-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=native/mingw-w64.cmake`.
To check the routines against the original, with
[HarvestMoonSNESRecomp](https://github.com/RodriLoy/HarvestMoonSNESRecomp)
and HM-Decomp next to this folder:

```
tools/build.sh --rom /path/to/your/rom.sfc
HM_ROM=/path/to/your/rom.sfc tools/check.sh 2000 10
```

## Why it exists

Harvest Moon is one of my favourite games. After the recompilation I
wanted to go further: understand the game routine by routine, and have it
play on that code alone.

**This project was made with the help of AI.** I directed it and
supervised every step: what to do, how it should behave, testing it on my
own PC and deciding what stays. If you don't like that it was made with
AI's help, that's fine: just don't use it.
```

```md
# Estado de la descompilación (al 29-oct-2026)

Memoria del proyecto para retomarlo sin perder nada. El clima y el daño
del clima a la granja ya están reescritos y verificados. Porcentaje actual
en el README (`tools/progress.py`).

## Hecho

- **Proyecto separado** del juego. Se compila con `tools/build.sh` (usa la
  recompilación como base, sin modificarla) y se prueba con `tools/check.sh`.
- **Nombres**: 522 rutinas renombradas con los nombres de HM-Decomp
  (`data/decomp_names.tsv`).
- **Comprobador**: cada rutina reescrita se compara byte por byte con la
  original, en partidas reales (`HM_DECOMP_CHECK=1`) y con entradas al azar
  (`HM_DECOMP_FUZZ=<cuadro>:<veces>`).
- **Todas las rutinas reescritas y verificadas (778)** (0 diferencias):

## El clima (hecho el 19-oct-2026)

Verificado con 10 semillas × 2.000 llamadas al azar por rutina, más una
partida con 10 noches forzadas en fechas elegidas (`scripts/nights.txt`):
0 diferencias. Las entradas al azar producen todos los resultados posibles
del clima (soleado, lluvia, nieve, huracán, las dos tormentas del año 1 y
los seis festivales).

Lo aprendido:
- **RNGReturn0toA(n)** no es del todo justo: con n = 6, el 0 sale con 43
  de los 256 valores del RNG. "1 de cada n" en el juego es "salió 0".
- **Tormentas del año 1** (códigos 4 y 5): invierno, segura el día 8 (se
  decide el 7) o 1/8 antes; verano, segura el día 30 (se decide el 29) o
  1/30 antes. Cada una se marca vista en $7F1F64 (bit 1 y bit 0).
- **Huracán**: solo verano, 1/30; con el caparazón de tortuga ($7F1F6C bit
  $1000) 1/60. Nunca se decide el día 30.
- Lluvia 1/6 primavera, 1/10 verano y otoño. Nieve 1/3 solo en invierno.
- **WeatherTomorrow no tiene cuerpo compilado**: la recompilación la corre
  en su intérprete (igual que NightReset). Por eso no lleva envoltorio; está
  marcada `HM_INTERP` y la prueba al azar la compara llamando al original
  con `interp_tier_dispatch`. En vivo solo se comprueban las rutinas
  compiladas que llama.
- Las reescrituras ahora imitan también la **pila**: PHA/PHY y los marcos de
  JSL quedan en la WRAM y el comprobador los compara. Un JSL guarda el banco
  actual (PB) y cambia al de la rutina llamada (`hm_jsl` / `hm_rtl`).

## Daño del clima a la granja (hecho el 19-oct-2026)

Verificado con 10 semillas: 2.000 llamadas al azar por rutina, y 40 granjas
enteras al azar por semilla para las dos rutinas que recorren las 4.096
casillas. 0 diferencias.

- La granja es una cuadrícula de 64 × 64 casillas en $7E:A4E6 (una casilla =
  16 × 16 píxeles). Códigos: 02 tierra, 05 cerca, 06 cerca rota, 07/08
  tierra arada, 1D pasto recién sembrado, 1E-6F cultivos, 70-79 pasto
  creciendo (79 = crecido), A0+ no es campo.
- Probabilidades por noche (tabla $82:8298; fila = clima):
  lluvia cercas 1/96; nieve cercas 1/64; huracán cercas 1/8, pasto 1/16,
  cultivos 1/4; tormenta de invierno del año 1 cercas 1/8, cultivos 1/4;
  la tormenta de verano del año 1 no hace daño; año nuevo pasto 1/64,
  cultivos 1/32.
- Rareza: el contador de pasto crecido ($092E) solo baja en las primeras
  4 filas (compara 16 bits con el byte alto del índice de casilla).
- ClimateFarmDamageCheck no cabe en un cuadro: en el juego real se pausa y
  sigue en el siguiente, así que su llamada real sale "omitida". Se verifica
  con la prueba al azar (que pone el reloj del cuadro en 0 y no comprueba
  las llamadas anidadas, que tienen su propia prueba).

## Crecimiento de los cultivos (hecho el 20-oct-2026)

Verificado con 10 semillas × 40 granjas enteras al azar (con fechas,
lluvia y el primer día de invierno). 0 diferencias.

- Las casillas van en pares: código par = seco, el impar siguiente = regado.
  07/08 tierra arada, 1E/1F semillas, 20-6F etapas de cultivo; 39, 53, 61 y
  6F son tomate, maíz, papa y nabo maduros (regados).
- De noche (NightlyFarmTilesCheck): la lluvia riega lo seco (+1); lo regado
  sin lluvia se seca (-1); un cultivo regado crece una etapa (+1) y, si
  llueve, queda regado otra vez (+1). En otoño los regados solo se secan; en
  invierno nada crece. El pasto (70-9F) crece cada noche salvo en invierno;
  7C (pasto cortado) vuelve a 73.
- Tierra vacía (01/02), primavera y verano, cada 4 días: 1/256 de que salga
  hierba o piedra (03). Cerca rota: 1/8 de poner $0196 bit $0400.
- Primer día de invierno (MonthlyFarmTilesCheck): cultivos → 07, pasto → 7A.
- CalculateFarmDevelopment (evaluación final) cuenta las casillas con cercas,
  cultivos o pasto en $7F1F56.
- `farm.c` tiene un recorrido de casillas común: `tile_begin` / `tile_end` y
  `FOR_EACH_FARM_TILE`.

## Los animales y los eventos (hecho el 20-oct-2026)

Verificado con 10 semillas (200 noches al azar de CowFeedingAndStatus por
semilla, con 12 vacas, 13 gallinas y todas las banderas al azar) y llamadas
reales de SetEventSlotPointer / ResetCurrentEventSlotLong. 0 diferencias.

- Registro de vaca (16 bytes en $7E:C1C6): +0 estado (01 existe, 02 recién
  nacida, 04 cría, 08 adulta, 10 de mal humor, 20 enferma, 40 preñada, 80
  acaba de parir), +1 banderas del día (80 = poción milagrosa), +2 mapa ($27
  establo), +3 contador, +4 felicidad, +5 días fuera.
- Registro de gallina (8 bytes en $7E:C286): +0 estado (01, 02 huevo, 04
  pollito, 08 gallina, 10 con hambre), +1 mapa ($28 gallinero), +2 contador.
- Eventos: "CC structs" de 64 bytes desde $7E:B586; los guiones están en la
  ROM ($B3:8000: tabla de grupos de 24 bits).
- **Bug del juego** en $83:BDE1 (BRK): ver `cow_after_meal` en animals.c.
- Infraestructura nueva: lectura de ROM y punteros largos (`hm_bus_rd8`,
  `hm_dp_long`), nombres manuales para etiquetas locales
  (`import_decomp_names.py` MANUAL, `progress.py` LOCAL), una rutina por
  cuadro en la prueba al azar (el vigilante de 5 s es por cuadro),
  `HM_DECOMP_DIFF_ALL`, `HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_ONLY`, `HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_CALL`.
  Para trazar el original: `SNESRECOMP_INTERP_PCTRACE=1` (así se encontró
  el BRK).

## La noche, parte lógica (hecho el 20-oct-2026)

Las subrutinas de NightReset que son lógica del juego ya están todas:
clima, granja, animales, nombres de la fecha, la chica favorita, esposa e
hijos, dinero. NightReset misma toca pantalla, sonido y guardado (registros
del hardware y SRAM), que el comprobador no modela, así que queda para
después.

- Hijos: primero 450 corazones, segundo 650 y el primer hijo con 90 días;
  casa nivel 2 ($7F1F64 bit $0080) y 20 días de casados ($7F1F3B). Nace a
  los 60 días de concebido ($7F1F37 / $7F1F39); cada 120 días, cumpleaños
  ($7F1F6C $0100 / $0200). El aniversario: cada 120 días de casados.
- FindMostLovedName: en empate gana la última; las etiquetas de HM-Decomp
  están cruzadas (Ann / Nina).
- HaveLunch y ChangeStamina solo comparan la WRAM (sus registros de salida
  no están modelados).

## Herramientas (hecho el 21-oct-2026)

- Cada mapa tiene una tabla de propiedades de casilla en `[$0D]` (puntero
  largo en la página directa): 4 bytes por tipo de casilla. +1..+2 = qué
  hace la casilla (los bits bajos: qué herramientas funcionan), +2 bit 7 =
  "sin valor por omisión", +3 = desde qué lados (01-08) y en qué estaciones
  (10-80) aplica.
- La regadera se rellena en casillas F0/F9-FD (granja y mapas $3D+) o
  F0/F4 (montaña $10-$13); en los mapas 04-0F y 14-3C no se riega.
- La pintura solo funciona en la granja, en C3 o E2-E4.
- Prueba al azar: cada rutina tiene ahora su propia semilla, así que
  `HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_ONLY` + `HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_CALL` reproducen la llamada exacta.
  Cuidado con leer tablas con índices grandes: si la dirección sale de la
  ROM ($83:40FA...) la original lee registros del hardware y no se puede
  comparar.

- La casilla donde cae la herramienta: CalculateTileInFront (N casillas
  hacia donde mira el jugador: 0 abajo, 1 arriba, 2 = +X, otro = -X) o
  TileAtOffsetFromPlayer (un desplazamiento fijo; las herramientas de oro
  usan la tabla de 9 casillas $82:92FA alrededor del jugador).
- Cambiar una casilla del mapa (mapedit.c): la tabla $81:B363 (6 bytes por
  cambio: gráfico en $A6:A096, filas, columnas, tipo de casilla) dice qué
  poner; DrawTileChange copia el gráfico al mapa BG1 en $7E:2000 y SetTileTypeBlock
  escribe el tipo en $09B6. ChangeMapTile (CODE_81A688) hace todo eso y
  además encola la copia del gráfico a la VRAM con QueueTileGraphicsDMA
  (CODE_81A6C1) → AddProgrammedDMA.
- Siguiente en herramientas: los ToolUsed* (ya tienen ChangeMapTile, que
  usan 27 veces) necesitan CODE_81A500 (crea un objeto; ojo: si los 10
  lugares están ocupados se queda en un bucle infinito, `BRA` a sí mismo en
  $81:A528).

## DMA de video (hecho el 21-oct-2026)

- La cola de "DMA programado" ($80:8A33 AddProgrammedDMA): el juego prepara
  durante el cuadro copias a la VRAM / CGRAM y el NMI las arranca todas
  juntas. Página directa: $27 próximo canal, $28 canales a arrancar (un bit
  cada uno), $29 registro destino ($18 = datos de VRAM), $2A+canal modo de
  dirección de VRAM, $32+2·canal dirección destino, $72-$74 origen, $C7
  bytes que quedan este cuadro (se descuenta leyendo de vuelta el registro
  de tamaño).
- El comprobador ahora guarda, restaura y compara también los registros de
  DMA $4300-$437F (`g_hm_dma_regs`; `hm_bus_rd8/wr8` los alcanzan).
- QueueTileGraphicsDMA: la dirección VRAM del mapa BG1 es $6000 + 2·columna
  + 64·fila, cada pantalla de 32×32; la segunda pantalla horizontal suma
  $3E0 (= $400 − 32) y la vertical $400. Encola dos medias filas por fila
  de 16 px, por los canales 2/3 y luego 0/1.
- Con 0 filas (cambio 0) su bucle daría 32768 vueltas; ChangeMapTile lo
  evita saliendo antes si A = 0.

## Objetos con sprite (hecho el 21-oct-2026)

- **Objetos del juego** ("gobj"): 40 registros de $24 bytes en $019C
  (en uso = $7777, sprite, volteo, X, Y, pieza por pieza el lugar de su
  gráfico). $DC cuenta cuántos se repartieron (solo crece, hasta 40).
  CreateGameObject toma uno libre y carga sus piezas.
- **Sprites**: 0-$261 se describen en el banco $86 (tabla $86:8080) y
  $262-$44F en el $87 ($87:8080). Cada sprite es una lista de piezas (como
  mucho 12), 5 bytes cada una.
- **Gráficos de las piezas**: $7F:0F00 + pieza = en qué lugar de la VRAM
  está ($FF = no cargada); $7E:A320 + 4·lugar = cuántas piezas lo usan. Las
  no cargadas van a una cola circular de 64 en $7E:A220 ($BD escribe, $BB
  lee el cargador del NMI). Si la cola está llena, LoadSpriteComponent
  espera a que el NMI la vacíe (`CMP $BB; BEQ` a sí mismo).
- **Objetos del mapa**: 10 registros de 16 bytes en $7E:B4E6 (los efectos
  de las herramientas; RunItemsOnMap los mueve cada cuadro). SpawnMapObject toma
  uno libre; **con los 10 ocupados el juego se cuelga** ($81:A528). Si no
  hay objeto del juego libre, guarda el número del último creado ($A5 no
  cambia).
- En la partida real estas rutinas salen "omitidas": quien las llama corre
  en el intérprete de la recompilación y el cuerpo compilado le devuelve la
  llamada al instante. Las verifica la prueba al azar.

## Usar las herramientas (hecho el 21-oct-2026)

- Tabla `Tool_Used_Table` en $82:A5C3, una rutina por objeto en la mano
  ($0921); la llama UseToolInHand. Todas JSR/RTS, entran con A de 8 bits.
- Plan común: PreCheckToolSuccess (Square / Line para semillas y oro) →
  ChangeMapTile → SpawnMapObject (efecto) → a veces un hallazgo (evento
  con StartScriptAtTileInFront) → $D4 = 0 y ChangeStamina ($FE = -2, $FF = -1, $FC = -4,
  $F8 = -8).
- Banderas de hallazgos: $7F1F5A ($1000 topo, $2000 rana), $7F1F5C ($0200
  moneda/bolsa del día, $0100 baya del día, $0080 baya del martillo del
  día), $7F1F64 ($0800/$1000 bayas de la azada, $0200 del martillo, $0400
  del hacha), $7F1F66 (las 4 partes de la casa pintadas), $7F1F6A ($0020
  evento del hacha en la montaña). $7F1F60 bit 3: "sin hallazgos" (y
  energía congelada).
- La bandera C importa: con la energía congelada ChangeStamina no la toca,
  así que la deja la última comparación del camino. Las reescrituras la
  llevan (`is`, `below`, `add_c`, `sub_c`).
- ChangeStamina ahora modela sus registros de salida. **Diferencia de la
  recompilación con el SNES real:** su `SEP #$10` no borra el byte alto de
  X/Y (el hardware sí); la reescritura imita a la recompilación.
- `tools/calls.py`: lista los JSR/JSL de una rutina con su dirección de
  retorno leída de la ROM.
- Prueba al azar: la semilla del dado ($0100-$0102) se sortea en cada
  llamada (si no, todas sacan la misma tirada y los hallazgos nunca
  salen); una tabla de propiedades propia en $7F:F000 para que las
  herramientas funcionen; el jugador a 7 casillas del borde (la azada de
  oro mira 6 adelante; fuera del mapa el original lee hardware).
- En vivo no se ven: todo el uso de herramientas corre en el intérprete
  de la recompilación (se pulsa X en el guion, pero el envoltorio no ve la
  llamada). Las verifica la prueba al azar.
- La regadera y el aspersor se hicieron después, cuando el comprobador
  aprendió a grabar el chip de sonido (ver "El chip de sonido").

## Animales en el mapa y el final (hecho el 21-oct-2026)

- PlaceAnimalsOnMap: al entrar a un mapa arranca el guion de cada
  gallina (evento $24+n), vaca ($18+n), perro ($16) y caballo ($17) que
  esté ahí. "Está ahí" agrupa mapas: 00-03, 04-07, 08-0F con 0C-0F,
  10-13, 14-17 con 15-17, 31+; el resto solo el mismo mapa. El caballo no
  tiene el grupo 14-17. Con lluvia ($0196 bit 1) las vacas que no están en
  el establo usan otros guiones ($17 / $2F / 9). Verificada también en
  vivo (al entrar a mapas en la partida y las noches).
- AddNewChicken / AddNewCow: buscan el primer registro libre; no cambian
  los contadores $7F1F0A/0B. Gallina: 1 comprada, 2 nacida (+1 =
  estación + 4), otro valor = estado $43. Vaca nacida: estado 3, felicidad
  de $7F1F2B, +70 de felicidad al jugador.
- RanchMasteryCalculator ($83:F26D, se llega con JMP; sin cuerpo
  compilado: `HM_INTERP | HM_JSR`). Errores del original documentados en
  src/ending.c (AND #$1FF en corazones y envíos; dinero de 16 bits).
- El fuzz ahora pone PB en el banco de la rutina también para las JSR
  (hacía falta para las que corren por el intérprete).
- `tools/candidates.py`: lista las rutinas que faltan, su tamaño, qué
  llaman que aún no está hecho y si tocan hardware.
- (La regadera y el aspersor ya están: ver "El chip de sonido".)

## Comandos de los guiones de evento (hecho el 21-oct-2026)

- Tabla `EventInstructionPointers` ($84:9419): 90 comandos, uno por byte
  de guion. $C9-$CB = posición en el guion (cada comando la avanza con
  CLC; ADC, y eso deja en A y C); $CC-$CE = el slot. Los argumentos van
  después del byte del comando.
- Hechos 25: la gallina y el perro de cada cuadro, y 23 chicos (saltos,
  pruebas, reloj, jugador, slots, banderas $7F1F7A).
- Perro: ánimo en $7F1F58 (bits 1, 2, 4, 8, $10), cambia cada $78
  cuadros con el byte al azar $DE; $7F1F60 bit $10 lo llama.
- Gallina: levantarla con A (objeto $26 pollito, $25 gallina); venta
  ($7F1F5A bit 3, precio $32); contador $093B+2n hasta $200.
- Verificados también en vivo: los guiones reales de la partida y de las
  noches ejecutan muchos de estos comandos (miles de saltos).
- Prueba al azar: el guion se arma en $7F:F000 con bytes al azar; para
  los Jumpif con dirección, el banco se fuerza a $7E/$7F, y 1 de cada 4
  veces se fuerza la igualdad para que la rama del salto se pruebe.
- HM-Decomp anota Event_TimeStopped en ;808A0D; es $84:8A0D (nombre
  manual). `progress.py` ahora guarda el texto de las etiquetas con
  dirección para poder encontrarlas en `LOCAL`.

## Más comandos de evento (hecho el 21-oct-2026)

- 31 más: valores en cualquier dirección (Jumpif*Value*, SetFlag,
  StoreValue, SetValue*), sumas con tope (UNKTextrelated 0-255,
  UNKCCchanges14 0-999), ChangeMoney, esperas (UNKCCchanges12/13 con
  $08FD/$08FF, UNK2), levantar cosas (topo $29, pescado $07, objeto $08),
  caminatas (UNKCCchanges4/6/10), transiciones, objetos en la mano,
  banderas.
- Nombres corregidos: HM-Decomp anota $80 en vez de $84 en
  Event_AddToByteClamped, Event_MapScrolling; Event_ChangeItemOnHand empieza
  en $84:B4DC (dice B4DE); Event_StoreValue ($84:A90F),
  Event_MakeSlotPassable ($84:BA51) y Event_UseTileProperties ($84:BB31) no tenían
  dirección. ResetFlagD / ResetFlagDD no están en la tabla (código
  muerto); Event_ReturnToolsToShed ($84:BB65) tampoco y no tiene cuerpo compilado.
- La prueba al azar de los comandos con dirección evita la pila y la
  página directa ($7E:0000-1FFF) y el final de un banco.
- Faltan 34 comandos: los de texto (StartTextBox), pantalla (fades,
  paleta), sonido, la vaca (Event_CowFrame, 1.567 instrucciones),
  Event_PutDownCarried, Event_HorseFrame, y los que usan
  SetSlotAnimation.

## El chip de sonido (hecho el 21-oct-2026)

- El comprobador graba en orden lo que el original lee y escribe en los
  puertos $2140-$217F y se lo reproduce a la reescritura; cualquier
  diferencia (puerto, valor u orden) es un MISMATCH. Ver GUIDE.md 3.4.
- src/audio.c: SoundChipBusy, 7, 8, 15, 19, 16, 2. En vivo: 248 efectos de
  sonido del texto de una partida nueva, todos iguales.
- Con eso: ToolUsedWateringCan y ToolUsedSprinkler (src/toolused.c) y
  EditTileOnMap / EditFarmTile (src/mapedit.c).

## Desplazar el mapa (hecho el 22-oct-2026)

- `src/scroll.c`: las 4 rutinas de la cámara (abajo, arriba, derecha,
  izquierda) y las 4 que copian la fila o columna nueva de la WRAM a dos
  búferes y programan dos DMA a la VRAM.
- prep_scroll limita $16 < $7000, $1C < $400, $12 < $E0 y los tramos
  $7E-$84 pares < $40: con valores más grandes una lectura de 16 bits cae
  en $7E:FFFF y la recompilación toma el segundo byte de $7E:0000 (el SNES
  de $7F:0000). Anotado como diferencia 2 en la guía.
- Fuzz 3 semillas × 2000 y en vivo (newgame.txt, ~1.200 llamadas): 0
  diferencias. Sabotajes detectados (el de `<` por `<=` en el tope de
  velocidad es equivalente: no cambia nada).

## Los colores del día (hecho el 22-oct-2026)

- `src/palette.c`: las 14 rutinas de paletas ($80:8FC7-$80:9501 y el
  comando de evento $84:9356).
- `CustomiseSpritePalette` está en $80:93A4 (HM-Decomp dice 93A3, que es el
  RTL anterior): entrada en MANUAL (import_decomp_names.py) y en LOCAL
  (progress.py).
- Dos preparaciones: prep_palette (mapas con paletas válidas en la tabla,
  para las que cargan de la tabla) y prep_palette_any (cualquier mapa).
- Fuzz 3 semillas × 2000 y en vivo (newgame + nights, unas 13.000
  llamadas): 0 diferencias. 15 sabotajes detectados.

## Choques (hecho el 22-oct-2026)

- `src/collision.c`: CollideMap (el mapa, dos esquinas), CollideTileCorner (una esquina),
  CollideEventObjects (objetos de evento), CollidePlayer (el jugador). Tablas de saltos leídas
  de la ROM (HM-Decomp las desensambla como código). Etiquetas indentadas:
  entradas en MANUAL y LOCAL.
- prep_collision: posiciones lejos del borde (con una esquina negativa el
  original lee bus abierto: $B1).
- Fuzz 3 × 2000 y en vivo (~2.900 llamadas): 0 diferencias; sabotajes
  detectados.

## Los botones al caminar (hecho el 22-oct-2026)

- `src/playerinput.c`: PlayerMovementInputs es una sola rutina con muchas
  salidas (HM-Decomp la parte en 15 etiquetas unidas con JMP). LOCAL de
  $84:C6B7 hasta TextBoxAutoClose. progress.py: una línea ya separada por
  split_called (ReadEventPad) se resta de esa rutina, no del bloque (si no,
  se contaba dos veces).
- HM_INTERP: no tiene cuerpo compilado propio (está dentro de
  InputTypeSelector); en vivo se probará cuando se reescriba
  InputTypeSelector (falta NameMenuInputs y MenuInputs).
- prep_player_input: $DA siempre 0-3 (CollideMap/CollideEventObjects saltan por una tabla de
  4), jugador lejos del borde (bus abierto), a veces piso parejo con
  propiedad en el byte +2 (se lee con A = 2: bytes +2/+3) y sin objetos.
- Fuzz 4 × 2500: 0 diferencias. 23 sabotajes detectados (el de las
  esquinas $C0-$CF de "dejar algo" solo 1 vez en 6000: camino raro).

## Todos los modos de entrada (hecho el 22-oct-2026)

- InputTypeSelector reescrito (solo tiene cuerpo compilado en la copia
  $00, `_lo`): ahora todo el sistema de botones se prueba en vivo cada
  cuadro (newgame 3.321, actions 10.271, nights 7.474 llamadas: 0
  diferencias).
- ReadEventPad es una rutina de verdad (MenuInputs la llama con JSL):
  registrada aparte; progress.py deja sus líneas fuera del rango LOCAL de
  PlayerMovementInputs.
- La pantalla del nombre: cuadrículas de 71, 84 y 49 casillas; la
  preparación elige a veces casillas con código (cambio de página, listo).
- Regresión completa (248 rutinas, 2 semillas): 0 diferencias.

## HmRegs.p (22-oct-2026)

- HmRegs tiene `p`: todas las banderas de la entrada (el comprobador la
  llena con cpu_mirrors_to_p). Sirve para `PHP` (su byte queda en la pila,
  que se compara). Va al final de la estructura: los inicializadores
  viejos siguen valiendo.

## Lo siguiente

Todo el código del juego está reescrito (100 %, `tools/progress.py`). Lo
que queda es mejorar el texto: poner nombres claros a las rutinas que aún
tienen el de HM-Decomp (`UNK_*`, `SUB_*`, `CODE_*`) y a las variables de
la WRAM, y seguir usando la descompilación para las ideas de la sección 7
de MEMORIA.md (minimapa, objetos y animales nuevos).
```

```

Para cada rutina nueva: escribirla en `src/`, registrarla en
`src/hm_decomp.c` (con su rango de entradas para la prueba al azar),
compilar y comprobar. Ver `DECOMPILATION.md`.
```

```gradle
// The app: the game's C (native/, built by CMake with the NDK) and SDL3, whose
// source folder is given by HM_SDL3_SOURCE_DIR (or -PsdlDir=...): its C is
// built with the game and its Java (SDLActivity...) goes into the app.
// build_android.bat sets all of this up.
plugins {
    id 'com.android.application'
}

def sdlDir = (project.findProperty('sdlDir') ?: System.getenv('HM_SDL3_SOURCE_DIR') ?: '').toString().replace('\\', '/')
if (!sdlDir || !file("${sdlDir}/android-project/app/src/main/java/org/libsdl/app/SDLActivity.java").exists())
    throw new GradleException("SDL3's source folder is needed: set HM_SDL3_SOURCE_DIR (or -PsdlDir=...)")

android {
    namespace = "io.github.rodriloy.harvestmoon"
    compileSdk 35
    ndkVersion = "28.2.13676358"

    defaultConfig {
        applicationId "io.github.rodriloy.harvestmoon"
        minSdk 26
        targetSdk 35
        versionCode 2
        versionName "0.2.0-beta"
        externalNativeBuild {
            cmake {
                arguments "-DANDROID_STL=c++_static", "-DHM_SDL3_SOURCE_DIR=${sdlDir}"
                abiFilters 'arm64-v8a', 'x86_64'   // x86_64: Android emulators on a PC
            }

            java.srcDirs += ["${sdlDir}/android-project/app/src/main/java"]
        }
    }

        }
    }

    signingConfigs {

                storeFile file(project.property('hmKeystore'))
                storePassword project.property('hmPassword')

    }
```

`android/app/src/main/java/io/github/rodriloy/harvestmoon/HarvestMoonActivity.java`:

```java
/*
 * HarvestMoonActivity — the game on Android: SDL's activity (SDL3 and the
 * game, libmain.so: native/), plus a second screen when the device has one
 * (the AYN Thor's lower screen, or any other display): the pause menu,
 * live, drawn by the game (native/second.c) and used by touch.
 *
 * The second screen is a Presentation on the other display. It never takes
 * the keys' focus, so the device's buttons keep playing the game; a key
 * that reaches it anyway is handed back to the game.
 */
package io.github.rodriloy.harvestmoon;

import android.content.Context;
import android.hardware.display.DisplayManager;
import android.os.Bundle;
import android.os.Handler;
import android.os.Looper;
import android.util.Log;
import android.view.Display;

import org.libsdl.app.SDLActivity;

public class HarvestMoonActivity extends SDLActivity {
    private static final String TAG = "HarvestMoon";
    private static volatile HarvestMoonActivity sSelf;
    private static volatile boolean sWanted = true;      /* the option: Controls > Touch > Second screen */

    private DisplayManager mDisplays;
    private SecondScreen mSecond;
    private final DisplayManager.DisplayListener mListener = new DisplayManager.DisplayListener() {
        @Override public void onDisplayAdded(int id) { updateSecond(); }
        @Override public void onDisplayRemoved(int id) { updateSecond(); }
        @Override public void onDisplayChanged(int id) { updateSecond(); }
    };

    @Override
    protected String[] getLibraries() {
        return new String[] { "SDL3", "main" };
    }

    @Override
    protected void onCreate(Bundle savedInstanceState) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState);
        sSelf = this;
        mDisplays = (DisplayManager) getSystemService(Context.DISPLAY_SERVICE);
        if (mDisplays != null) mDisplays.registerDisplayListener(mListener, new Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()));
    }

    @Override
    protected void onResume() {
        super.onResume();
        updateSecond();
    }

    @Override
    protected void onDestroy() {
        if (mDisplays != null) mDisplays.unregisterDisplayListener(mListener);
        closeSecond();
        sSelf = null;
        super.onDestroy();
    }

    /* the display that is not ours: a presentation display first, else any
     * other real one (not a private or virtual one, such as a recording) */
    private Display otherDisplay() {
        if (mDisplays == null) return null;
        Display mine = getWindowManager().getDefaultDisplay();
        int me = mine != null ? mine.getDisplayId() : Display.DEFAULT_DISPLAY;
        for (Display d : mDisplays.getDisplays(DisplayManager.DISPLAY_CATEGORY_PRESENTATION))
            if (d.getDisplayId() != me && d.isValid()) return d;
        for (Display d : mDisplays.getDisplays())
            if (d.getDisplayId() != me && d.isValid() && (d.getFlags() & Display.FLAG_PRIVATE) == 0) return d;
        return null;
    }

    private void updateSecond() {
        if (isFinishing()) return;
        Display other = otherDisplay();
        try {
            nativeSecondAvailable(other != null);      /* the option shows only then */
        } catch (UnsatisfiedLinkError e) {
            /* the game's library is not loaded (yet) */
        }
        Display d = sWanted ? other : null;
        if (mSecond != null && (d == null || mSecond.getDisplay().getDisplayId() != d.getDisplayId())) closeSecond();
        if (d != null && mSecond == null) {
            try {
                SecondScreen s = new SecondScreen(this, d);
                s.show();
                mSecond = s;
            } catch (RuntimeException e) {          /* WindowManager.InvalidDisplayException among them */
                Log.w(TAG, "no second screen on display " + d.getDisplayId(), e);
                mSecond = null;
            }
        }
        try {
            nativeSecondShown(mSecond != null);
        } catch (UnsatisfiedLinkError e) {
            /* the game's library is not loaded (yet) */
        }
    }

    private void closeSecond() {
        if (mSecond == null) return;
        try { mSecond.dismiss(); } catch (RuntimeException e) { /* gone already */ }
        mSecond = null;
    }

    /* ── called by the game (native/second.c), on its own thread ── */
    public static void secondEnable(boolean on) {
        sWanted = on;
        final HarvestMoonActivity a = sSelf;
        if (a != null) a.runOnUiThread(new Runnable() { @Override public void run() { a.updateSecond(); } });
    }

    public static void secondFrame(int[] pixels) {
        HarvestMoonActivity a = sSelf;
        SecondScreen s = a != null ? a.mSecond : null;
        if (s != null) s.frame(pixels);
    }

    /* ── the game's side ── */
    static native void nativeSecondTouch(int action, int x, int y);
    static native void nativeSecondShown(boolean on);
    static native void nativeSecondAvailable(boolean on);
}
```

`android/app/src/main/java/io/github/rodriloy/harvestmoon/SecondScreen.java`:

```java
/*
 * SecondScreen — the pause menu on the other display (HarvestMoonActivity):
 * the game's 256 x 224 picture of it, enlarged with sharp pixels, and the
 * touches on it sent back to the game in the menu's own pixels.
 */
package io.github.rodriloy.harvestmoon;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.app.Presentation;
import android.content.Context;
import android.graphics.Bitmap;
import android.graphics.Canvas;
import android.graphics.Paint;
import android.graphics.Rect;
import android.os.Bundle;
import android.view.Display;
import android.view.KeyEvent;
import android.view.MotionEvent;
import android.view.View;
import android.view.Window;
import android.view.WindowManager;

class SecondScreen extends Presentation {
    private final Activity mOwner;
    private MenuView mView;

    SecondScreen(Activity owner, Display display) {
        super(owner, display);
        mOwner = owner;
    }

    @Override
    protected void onCreate(Bundle savedInstanceState) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState);
        Window w = getWindow();
        if (w != null) {
            /* the keys stay with the game; the screen stays on */
            w.addFlags(WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE
                     | WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON
                     | WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_FULLSCREEN);
        }
        mView = new MenuView(getContext());
        setContentView(mView);
    }

    void frame(int[] pixels) {
        MenuView v = mView;
        if (v != null) v.frame(pixels);
    }

    /* a key or a stick that lands here anyway: the game's */
    @Override
    public boolean dispatchKeyEvent(KeyEvent event) {
        return mOwner.dispatchKeyEvent(event);
    }

    @Override
    public boolean dispatchGenericMotionEvent(MotionEvent event) {
        return mOwner.dispatchGenericMotionEvent(event);
    }

    static class MenuView extends View {
        static final int W = 256, H = 224;
        private final int[] mPixels = new int[W * H];
        private final Bitmap mBitmap = Bitmap.createBitmap(W, H, Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888);
        private final Paint mPaint = new Paint();
        private final Rect mSrc = new Rect(0, 0, W, H);
        private final Rect mDst = new Rect();
        private boolean mHave;

        MenuView(Context c) {
            super(c);
            mPaint.setFilterBitmap(false);           /* sharp pixels, as the game's */
            mPaint.setAntiAlias(false);
            mPaint.setDither(false);
            setKeepScreenOn(true);
        }

        void frame(int[] pixels) {
            synchronized (mPixels) {
                System.arraycopy(pixels, 0, mPixels, 0, W * H);
                mHave = true;
            }
            postInvalidate();
        }

        private void fit() {
            int vw = getWidth(), vh = getHeight();
            float s = Math.min(vw / (float) W, vh / (float) H);
            int dw = Math.round(W * s), dh = Math.round(H * s);
            mDst.set((vw - dw) / 2, (vh - dh) / 2, (vw - dw) / 2 + dw, (vh - dh) / 2 + dh);
        }

        @Override
        protected void onDraw(Canvas canvas) {
            canvas.drawColor(0xFF3A1E0C);            /* the frames' dark wood */
            synchronized (mPixels) {
                if (!mHave) return;
                mBitmap.setPixels(mPixels, 0, W, 0, 0, W, H);
            }
            fit();
            canvas.drawBitmap(mBitmap, mSrc, mDst, mPaint);
        }

        @Override
        public boolean onTouchEvent(MotionEvent e) {
            int a;
            switch (e.getActionMasked()) {
                case MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN: a = 0; break;
                case MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE: a = 1; break;
                case MotionEvent.ACTION_UP:
                case MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL: a = 2; break;
                default: return true;
            }
            fit();
            if (mDst.width() <= 0 || mDst.height() <= 0) return true;
            int x = (int) ((e.getX() - mDst.left) * W / mDst.width());
            int y = (int) ((e.getY() - mDst.top) * H / mDst.height());
            try {
                HarvestMoonActivity.nativeSecondTouch(a, x, y);
            } catch (UnsatisfiedLinkError err) {
                /* the game is not loaded */
            }
            if (a == 2) performClick();
            return true;
        }

        @Override
        public boolean performClick() {
            return super.performClick();
        }
    }
}
```

`android/build_android.ps1`:

```ps1
# build_android.ps1 - builds the Android version (an APK) on this PC.
#
# Opened by build_android.bat (double-click). The first time it downloads,
# into build\tools: a Java JDK (Microsoft's, about 190 MB), Android's
# command-line tools, and through them the Android SDK pieces the build needs
# (platform 35, build-tools, the NDK, CMake: about 2 GB), SDL3's source and
# Gradle. Android's license is shown first: read it and answer y. Then it
# builds HarvestMoon.apk in the project folder (the first time 10-20
# minutes) and, if an Android device is connected over USB with debugging
# on, offers to install it.
#
# Everything it writes stays in build\ (and Gradle's cache in your user
# folder, .gradle). Its messages also go to build\android.log.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'      # Invoke-WebRequest is very slow with the bar
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12

$root  = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$tools = Join-Path $root 'build\tools'
$old = Join-Path $root 'build\herramientas'   # the folder's name before 0.2 / su nombre antes de la 0.2
if ((Test-Path $old) -and -not (Test-Path $tools)) { Move-Item $old $tools
  # the native build's cache points at the old folder: built again
  foreach ($d in 'android\app\.cxx', 'android\app\build') { $p = Join-Path $root $d; if (Test-Path $p) { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $p } }
}
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $tools | Out-Null
$log = Join-Path $root 'build\android.log'
Start-Transcript -Path $log -Force | Out-Null

function Say($en, $es) { Write-Host ''; Write-Host "== $en / $es" }

function Get-File($url, $out, $what) {
  Write-Host "Downloading / Descargando $what..."
  Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile "$out.part" -UseBasicParsing
  Move-Item -Force "$out.part" $out
}

function Test-Hash($file, $algo, $expected, $what) {
  $got = (Get-FileHash $file -Algorithm $algo).Hash
  if ($got -ne $expected.Trim().ToUpper()) {
    Remove-Item $file
    throw "The download of $what is not the expected file / La descarga de $what no coincide con la esperada."
  }
}

function Expand-Here($zip, $dest) {
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $dest | Out-Null
  tar -xf $zip -C $dest
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Could not unpack / No se pudo descomprimir $zip" }
}

try {
  $arm = ($env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE -eq 'ARM64') -or ($env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432 -eq 'ARM64')

  # 1. Java (Microsoft Build of OpenJDK 17)
  Say 'Java' 'Java'
  $jdkVer = '17.0.21.0.2'
  $jdkArch = if ($arm) { 'aarch64' } else { 'x64' }
  $jdkName = "microsoft-jdk-$jdkVer-windows-$jdkArch"
  $jdkDir = Join-Path $tools $jdkName
  $javaHome = Get-ChildItem $jdkDir -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { Test-Path "$($_.FullName)\bin\java.exe" } | Select-Object -First 1
  if (-not $javaHome) {
    $zip = Join-Path $tools "$jdkName.zip"
    $url = "https://aka.ms/download-jdk/$jdkName.zip"
    Get-File $url $zip 'Java (190 MB)'
    $sum = (Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "$url.sha256sum.txt" -UseBasicParsing).Content
    if ($sum -is [byte[]]) { $sum = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($sum) }
    Test-Hash $zip 'SHA256' (($sum -split '\s+')[0]) 'Java'
    Expand-Here $zip $jdkDir
    Remove-Item $zip
    $javaHome = Get-ChildItem $jdkDir -Directory | Where-Object { Test-Path "$($_.FullName)\bin\java.exe" } | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $javaHome) { throw 'Java is not where it should be / Java no quedo donde debia.' }
  }
  $env:JAVA_HOME = $javaHome.FullName
  $env:Path = "$env:JAVA_HOME\bin;$env:Path"

  # 2. Android's command-line tools (the latest, from Google's own index)
  Say 'Android SDK' 'SDK de Android'
  $sdk = Join-Path $tools 'android-sdk'
  $sdkm = Join-Path $sdk 'cmdline-tools\latest\bin\sdkmanager.bat'
  if (-not (Test-Path $sdkm)) {
    $base = 'https://dl.google.com/android/repository/'
    $raw = (Invoke-WebRequest -Uri ($base + 'repository2-3.xml') -UseBasicParsing).Content
    if ($raw -is [byte[]]) { $raw = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString($raw) }
    [xml]$repo = $raw
    $pkg = $repo.SelectNodes("//*[local-name()='remotePackage']") | Where-Object { $_.GetAttribute('path') -eq 'cmdline-tools;latest' } | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $pkg) { throw "Android's tools are not in Google's index / Las herramientas de Android no estan en el indice de Google." }
    $arc = $pkg.SelectNodes(".//*[local-name()='archive']") | Where-Object {
      $h = $_.SelectSingleNode("*[local-name()='host-os']"); $h -and $h.InnerText -eq 'windows' } | Select-Object -First 1
    $done = $arc.SelectSingleNode("*[local-name()='complete']")
    $file = $done.SelectSingleNode("*[local-name()='url']").InnerText
    $check = $done.SelectSingleNode("*[local-name()='checksum']")
    $zip = Join-Path $tools $file
    Get-File ($base + $file) $zip "Android's tools (150 MB)"
    $algo = if ($check.GetAttribute('type') -match '256') { 'SHA256' } else { 'SHA1' }
    Test-Hash $zip $algo $check.InnerText "Android's tools"
    $tmp = Join-Path $tools 'cmdline-tmp'
    if (Test-Path $tmp) { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $tmp }
    Expand-Here $zip $tmp
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Join-Path $sdk 'cmdline-tools') | Out-Null
    Move-Item (Join-Path $tmp 'cmdline-tools') (Join-Path $sdk 'cmdline-tools\latest')
    Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $tmp
    Remove-Item $zip
  }
  if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $sdk 'licenses\android-sdk-license'))) {
    Say "Android's license: read it and answer y" 'La licencia de Android: leela y contesta y'
    & $sdkm "--sdk_root=$sdk" --licenses
  }
  $ndk = '28.2.13676358'
  if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $sdk "ndk\$ndk\source.properties")) -or -not (Test-Path (Join-Path $sdk 'platforms\android-35')) -or
      -not (Test-Path (Join-Path $sdk 'cmake\3.22.1')) -or -not (Test-Path (Join-Path $sdk 'build-tools\35.0.0'))) {
    Say 'Android SDK pieces (about 2 GB, the first time)' 'Piezas del SDK de Android (unos 2 GB, la primera vez)'
    & $sdkm "--sdk_root=$sdk" 'platform-tools' 'platforms;android-35' 'build-tools;35.0.0' "ndk;$ndk" 'cmake;3.22.1'
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'The Android SDK could not be installed / No se pudo instalar el SDK de Android.' }
  }
  $env:ANDROID_HOME = $sdk
  $env:ANDROID_SDK_ROOT = $sdk

  # 3. SDL3's source (its C is built with the game; its Java goes into the app)
  Say 'SDL3' 'SDL3'
  $sdlName = 'SDL3-3.4.10'
  $sdlDir = Join-Path $root 'build\sdl'
  if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $sdlDir "$sdlName\android-project\app\src\main\java\org\libsdl\app\SDLActivity.java"))) {
    $tgz = Join-Path $tools "$sdlName.tar.gz"
    Get-File "https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/download/release-3.4.10/$sdlName.tar.gz" $tgz 'SDL3 (15 MB)'
    Test-Hash $tgz 'SHA256' '12b34280415ec8418c864408b93d008a20a6530687ee613d60bfbd20411f2785' 'SDL3'
    Expand-Here $tgz $sdlDir
    Remove-Item $tgz
  }
  $env:HM_SDL3_SOURCE_DIR = Join-Path $sdlDir $sdlName

  # 4. Gradle
  Say 'Gradle' 'Gradle'
  $gName = 'gradle-8.12'
  $gradle = Join-Path $tools "$gName\bin\gradle.bat"
  if (-not (Test-Path $gradle)) {
    $zip = Join-Path $tools "$gName-bin.zip"
    $url = "https://services.gradle.org/distributions/$gName-bin.zip"
    Get-File $url $zip 'Gradle (130 MB)'
    $sum = (Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "$url.sha256" -UseBasicParsing).Content
    if ($sum -is [byte[]]) { $sum = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($sum) }
    Test-Hash $zip 'SHA256' (($sum -split '\s+')[0]) 'Gradle'
    Expand-Here $zip $tools
    Remove-Item $zip
  }

  # 5. A key of your own to sign the app (made once; keep it: an update
  #    installs over the old app only when signed with the same key)
  $ks = Join-Path $tools 'harvestmoon.jks'
  if (-not (Test-Path $ks)) {
    & "$env:JAVA_HOME\bin\keytool.exe" -genkeypair -keystore $ks -alias harvestmoon -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 `
      -storepass harvestmoon -keypass harvestmoon -dname 'CN=Harvest Moon native build' | Out-Null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'The signing key could not be made / No se pudo crear la llave para firmar.' }
  }

  # 6. The app
  Say 'Building the app (the first time 10-20 minutes)' 'Compilando la app (la primera vez 10-20 minutos)'
  & $gradle -p (Join-Path $root 'android') --no-daemon assembleRelease "-PhmKeystore=$ks" '-PhmPassword=harvestmoon'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'The build failed, see the messages above / La compilacion fallo, mira los mensajes de arriba.' }
  $apk = Join-Path $root 'android\app\build\outputs\apk\release\app-release.apk'
  if (-not (Test-Path $apk)) { throw 'No APK came out / No salio el APK.' }
  Copy-Item -Force $apk (Join-Path $root 'HarvestMoon.apk')
  Say 'Done: HarvestMoon.apk is in the project folder' 'Listo: HarvestMoon.apk esta en la carpeta del proyecto'
  Write-Host 'Copy it to the phone or the AYN Thor and open it to install it (allow installing from that app when asked).'
  Write-Host 'Copialo al telefono o a la AYN Thor y abrelo para instalarlo (permite instalar desde esa app si lo pide).'

  # 7. A device connected over USB (with USB debugging on): install it now?
  $adb = Join-Path $sdk 'platform-tools\adb.exe'
  if (Test-Path $adb) {
    $devs = & $adb devices | Select-String "`tdevice$"
    if ($devs) {
      $a = Read-Host 'An Android device is connected. Install it there now? / Hay un Android conectado. Instalarla ahi ahora? (y/n)'
      if ($a -match '^[yYsS]') { & $adb install -r (Join-Path $root 'HarvestMoon.apk') }
    }
  }
} catch {
  Write-Host ''
  Write-Host "ERROR: $_"
  Write-Host "The messages are also in / Los mensajes tambien estan en: $log"
} finally {
  Stop-Transcript | Out-Null
}
```

`build_mac.command`:

```command
#!/bin/bash
# build_mac.command - builds the native Harvest Moon on this Mac.
#
# Double-click it in Finder (the first time macOS may say it is from an
# unidentified developer: right-click it > Open > Open). Or, in Terminal:
#     bash build_mac.command
#
# Needs Apple's command line tools (the C compiler); if they are missing it
# asks macOS to install them. The first time it downloads CMake (50 MB,
# checked by its SHA-256, into build/tools) unless you have one, and
# SDL3's source (window, sound, controls). Then it builds the game, a few
# minutes the first time, and leaves HarvestMoonNative and
# "Harvest Moon.command" (double-click to play) in this folder.
# Works on Apple Silicon (M1 and later) and Intel Macs, macOS 11 or newer.

cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
ROOT="$(pwd)"

finish() {
  echo
  read -r -p "Press Enter to close / Enter para cerrar... " _
  exit "$1"
}
fail() {
  echo
  echo "ERROR: $1"
  finish 1
}

# 1. the C compiler (Apple's command line tools)
if ! xcode-select -p >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! /usr/bin/xcrun --find clang >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Apple's command line tools are needed (the C compiler)."
  echo "Hacen falta las herramientas de linea de comandos de Apple (el compilador)."
  xcode-select --install >/dev/null 2>&1
  echo
  echo "A window to install them should open: accept it, wait until it ends,"
  echo "then open this file again."
  echo "Deberia abrirse una ventana para instalarlas: acepta, espera a que"
  echo "termine y vuelve a abrir este archivo."
  finish 1
fi

# 2. CMake: the one installed (Homebrew...), or a copy of its own
CMAKE="$(command -v cmake 2>/dev/null)"
if [ -z "$CMAKE" ]; then
  TOOLS="$ROOT/build/tools"
  [ -d "$ROOT/build/herramientas" ] && [ ! -d "$TOOLS" ] && mv "$ROOT/build/herramientas" "$TOOLS"   # its name before 0.2
  NAME="cmake-3.31.10-macos-universal"
  SHA="be9f3faeeaf7921cc2d77cea711dd5e6f72c63af2810cacd9205b3ce8d1593c9"
  CMAKE="$TOOLS/$NAME/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake"
  if [ ! -x "$CMAKE" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$TOOLS" || fail "cannot create $TOOLS"
    echo "Downloading / Descargando CMake (50 MB)..."
    curl -fL --progress-bar -o "$TOOLS/$NAME.tar.gz.part" \
      "https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v3.31.10/$NAME.tar.gz" \
      || fail "the download of CMake failed / la descarga de CMake fallo"
    GOT="$(shasum -a 256 "$TOOLS/$NAME.tar.gz.part" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    if [ "$GOT" != "$SHA" ]; then
      rm -f "$TOOLS/$NAME.tar.gz.part"
      fail "the download of CMake is not the expected file / la descarga de CMake no coincide"
    fi
    tar -xzf "$TOOLS/$NAME.tar.gz.part" -C "$TOOLS" || fail "could not unpack CMake / no se pudo descomprimir CMake"
    rm -f "$TOOLS/$NAME.tar.gz.part"
  fi
fi

# 3. the console's chips (picture and sound): native/chips, or copied from
#    the recompilation project next to this one
CHIPS="$ROOT/native/chips"
if [ ! -f "$CHIPS/snes/ppu.c" ]; then
  RECOMP="$HM_RECOMP"
  if [ -z "$RECOMP" ]; then
    for c in "$ROOT/../HarvestMoonSNESRecomp" "$ROOT/../HarvestMoonRecomp"; do
      if [ -f "$c/snesrecomp/runner/src/snes/ppu.c" ]; then RECOMP="$c"; break; fi
    done
  fi
  [ -n "$RECOMP" ] || fail "native/chips is missing / falta la carpeta native/chips"
  R="$RECOMP/snesrecomp/runner/src"
  mkdir -p "$CHIPS/snes"
  for f in ppu ppu_legacy ws_shadow dma sdd1 apu spc dsp dsp_shadow audio_shadow color_lut; do
    cp "$R/snes/$f.c" "$CHIPS/snes/" || fail "cannot copy $f.c"
  done
  cp "$R"/snes/*.h "$CHIPS/snes/"
  for f in audio_trace.c audio_trace.h types.h debug_server.h; do cp "$R/$f" "$CHIPS/"; done
  cp "$RECOMP/src/hm_ram.h" "$CHIPS/"
fi

# 4. the game
echo "Building / Compilando (a few minutes the first time / unos minutos la primera vez)..."
"$CMAKE" -S native -B build/native-mac -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0 \
  || fail "the build could not be set up / no se pudo preparar la compilacion"
"$CMAKE" --build build/native-mac --parallel "$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu 2>/dev/null || echo 4)" \
  || fail "the build failed, see the messages above / la compilacion fallo, mira los mensajes de arriba"
cp build/native-mac/HarvestMoonNative "$ROOT/HarvestMoonNative" || fail "cannot copy HarvestMoonNative"

# 5. a double-click to play
cat > "$ROOT/Harvest Moon.command" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Double-click to play / Doble clic para jugar.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" && exec ./HarvestMoonNative "$@"
EOF
chmod +x "$ROOT/Harvest Moon.command" "$ROOT/HarvestMoonNative"

echo
echo "Done / Listo: double-click \"Harvest Moon.command\" to play / doble clic para jugar."
finish 0

```
