```c
const int g_hm_decomp_count = (int)(sizeof g_hm_decomp_fns / sizeof g_hm_decomp_fns[0]);

int g_hm_decomp_check;

typedef struct Snapshot {
  CpuState cpu;
  uint8_t ram[0x20000];
  uint8_t dma[0x80];       /* $4300-$437F before the call */
  uint8_t *sram;           /* the battery RAM before the call (or NULL) */
  int apu_from;            /* where its sound-port traffic starts in s_apu_log */
  HmIoState *io;           /* HM_IO: the chips before the call (hm_io.c) */
} Snapshot;
static void snapshot_free(Snapshot *s) { hm_io_free(s->io); free(s->sram); free(s); }

typedef struct Stats { unsigned calls, ok, bad, skipped; } Stats;
static Stats *s_stats;

static const HmDecompFn *find(const char *name, int *index)
{
  for (int i = 0; i < g_hm_decomp_count; i++)
    if (!strcmp(g_hm_decomp_fns[i].name, name)) { *index = i; return &g_hm_decomp_fns[i]; }
  return NULL;
}

static void report(void)
{
  if (!s_stats) return;
  fprintf(stderr, "[decomp-check] summary:\n");
  for (int i = 0; i < g_hm_decomp_count; i++)
    fprintf(stderr, "[decomp-check]   %-24s calls=%u ok=%u MISMATCH=%u skipped=%u\n",
            g_hm_decomp_fns[i].name, s_stats[i].calls, s_stats[i].ok, s_stats[i].bad,
            s_stats[i].skipped);
}

__attribute__((constructor)) static void hm_decomp_init(void)
{
  const char *e = getenv("HM_DECOMP_CHECK");
  g_hm_decomp_check = e && *e && *e != '0';
  if (g_hm_decomp_check) {
    s_stats = calloc((size_t)g_hm_decomp_count, sizeof *s_stats);
    atexit(report);
    fprintf(stderr, "[decomp-check] checking %d decompiled routines\n", g_hm_decomp_count);
  }
  RtlAddApuPortObserver(apu_wrote);
  RtlAddApuPortReadObserver(apu_read);
  /* The interpreter gives up on a routine after 2 million steps; the sound
   * uploads run by it (LoadDefaultInstruments) take far more while the chip answers.
   * While fuzzing, allow them (a constructor runs before anything is
   * interpreted, and an explicit setting wins). */
  const char *fz = getenv("HM_DECOMP_FUZZ");
  if (fz && *fz) setenv("SNESRECOMP_INTERP_STEP_CAP", "400000000", 0);
}

/* While fuzzing, only the routine being fuzzed is compared: the calls it
 * makes have their own fuzz entries, and checking thousands of nested calls
 * (each one copies 128 KB) is too slow for the 4096-tile farm loops. */
static int s_fuzzing, s_check_depth;

/* HM_DECOMP_SKIP_WHY=1: say why a call was skipped (debugging). */
static void skip_why(const char *name, const char *why)
{
  static int on = -1;
  if (on < 0) on = getenv("HM_DECOMP_SKIP_WHY") != NULL;
  if (on) fprintf(stderr, "[decomp-check] skipped %s: %s\n", name, why);
}

void *hm_decomp_check_begin(const CpuState *cpu, const char *name)
{
  if (s_fuzzing && s_check_depth > 0) return NULL;
  int index = 0;
  const HmDecompFn *f = find(name, &index);
  s_check_depth++;
  Snapshot *s = malloc(sizeof *s);
  if (!s) { s_check_depth--; return NULL; }
  if (s_check_depth == 1) { s_apu_n = 0; s_apu_overflow = 0; }
  s_apu_recording = 1;
  s->apu_from = s_apu_n;
  s->cpu = *cpu;
  memcpy(s->ram, cpu->ram, sizeof s->ram);
  dma_regs_save(s->dma);
  s->sram = NULL;
  if (g_sram && g_sram_size > 0 && (s->sram = malloc((size_t)g_sram_size)) != NULL)
    memcpy(s->sram, g_sram, (size_t)g_sram_size);
  s->io = (f && (f->out_mask & HM_IO)) ? hm_io_save() : NULL;
  return s;
}

void hm_decomp_check_end(const char *name, void *snapshot, const CpuState *cpu, int completed)
{
  Snapshot *s = snapshot;
  int index = 0;
  if (!s) return;                       /* nested call not checked (fuzzing) */
  s_check_depth--;
  if (s_check_depth == 0) s_apu_recording = 0;
  HmApuReplay apu = { s_apu_log + s->apu_from, s_apu_n - s->apu_from, 0, 0, "" };
  const HmDecompFn *f = find(name, &index);
  if (!f) { snapshot_free(s); return; }
  Stats *st = &s_stats[index];
  st->calls++;
  /* A routine interrupted mid-way (the frame deadline yielded), handed to
   * the interpreter (its caller runs there: the compiled body returns at
   * once and the interpreter runs it, e.g. the sprite routines of bank $85)
   * or run in decimal mode is not comparable here; the rewrites assume
   * binary mode. The fuzzer still checks them. */
  if (!completed || s->cpu._flag_D) { skip_why(name, completed ? "decimal mode" : "interrupted"); st->skipped++; snapshot_free(s); return; }

  HmRegs in = { s->cpu.A, s->cpu.X, s->cpu.Y, s->cpu._flag_C, s->cpu._flag_N, s->cpu.DB, s->cpu.D,
                s->cpu.S, s->cpu.PB };
  { CpuState flags = s->cpu; cpu_mirrors_to_p(&flags); in.p = flags.P; }
  HmRegs out = in;
  uint8_t dma_after[0x80];
  dma_regs_save(dma_after);
  if (s_apu_overflow) { skip_why(name, "sound-port log full"); st->skipped++; snapshot_free(s); return; }
  /* HM_IO: the rewrite runs on the real machine (WRAM and chips) put back
   * as they were before the call; afterwards what it left is taken (WRAM to
   * s->ram, the DMA registers to s->dma, the chips to `io_rw`) and the
   * original's result is put back. */
  int io = (f->out_mask & HM_IO) != 0;
  HmIoState *io_rom = NULL, *io_rw = NULL;
  uint8_t *ram_rom = NULL;
  uint64_t clock = g_cpu.master_cycles;
  if (io) {
    if (!s->io || !(io_rom = hm_io_save()) || !(ram_rom = malloc(sizeof s->ram))) {
      hm_io_free(io_rom); skip_why(name, "chip state not available"); st->skipped++; snapshot_free(s); return;
    }
    memcpy(ram_rom, cpu->ram, sizeof s->ram);
    memcpy(cpu->ram, s->ram, sizeof s->ram);
    hm_io_load(s->io);
  }
  g_hm_dma_regs = io ? NULL : s->dma;
  g_hm_io_live = io;
  g_hm_sram = s->sram;
  g_hm_sram_size = (uint32_t)g_sram_size;
  g_hm_apu = &apu;
  if (!setjmp(s_apu_abort)) f->fn(io ? cpu->ram : s->ram, &out);
  g_hm_apu = NULL;
  g_hm_sram = NULL;
  g_hm_dma_regs = NULL;
  g_hm_io_live = 0;
  if (io) {
    io_rw = hm_io_save();
    dma_regs_save(s->dma);
    memcpy(s->ram, cpu->ram, sizeof s->ram);
    memcpy(cpu->ram, ram_rom, sizeof s->ram);
    hm_io_load(io_rom);
    g_cpu.master_cycles = clock;
    free(ram_rom);
  }
  if (!apu.bad && apu.pos != apu.n)
    snprintf(apu.why, sizeof apu.why, "APU: rewrite did %d port accesses, rom %d", apu.pos, apu.n), apu.bad = 1;

  int bad = 0;
  char why[256] = "";
  if (apu.bad) { bad = 1; snprintf(why, sizeof why, "%s", apu.why); }
  if (!bad && io && io_rw && hm_io_diff(io_rw, io_rom, why, sizeof why)) bad = 1;
  hm_io_free(io_rw);
  hm_io_free(io_rom);
  if (!bad && (f->out_mask & HM_OUT_A) && out.a != cpu->A) { bad = 1; snprintf(why, sizeof why, "A %04X != rom %04X", out.a, cpu->A); }
  if (!bad && (f->out_mask & HM_OUT_X) && out.x != cpu->X) { bad = 1; snprintf(why, sizeof why, "X %04X != rom %04X", out.x, cpu->X); }
  if (!bad && (f->out_mask & HM_OUT_Y) && out.y != cpu->Y) { bad = 1; snprintf(why, sizeof why, "Y %04X != rom %04X", out.y, cpu->Y); }
  if (!bad && (f->out_mask & HM_OUT_C) && out.c != cpu->_flag_C) { bad = 1; snprintf(why, sizeof why, "C %u != rom %u", out.c, cpu->_flag_C); }
  if (!bad) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 0x80; i++) {
      int reg = i & 0xF;                 /* $43xC-$43xE don't exist (read 0) */
      if ((reg <= 0xB || reg == 0xF) && s->dma[i] != dma_after[i]) {
        bad = 1;
        snprintf(why, sizeof why, "DMA $43%02X = %02X, rom wrote %02X", i, s->dma[i], dma_after[i]);
        break;
      }
    }
  }
  if (!bad && s->sram) {
    for (int i = 0; i < g_sram_size; i++)
      if (s->sram[i] != g_sram[i]) {
        bad = 1;
        snprintf(why, sizeof why, "SRAM %04X = %02X, rom wrote %02X", i, s->sram[i], g_sram[i]);
        break;
      }
  }
  /* HM_LOOSE: the stack below the final stack pointer is not compared */
  size_t junk_lo = 1, junk_hi = 0;
  if (f->out_mask & HM_LOOSE) {
    junk_hi = cpu->S & 0x1FFF;
    junk_lo = junk_hi >= 0x7FF ? junk_hi - 0x7FF : 0;
  }
  if (!bad) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof s->ram; i++)
      if (s->ram[i] != cpu->ram[i] && !(i >= junk_lo && i <= junk_hi)) {
        bad = 1;
        snprintf(why, sizeof why, "WRAM %05zX = %02X, rom wrote %02X", i, s->ram[i], cpu->ram[i]);
        break;
      }
  }
  if (bad) {
    st->bad++;
    if (st->bad <= 5) {
      fprintf(stderr, "[decomp-check] MISMATCH %s: %s (in A=%04X X=%04X Y=%04X C=%u DB=%02X)\n",
              name, why, in.a, in.x, in.y, in.c, in.db);
      /* HM_DECOMP_DIFF_ALL=1: list every differing byte (rewrite / rom). */
      static int all = -1;
      if (all < 0) { const char *e = getenv("HM_DECOMP_DIFF_ALL"); all = e && *e && *e != '0'; }
      for (size_t i = 0, n = 0; all && i < sizeof s->ram && n < 24; i++)
        if (s->ram[i] != cpu->ram[i] && !(i >= junk_lo && i <= junk_hi)) {
          fprintf(stderr, "[decomp-check]     %05zX: %02X / rom %02X\n", i, s->ram[i], cpu->ram[i]);
          n++;
        }
    }
  } else {
    st->ok++;
  }
  snapshot_free(s);
}

/* ── Fuzzing (HM_DECOMP_FUZZ=<frame>:<iterations>) ─────────────────── */
static uint32_t s_rng = 0x12345678u, s_seed;
static uint32_t rnd(void) { s_rng ^= s_rng << 13; s_rng ^= s_rng >> 17; s_rng ^= s_rng << 5; return s_rng; }
static uint16_t rnd_in(uint16_t lo, uint16_t hi)
{
  /* Mostly uniform in range, sometimes the edges, which is where bugs hide. */
  uint32_t k = rnd() % 8;
  if (k == 0) return lo;
  if (k == 1) return hi;
  return (uint16_t)(lo + rnd() % ((uint32_t)hi - lo + 1));
}

/* HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_ONLY=a,b,c names it */
static int named_in_only(const char *name)
{
  const char *only_name = getenv("HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_ONLY");
  if (!only_name || !*only_name) return 0;
  size_t len = strlen(name);
  for (const char *s = only_name; (s = strstr(s, name)) != NULL; s += len)
    if ((s == only_name || s[-1] == ',') && (s[len] == '\0' || s[len] == ',')) return 1;
  return 0;
}

static void fuzz_at(unsigned frame)
{
  static int at = -2, iters;
  if (at == -2) {
    const char *e = getenv("HM_DECOMP_FUZZ");
    at = -1;
    if (e && *e) { at = atoi(e); const char *c = strchr(e, ':'); iters = c ? atoi(c + 1) : 1000; }
    /* HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_SEED=<n>: other random inputs (a frame only fits a few
     * thousand calls per routine, so run several seeds for more). */
    const char *seed = getenv("HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_SEED");
    if (seed && *seed) s_rng ^= (uint32_t)strtoul(seed, NULL, 0) * 0x9E3779B9u;
    if (!s_rng) s_rng = 1;
    s_seed = s_rng;
  }
  /* One routine per frame, starting at frame `at`: the frame watchdog
   * (5 s of real time per frame) then applies to each routine on its own. */
  /* The routines that talk to the sound chip get a window of their own
   * (HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_APU=<frame>, by default 900 frames earlier): in some
   * moments of the game the chip is busy for a long time (loading music)
   * and never says "ready" (in the demo, around frames 1210 and 1650). */
  static int apu_at = -2;
  if (apu_at == -2) {
    const char *e = getenv("HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_APU");
    apu_at = e && *e ? atoi(e) : (at >= 900 ? at - 900 : at + g_hm_decomp_count);
  }
  if (at < 0) return;
  int only = -1;
  if ((int)frame >= at && (int)frame < at + g_hm_decomp_count &&
      !(g_hm_decomp_fns[(int)frame - at].out_mask & HM_APU))
    only = (int)frame - at;
  /* HM_LIVE (the upload to the chip's boot ROM): frame 1, before the
   * game's own upload is done; only when named (below). */
  for (int i = 0; i < g_hm_decomp_count && only < 0; i++)
    if ((g_hm_decomp_fns[i].out_mask & HM_LIVE) && frame == 1 && named_in_only(g_hm_decomp_fns[i].name)) only = i;
  for (int i = 0, k = 0; i < g_hm_decomp_count && only < 0; i++)
    if ((g_hm_decomp_fns[i].out_mask & HM_APU) && !(g_hm_decomp_fns[i].out_mask & HM_LIVE)) {
      if ((int)frame == apu_at + k) only = i;
      k++;
    }
  if (only < 0) return;

  static CpuState saved_cpu;
  static uint8_t saved_ram[0x20000], saved_dma[0x80];
  saved_cpu = g_cpu;
  memcpy(saved_ram, g_cpu.ram, sizeof saved_ram);
  static uint8_t *saved_sram;                    /* the saved games: put back too */
  if (g_sram && g_sram_size > 0 && !saved_sram) saved_sram = malloc((size_t)g_sram_size);
  if (saved_sram) memcpy(saved_sram, g_sram, (size_t)g_sram_size);
  dma_regs_save(saved_dma);
  HmIoState *saved_io = hm_io_save();           /* the chips (HM_IO routines change them) */
  HmBeam *saved_beam = hm_beam_save();
  uint16_t saved_pad[2] = { RtlGetPadState(0), RtlGetPadState(1) };  /* prep_joypad */
  int prev = g_hm_decomp_check;
  if (!s_stats) { s_stats = calloc((size_t)g_hm_decomp_count, sizeof *s_stats); atexit(report); }
  g_hm_decomp_check = 1;
  s_fuzzing = 1;
  /* Long interpreted routines (CowFeedingAndStatus) would otherwise pause at
   * the frame's deadline half-way, as they do in the game, and not be
   * comparable. The frame driver sets the deadline again every frame. */
  interp_bridge_set_master_deadline(0);
  {
    const char *w = getenv("HM_DECOMP_WATCH");
    if (w && *w) {
      s_watch = strtol(w, NULL, 16);
      g_interp_bridge_pc_hook = watch_step;
      if (getenv("HM_DECOMP_WATCH_BOUNCE")) g_interp_bridge_bounce_hook = watch_bounce;
    }
  }
  interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x808654, nmi_at_wait);   /* WaitForNMI */
  interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x80866C, nmi_at_wait);   /* WaitForNMIATimes */
  interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x808085, nmi_at_wait);   /* GameLoop */
  interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x82E961, nmi_at_wait);   /* NamesScreen */
  interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x82D80F, nmi_at_wait);   /* the intro's loops */
  interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x82D941, nmi_at_wait);
  interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x82E0ED, nmi_at_wait);
  interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x82E339, nmi_at_wait);
  interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x82D34D, nmi_at_wait);   /* the demos */
  interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x82D6CF, nmi_at_wait);
  {                                                           /* HM_TOLOOP */
    static const uint32_t *lists[8] = { STOPS_GAME, STOPS_FRAME, STOPS_NAMES, STOPS_DEMO1, STOPS_DEMO2, STOPS_INTRO,
                                        STOPS_RESET, STOPS_SELF };
    static const int sizes[8] = { 1, 2, 8, 2, 2, 9, 1, 1 };
    interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(0x808428, reset_entry);
    for (int l = 0; l < 8; l++)
      for (int k = 0; k < sizes[l]; k++) interp_bridge_add_pre_opcode_hook(lists[l][k], stop_at_loop);
  }
  if (only == 0)
    fprintf(stderr, "[decomp-fuzz] frames %u-%u: %d calls per routine\n", frame,
            frame + g_hm_decomp_count - 1, iters);
  for (int i = only; i == only; i++) {
    const HmDecompFn *f = &g_hm_decomp_fns[i];
    int n_calls = (f->fuzz_max && f->fuzz_max < iters) ? f->fuzz_max : iters;
    /* Each routine gets its own stream of random inputs (from the seed and
     * its place in the list), so a call can be replayed on its own with
     * HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_ONLY / HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_CALL. */
    s_rng = s_seed ^ (0x9E3779B9u * (uint32_t)(i + 1));
    if (!s_rng) s_rng = 1;
    /* HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_ONLY=<name>: fuzz just that routine (debugging). */
    const char *only_name = getenv("HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_ONLY");
    if (only_name && *only_name) {                /* a name, or several: a,b,c */
      size_t len = strlen(f->name);
      const char *s = only_name;
      int found = 0;
      while (!found && (s = strstr(s, f->name)) != NULL) {
        found = (s == only_name || s[-1] == ',') && (s[len] == '\0' || s[len] == ',');
        s += len;
      }
      if (!found) n_calls = 0;
      else if (f->out_mask & HM_LIVE) n_calls = 1;   /* named: one call */
    } else if (f->out_mask & HM_LIVE) n_calls = 0;
    /* HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_CALL=<n>: run only call n of it (same inputs as in the
     * full run), e.g. to trace it. */
    const char *one_call = getenv("HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_CALL");
    int pick = one_call && *one_call ? atoi(one_call) : -1;
    /* A routine that talks to the sound chip changes the chip too, and the
     * chip only runs up to the CPU's time. Before each call, wait (outside
     * the check) until the chip says "ready" (port 3 = 1), as the game
     * would before sending anything; if it does not (busy loading music),
     * the call is skipped. */
    int apu = (f->out_mask & HM_APU) != 0;
    uint64_t apu_clock = saved_cpu.master_cycles;
    /* The sound routines: with the chip going on from call to call while
     * the WRAM that keeps count is put back every time, what each call
     * sends piles up in the chip (instruments in its memory, a song
     * changing) until the sound program stops answering or stays busy.
     * So for them the whole machine is saved once and put back before
     * every call (and after the last), the chip included: every call
     * starts from the same moment. */
    static uint8_t *machine;
    size_t machine_size = 0;
    if (apu && !(f->out_mask & HM_LIVE)) {
      if (!machine) machine = malloc(4u << 20);
      if (machine) machine_size = RtlSaveSnapshotToMemory(machine, 4u << 20);
    }
    volatile int hangs = 0;
    for (int n = 0; n < n_calls; n++) {
      if (machine_size) {
        RtlLoadSnapshotFromMemory(machine, machine_size);
        apu_clock = saved_cpu.master_cycles;
      }
      /* Between frames nothing is being checked: a check left open by a
       * call that never came back (a sound routine waiting for the chip
       * when the frame was cut) would make every later call look nested,
       * and unchecked. */
      s_check_depth = 0;
      s_apu_recording = 0;
      g_cpu = saved_cpu;
      memcpy(g_cpu.ram, saved_ram, sizeof saved_ram);
      if (saved_sram) memcpy(g_sram, saved_sram, (size_t)g_sram_size);
      dma_regs_restore(saved_dma);
      if (f->out_mask & HM_IO) { hm_io_load(saved_io); hm_beam_load(saved_beam); }
      /* Every call starts with a fresh frame budget: long routines (the
       * 4096-tile farm loop) would otherwise hit the frame deadline, yield
       * half-way and not be comparable. The machine is restored after. */
      g_cpu.master_cycles = apu ? apu_clock : (f->out_mask & HM_IO) ? saved_cpu.master_cycles : 0;
      if (apu && !(f->out_mask & HM_LIVE)) {
        int ready = 0;
        for (long k = 0; k < 200000 && !ready; k++) {
          g_cpu.master_cycles += 64;
          ready = ReadReg(0x2143) == 1;
        }
        apu_clock = g_cpu.master_cycles;
        if (!ready) { skip_why(f->name, "sound chip not ready"); s_stats[i].skipped++; continue; }
      }
      for (int v = 0; v < HM_FUZZ_MAX_VARS && f->vars[v].size; v++) {
        uint16_t x = rnd_in(f->vars[v].lo, f->vars[v].hi);
        g_cpu.ram[f->vars[v].addr] = (uint8_t)x;
        if (f->vars[v].size == 2) g_cpu.ram[f->vars[v].addr + 1] = (uint8_t)(x >> 8);
      }
      uint16_t a = rnd_in(f->a_lo, f->a_hi);
      g_cpu.A = f->entry_m ? (uint16_t)((rnd() & 0xFF00) | (a & 0xFF)) : a;
      g_cpu.X = (uint16_t)rnd(); g_cpu.Y = (uint16_t)rnd();
      if (f->prep) {
        HmRegs pr = { g_cpu.A, g_cpu.X, g_cpu.Y };
        f->prep(g_cpu.ram, &pr, rnd);
        g_cpu.A = pr.a; g_cpu.X = pr.x; g_cpu.Y = pr.y;
      }
      g_cpu.emulation = 0;
      g_cpu.D = 0;
      g_cpu._flag_D = 0;
      g_cpu._flag_C = rnd() & 1;
      g_cpu._flag_N = rnd() & 1;
      cpu_mirrors_to_p(&g_cpu);
      /* I set (IRQs masked): the interpreter otherwise hands control back to
       * the scheduler half-way through a long routine when an IRQ is pending,
       * as the real CPU would to run the handler. No rewritten routine
       * touches I. */
      g_cpu.P = (uint8_t)((g_cpu.P & ~0x30) | 0x04 | (f->entry_m ? 0x20 : 0) | (f->entry_x ? 0x10 : 0));
      cpu_p_to_mirrors(&g_cpu);
      if (f->entry_x) { g_cpu.X &= 0xFF; g_cpu.Y &= 0xFF; }
      /* JSL enters the routine's bank; a JSR runs in its caller's bank,
       * which is the routine's own bank too */
      g_cpu.PB = (uint8_t)(f->pc24 >> 16);
      uint8_t frame_size = 3;
      if (f->out_mask & HM_RTI) {
        /* an interrupt in the middle of the game's code: its bank, an
         * address and the flags; the handler starts with I set, decimal
         * clear and PB = 0 */
        cpu_push_interrupt_frame_at(&g_cpu, 0x808654);
        g_cpu.P = (uint8_t)((g_cpu.P | 0x04) & ~0x08);
        cpu_p_to_mirrors(&g_cpu);
        g_cpu.PB = 0x00;
        frame_size = 4;
      } else if (f->out_mask & HM_JSR) {
        cpu_push_jsr_return_frame(&g_cpu);
        frame_size = 2;
      } else {
        cpu_push_jsl_return_frame(&g_cpu);
      }
      if (pick >= 0 && n != pick) continue;
      /* HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_DUMP=<file>: with HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_CALL, save that call's
       * WRAM (128 KB) and registers before it runs (debugging). */
      const char *dump = getenv("HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_DUMP");
      if (dump && *dump && pick == n) {
        FILE *fd = fopen(dump, "wb");
        if (fd) {
          fwrite(g_cpu.ram, 1, 0x20000, fd);
          uint16_t regs[4] = { g_cpu.A, g_cpu.X, g_cpu.Y, g_cpu.DB };
          fwrite(regs, sizeof regs, 1, fd);
          fclose(fd);
        }
      }
      unsigned bad_before = s_stats[i].bad;
      /* the frame watchdog (5 s of real time per frame): the waiting
       * routines run many frames' worth of work in the interpreter, so each
       * call gets its own budget (the frame's guest code is over here: the
       * fuzzer runs after it, from the frame tick) */
      if ((f->out_mask & HM_WAIT) && g_recomp_stack_top == 0) WatchdogFrameStart();
      /* A sound routine can wait for ever for a chip that stays busy (with
       * the music playing it never gets free): the watchdog then cuts the
       * call, which counts as skipped, and the machine is put back. */
      jmp_buf keep;
      int guard = machine_size && g_recomp_stack_top == 0;
      if (guard) {
        memcpy(keep, g_watchdog_jmp, sizeof keep);
        WatchdogFrameStart();
        if (setjmp(g_watchdog_jmp)) {
          memcpy(g_watchdog_jmp, keep, sizeof keep);
          WatchdogFrameStart();
          g_hm_io_live = 0; g_hm_apu = NULL; g_hm_dma_regs = NULL; g_hm_sram = NULL;
          s_check_depth = 0; s_apu_recording = 0;
          if (s_nmi_sim) keep_waits_interpreted(0, NULL);
          s_nmi_sim = 0;
          set_stops(NULL);
          g_hm_wait_sim = 0;
          if (getenv("HM_DECOMP_HANG_TRACE")) interp_bridge_dump_recent_steps(24, stderr);
          skip_why(f->name, "hung: the chip never answered");
          s_stats[i].calls++; s_stats[i].skipped++;
          if (++hangs == 3) break;                   /* it stays busy: give up */
          continue;
        }
      }
      s_nmi_sim = (f->out_mask & HM_WAIT) != 0;
      keep_waits_interpreted(s_nmi_sim, f);
      set_stops(f);
      g_hm_wait_sim = s_nmi_sim;
      if (f->out_mask & (HM_INTERP | HM_WAIT | HM_RTI)) {
        /* No wrapper around it (or, waiting for the NMI, never a complete
         * call in the compiled code): check this call here. */
        void *snap = hm_decomp_check_begin(&g_cpu, f->name);
        /* No compiled body: run the original in the recompiler's
         * interpreter, as the game itself does. */
        uint16_t s_in = g_cpu.S;
        RecompReturn rr = (f->out_mask & HM_RTI)
          ? (interp_bridge_run_interrupt(&g_cpu, f->pc24 & 0x7FFFFF) ? RECOMP_RETURN_NORMAL : RECOMP_RETURN_SKIP_1)
          : interp_tier_dispatch(&g_cpu, f->pc24);
        /* The interpreter gives up on very long runs and still answers
         * NORMAL: only a run that returned (its frame popped) is complete. */
        hm_decomp_check_end(f->name, snap, &g_cpu,
                            rr == RECOMP_RETURN_NORMAL && g_cpu.S == (uint16_t)(s_in + frame_size));
      } else {
        cpu_dispatch_pc_paired(&g_cpu, f->pc24, frame_size);
      }
      if (s_nmi_sim) keep_waits_interpreted(0, NULL);
      s_nmi_sim = 0;
      set_stops(NULL);
      g_hm_wait_sim = 0;
      if (guard) memcpy(g_watchdog_jmp, keep, sizeof keep);
      if (s_stats[i].bad != bad_before && s_stats[i].bad <= 5)
        fprintf(stderr, "[decomp-fuzz]   (that was %s call %d)\n", f->name, n);
      if (apu) apu_clock = g_cpu.master_cycles;
    }
    if (machine_size) {
      RtlLoadSnapshotFromMemory(machine, machine_size);
      apu_clock = saved_cpu.master_cycles;
    }
    if (apu) saved_cpu.master_cycles = apu_clock;       /* time only goes forward */
  }
  g_cpu = saved_cpu;
  memcpy(g_cpu.ram, saved_ram, sizeof saved_ram);
  if (saved_sram) memcpy(g_sram, saved_sram, (size_t)g_sram_size);
  dma_regs_restore(saved_dma);
  hm_io_load(saved_io);
  hm_io_free(saved_io);
  hm_beam_load(saved_beam);
  free(saved_beam);
  RtlSetPadState(0, saved_pad[0]);
  RtlSetPadState(1, saved_pad[1]);
  g_hm_decomp_check = prev;
  s_fuzzing = 0;
  if (only == g_hm_decomp_count - 1)
    fprintf(stderr, "[decomp-fuzz] done; machine restored\n");
}

/* Hooked in through the mod runtime, so the game project needs no code for
 * the decompilation: frame callbacks are cleared whenever mods (re)activate,
 * and reset callbacks run right before, so re-register there. */
static void on_frame(void)
{
  static unsigned frame;
  fuzz_at(++frame);
}
static void on_reset(void) { snes_mod_register_frame_callback(on_frame); }

SNES_MOD_CONSTRUCTOR(register_hm_decomp)
{
  snes_mod_register_reset_callback(on_reset);
}

```

`src/hm_decomp.h`:

```h
/*
 * hm_decomp.h — the hand-written decompilation of Harvest Moon.
 *
 * The recompiler already turns every routine into C, but that C is a literal
 * translation of 65816 instructions. The decompilation rewrites routines as
 * C a person can read, named after what they do, using the names in
 * hm_ram.h (from the recompilation project). Each routine lives in
 * src/<system>.c.
 *
 * How we know a rewrite is right (differential checking): every decompiled
 * routine has a generated wrapper (tools/decomp_overrides.py) around the
 * recompiled original. Run the game with HM_DECOMP_CHECK=1 and, on every
 * call, the wrapper snapshots RAM and registers, lets the original run, then
 * runs the rewrite on the snapshot and compares the results byte for byte.
 * Any difference is logged with the inputs. Without HM_DECOMP_CHECK the
 * original runs alone, so the game is unchanged.
 */
#pragma once

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* The CPU state a routine sees and returns. Rewrites read the inputs they
 * use and write the outputs they produce; `out_mask` says which outputs the
 * checker compares. */
typedef struct HmRegs {
  uint16_t a, x, y;
  uint8_t c;          /* carry flag */
  uint8_t n;          /* negative flag (some routines branch on the caller's) */
  uint8_t db;         /* data bank */
  uint16_t d;         /* direct page */
  uint16_t s;         /* stack pointer (bank $00) */
  uint8_t pb;         /* program bank: $80-$87, or $00-$07 when the game runs
                       * the same code from the slow mirror */
  uint8_t p;          /* all the flags at the entry (for PHP: its byte goes on
                       * the stack); c and n above are the live ones */
} HmRegs;

/* The stack lives in WRAM, so what a routine pushes stays there after it
 * returns, and the checker compares it too. PHA/PHY/JSL write downwards. */
static inline void hm_push8(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t v)
{
  ram[r->s & 0x1FFF] = v;
  r->s = (uint16_t)(r->s - 1);
}
static inline uint8_t hm_pull8(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  r->s = (uint16_t)(r->s + 1);
  return ram[r->s & 0x1FFF];
}
/* JSL to a routine in `bank`: pushes the current bank (PB) and the address
 * of the JSL's own last byte, then runs in the new bank. RTL pops the 3
 * bytes and goes back to the caller's bank. */
static inline void hm_jsl(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t return_pc, uint8_t bank)
{
  hm_push8(ram, r, r->pb);
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)(return_pc >> 8));
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)return_pc);
  r->pb = bank;
}
static inline void hm_rtl(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  hm_pull8(ram, r);
  hm_pull8(ram, r);
  r->pb = hm_pull8(ram, r);
}

/* Direct-page variables ($00-$FF relative to D, in bank $00 = low WRAM). */
static inline uint8_t *hm_dp(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, unsigned off)
{
  return &ram[(uint16_t)(r->d + off) & 0x1FFF];
}
static inline void hm_dp_w16(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, unsigned off, uint16_t v)
{
  *hm_dp(ram, r, off) = (uint8_t)v;
  *hm_dp(ram, r, off + 1) = (uint8_t)(v >> 8);
}
static inline uint16_t hm_dp_r16(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, unsigned off)
{
  return (uint16_t)(*hm_dp(ram, r, off) | *hm_dp(ram, r, off + 1) << 8);
}

/* ── The whole address space, for long pointers ([$72],Y and friends) ──────
 * The ROM never changes, so rewrites may read it directly: g_rom is the
 * cartridge image the runtime loaded (LoROM: bank & $3F selects a 32 KB
 * chunk, addresses $8000-$FFFF). WRAM is `ram`: banks $7E/$7F, and the
 * first 8 KB mirrored in banks $00-$3F / $80-$BF. Hardware registers are
 * not modelled (reads give 0, writes are dropped), except the DMA
 * registers $4300-$437F (g_hm_dma_regs below), the sound chip's ports
 * $2140-$217F (g_hm_apu below) and the cartridge's battery RAM, where the
 * game is saved (g_hm_sram below). */
extern const uint8_t *g_rom;

/* The DMA registers $4300-$437F, while the checker runs a rewrite: a copy
 * of them taken before the call (the checker compares it with the real
 * ones afterwards). NULL otherwise. */
extern uint8_t *g_hm_dma_regs;

/* The battery RAM (SRAM, the saved games): banks $70-$7D / $F0-$FD,
 * addresses $0000-$7FFF (LoROM), mirrored every g_hm_sram_size bytes.
 * While the checker runs a rewrite: a copy taken before the call, compared
 * with the real one afterwards. NULL otherwise. */
extern uint8_t *g_hm_sram;
extern uint32_t g_hm_sram_size;

/* The sound chip's ports $2140-$217F. Their answers come from another
 * processor and cannot be computed, so the checker records every port
 * read and write the original makes, in order; while the rewrite runs on
 * the snapshot, each read it makes gets the value the original read at
 * that point, and each write must be the one the original made. Any
 * difference in the order, the port or the value is a mismatch. NULL when
 * no rewrite is being checked. */
typedef struct HmApuEvent { uint16_t reg; uint8_t val, write; } HmApuEvent;
typedef struct HmApuReplay {
  const HmApuEvent *ev;
  int n, pos, bad;
  char why[96];
} HmApuReplay;
extern HmApuReplay *g_hm_apu;
uint8_t hm_apu_read(uint16_t reg);
/* The console's own registers that a rewrite reads: $4212 (the beam and the
 * automatic pad reading) and $4214-$421F (the results of the multiplier and
 * divider, the pads). Asked to the emulator; reading them changes nothing in
 * WRAM ($4212 only moves the emulated beam a little). */
uint8_t hm_io_read(uint16_t reg);
static inline int hm_is_io_reg(uint32_t addr)
{
  uint16_t a = (uint16_t)addr;
  return ((addr >> 16) & 0x7F) < 0x40 && (a == 0x4212 || (a >= 0x4214 && a < 0x4220));
}
void hm_apu_write(uint16_t reg, uint8_t v);
static inline int hm_is_apu_port(uint32_t addr)
{
  uint16_t a = (uint16_t)addr;
  return ((addr >> 16) & 0x7F) < 0x40 && a >= 0x2140 && a < 0x2180;
}

static inline uint8_t *hm_bus_ram(uint8_t *ram, uint32_t addr)
{
  uint8_t bank = (uint8_t)(addr >> 16);
  uint16_t a = (uint16_t)addr;
  if (bank == 0x7E) return &ram[a];
  if (bank == 0x7F) return &ram[0x10000 + a];
  if ((bank & 0x7F) < 0x40 && a < 0x2000) return &ram[a];
  if ((bank & 0x7F) < 0x40 && a >= 0x4300 && a < 0x4380 && g_hm_dma_regs)
    return &g_hm_dma_regs[a - 0x4300];
  if ((bank & 0x7F) >= 0x70 && (bank & 0x7F) < 0x7E && a < 0x8000 && g_hm_sram)
    return &g_hm_sram[(((uint32_t)(bank & 0xF) << 15) | a) & (g_hm_sram_size - 1)];
  return NULL;
}
/* HM_IO routines: while the checker runs the rewrite on the real machine
 * (hm_io.c), the chips' registers are really read and written. */
extern int g_hm_io_live;
uint8_t hm_io_read_live(uint16_t reg);
void hm_io_write_live(uint16_t reg, uint8_t v);
static inline int hm_is_chip_reg(uint32_t addr)
{
  uint16_t a = (uint16_t)addr;
  return ((addr >> 16) & 0x7F) < 0x40 &&
         ((a >= 0x2100 && a < 0x2140) || (a >= 0x2180 && a < 0x2184) || (a >= 0x4200 && a < 0x4380));
}
static inline uint8_t hm_bus_rd8(uint8_t *ram, uint32_t addr)
{
  uint8_t *p = hm_bus_ram(ram, addr);
  if (p) return *p;
  uint8_t bank = (uint8_t)(addr >> 16);
  uint16_t a = (uint16_t)addr;
  if (a >= 0x8000 && (bank & 0x7F) < 0x7E)
    return g_rom[(uint32_t)(bank & 0x3F) << 15 | (a & 0x7FFF)];
  if (hm_is_apu_port(addr)) return hm_apu_read(a);
  if (g_hm_io_live && hm_is_chip_reg(addr)) return hm_io_read_live(a);
  if (hm_is_io_reg(addr)) return hm_io_read(a);
  return 0;
}
static inline uint16_t hm_bus_rd16(uint8_t *ram, uint32_t addr)
{
  return (uint16_t)(hm_bus_rd8(ram, addr) | hm_bus_rd8(ram, (addr + 1) & 0xFFFFFF) << 8);
}
static inline void hm_bus_wr8(uint8_t *ram, uint32_t addr, uint8_t v)
{
  uint8_t *p = hm_bus_ram(ram, addr);
  if (p) *p = v;
  else if (hm_is_apu_port(addr)) hm_apu_write((uint16_t)addr, v);
  else if (g_hm_io_live && hm_is_chip_reg(addr)) hm_io_write_live((uint16_t)addr, v);
}
static inline void hm_bus_wr16(uint8_t *ram, uint32_t addr, uint16_t v)
{
  hm_bus_wr8(ram, addr, (uint8_t)v);
  hm_bus_wr8(ram, (addr + 1) & 0xFFFFFF, (uint8_t)(v >> 8));
}
/* A 24-bit pointer stored in the direct page ($72-$74, $CC-$CE...), plus Y:
 * the address `[dp],Y` uses. */
static inline uint32_t hm_dp_long(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, unsigned off, uint16_t y)
{
  uint32_t p = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, off) | (uint32_t)*hm_dp(ram, r, off + 2) << 16;
  return (p + y) & 0xFFFFFF;
}

enum { HM_OUT_A = 1, HM_OUT_X = 2, HM_OUT_Y = 4, HM_OUT_C = 8,
       /* The recompiler has no compiled body for this routine (it runs in
        * its interpreter), so there is no wrapper to check live calls: the
        * fuzzer checks it by calling the original directly. */
       HM_INTERP = 16,
       /* Called with JSR / returns with RTS (2-byte frame), not JSL / RTL. */
       HM_JSR = 32,
       /* Talks to the sound chip: while fuzzing, the CPU clock keeps going
        * from call to call (the chip only runs up to the CPU's time, so a
        * clock set back to 0 would leave it stopped and the routine
        * waiting for its answer forever). */
       HM_APU = 64,
       /* Fuzzed only when named in HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_ONLY, once, without
        * waiting for "ready", at frame 1 (before the game's own upload is
        * done): UploadSoundProgram, which talks to the chip's boot ROM; after the
        * upload the chip runs the game's sound program and never answers
        * that way again. E.g. HM_DECOMP_FUZZ=100000:1
        * HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_ONLY=UploadSoundProgram. */
       HM_LIVE = 128,
       /* Writes the console's chips (PPU, DMA, WRAM port, $42xx): checked
        * by running the rewrite on the real machine from the state before
        * and comparing the chips' state (hm_io.c). */
       HM_IO = 256,
       /* An interrupt handler (RTI): fuzzed with an interrupt's 4-byte frame
        * (bank, address, flags) on the stack. */
       HM_RTI = 512,
       /* Waits for the NMI (WaitForNMI and what calls it). In the game the
        * compiled code yields to the frame scheduler there, so live calls
        * are never complete; the fuzzer runs the original in the
        * interpreter and, when it reaches the wait loop with $00 = 0, makes
        * the NMI happen right there (hm_nmi below does the same in C). */
       HM_WAIT = 1024,
       /* A long routine made of others that waits frames: the flags its
        * waits save (PHP) and the NMI pushes depend on N, Z and V left by
        * the routines before, which the rewrites do not follow, so the
        * stack below the final stack pointer (what is left there, never
        * read again) is not compared. Everything else is. */
       HM_LOOSE = 2048,
       /* Ends by going into the game loop (GameLoop, $80:8083), which never
        * returns: the original is stopped when it gets there (an RTL takes
        * it back as if it returned), and the rewrite returns there. For
        * GameLoop itself the stop is its JMP back ($80:80DB, one frame
        * done) or its JML into the names screen ($80:80E9); for the names
        * screen (NamesScreen) its JML back to the frame's start or to
        * the name's routine; for RESET, which throws the stack away, its
        * JML to the title, where the checker's frame is put back; for the
        * loop of one BRA (UnusedEndlessLoop), its second turn. */
       HM_TOLOOP = 4096 };

/* video.c: the NMI arriving at `pc` (the wait loop) with the flags `p`:
 * pushes bank, address and flags as the CPU does, runs NMI_Interrupt with
 * PB = 0, I set and decimal clear, and returns through its RTI. */
void hm_nmi(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t pc, uint8_t p);
/* game.c: the fifteen JSLs of a game frame (GameLoop's, and the demos'),
 * one every 4 bytes from `at` in the caller's bank */
void hm_game_frame(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t at);

/* ── Running the game on the rewrites alone (native/) ──────────────────────
 * The routines that never return (RESET, the title screen, the demos, the
 * names screen, GameLoop) end where the original jumps on (JML / JMP) to
 * the next one; g_hm_next is that address, so a host can call the next
 * routine itself. It changes nothing the checker compares.
 * g_hm_frame_hook, when set, runs at every NMI before its handler: the end
 * of a frame (draw it, read the pads, run the sound chip). NULL in the
 * checking build. */
extern uint32_t g_hm_next;
extern void (*g_hm_frame_hook)(uint8_t *ram);
/* The native build's improvements (native/mods.c) reach into three places,
 * through these; their values here are the ROM's own, so the checking
 * build (and a native build with the improvements off) is untouched:
 *   g_hm_oam_right / g_hm_oam_left: the screen X a sprite piece must be
 *     under / from to be drawn (PrepareOAMData, $85:853B / $85:8540;
 *     widescreen widens them);
 *   g_hm_no_ending: the house's date check for the ending (Summer 30,
 *     Year 3, $83:DEE7) fails while it is set (the endless game);
 *   g_hm_year_suffix: the diary's year ordinal past the game's three
 *     ("4th", "5th"... $82:F298);
 *   g_hm_crops_passable: the player walks through the crops of the farm
 *     (CollideTileCorner, the map's collision: a crop tile no longer blocks; and
 *     PutItemDown changes the tile A looked at, 7 pixels ahead);
 *   g_hm_single_seed: a seed bag sows one tile at a time, 9 per bag
 *     (the seeds' ToolUsed; g_hm_seeds_used, grass, corn, tomato, potato,
 *     turnip: the seeds gone from each open bag, kept in the saved game's
 *     unused bytes +20 to +25 by SaveGameSlot / LoadGameSlot);
 *   g_hm_bag_take: the crop bag gives back an item (PutItemDown leaves
 *     nothing on the map for it). */
extern uint16_t g_hm_oam_right, g_hm_oam_left;
extern int g_hm_no_ending;
extern int g_hm_crops_passable;
extern int g_hm_single_seed;
/* g_hm_bag_on: the crop bag (native/mods.c) is on: its items (g_hm_bag,
 * item ids, 0 = empty) are kept in the saved game's unused bytes +52 to
 * +5B by SaveGameSlot / LoadGameSlot; g_hm_bag_take: the next PutItemDown
 * (picking up) takes the item out of the bag: nothing is left on the map
 * and no sound (it clears it). */
extern int g_hm_bag_on, g_hm_bag_take;
extern uint8_t g_hm_bag[9];
extern uint8_t g_hm_seeds_used[5];
/* g_hm_wife_on: the wife's help (native/wife.c) is on; g_hm_wife_until:
 * the last day she helps (year x 120 + season x 30 + day; 0 none), kept in
 * the saved game's +5C-+5E by SaveGameSlot / LoadGameSlot */
extern int g_hm_wife_on;
extern uint16_t g_hm_wife_until;
extern uint16_t (*g_hm_year_suffix)(uint16_t x, uint16_t rom_value);
/* the loops' own entries the host needs (not checked on their own) */
void hm_IntroDemoCheck(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r);    /* intro.c: the demo check */
void hm_DemoFrame(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r);     /* demo.c: a frame of each demo */
void hm_DemoPresentationFrame(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r);

/* hm_io.c: the chips' state for HM_IO checks. */
typedef struct HmIoState HmIoState;
int hm_io_available(void);
HmIoState *hm_io_save(void);
void hm_io_load(const HmIoState *s);
void hm_io_free(HmIoState *s);
int hm_io_diff(const HmIoState *rewrite, const HmIoState *rom, char *why, size_t n);
void hm_io_quiet(void);
typedef struct HmBeam HmBeam;
HmBeam *hm_beam_save(void);
void hm_beam_load(const HmBeam *b);

/* Fuzzing: which inputs to randomize when testing a routine on its own
 * (HM_DECOMP_FUZZ). Ranges are inclusive; size 1 or 2 bytes. */
typedef struct HmFuzzVar { uint32_t addr; uint8_t size; uint16_t lo, hi; } HmFuzzVar;
enum { HM_FUZZ_MAX_VARS = 6 };

typedef struct HmDecompFn {
  const char *name;                       /* HM-Decomp label */
  void (*fn)(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r);    /* the rewrite: ram is WRAM (128 KB) */
  unsigned out_mask;                      /* outputs to compare */
  const char *source;                     /* where it is written */
  /* Fuzz spec: entry point, entry widths, A's range and RAM inputs. */
  uint32_t pc24;
  uint8_t entry_m, entry_x;
  uint16_t a_lo, a_hi;
  HmFuzzVar vars[HM_FUZZ_MAX_VARS];
  /* Optional: at most this many fuzz calls (0 = all) for slow routines, and
   * a function that prepares more inputs (e.g. a random farm). */
  uint16_t fuzz_max;
  void (*prep)(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint32_t (*rnd)(void));
} HmDecompFn;

/* Registry, defined in hm_decomp.c. */
extern const HmDecompFn g_hm_decomp_fns[];
extern const int g_hm_decomp_count;

/* Check mode (HM_DECOMP_CHECK=1); read by the generated wrappers. */
extern int g_hm_decomp_check;

struct CpuState;
/* HM_DECOMP_FUZZ=<frame>:<iterations>: at that frame boundary, call every
 * registered routine <iterations> times with random inputs (checking each
 * call), then restore the machine exactly as it was. Driven by a mod-runtime
 * frame callback registered in hm_decomp.c. */
void *hm_decomp_check_begin(const struct CpuState *cpu, const char *name);
void hm_decomp_check_end(const char *name, void *snapshot, const struct CpuState *cpu,
                         int completed);
```

`src/hm_io.c`:

```c
/*
 * hm_io.c — checking the routines that talk to the console's own chips:
 * the picture unit (PPU, $2100-$213F), the DMA unit ($4300-$437F, $420B,
 * $420C), the WRAM port ($2180-$2183) and the CPU's registers ($4200-$421F:
 * NMITIMEN, the timers, the multiplier and divider).
 *
 * The sound chip is checked by replaying what it answered (hm_decomp.c);
 * these chips keep state instead, so a routine flagged HM_IO is checked by
 * comparing that state:
 *   1. before the original runs: hm_io_save() (registers, the VRAM, CGRAM
 *      and OAM pointers and latches, the three memories, the DMA channels,
 *      HDMAEN, the CPU's registers and the RDNMI latch);
 *   2. the original runs as always, changing the real machine;
 *   3. its result is saved, the state before is put back, and the rewrite
 *      runs on the real machine: its writes go to the emulated chips
 *      (hm_io_write_live), so a DMA it starts really copies;
 *   4. what it left is compared with what the original left, and the
 *      original's result is put back for the game to go on.
 * The writes here do not move the emulated beam (WriteReg brings it up to
 * the CPU's clock first): the beam stays where the original left it, so
 * nothing is drawn, no NMI is raised and both runs see the same beam.
 */
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "cpu_state.h"
#include "snes/snes.h"
#include "snes/ppu.h"
#include "snes/dma.h"
#include "hm_decomp.h"

extern Snes *g_snes;
extern Ppu *g_ppu;
extern Dma *g_dma;
extern uint8_t g_snesrecomp_last_hdmaen;

int g_hm_io_live;

typedef struct HmPpuAccess {
  uint16_t vramPointer, vramReadBuffer;
  bool vramIncrementOnHigh;
  uint8_t vramRemapMode, vramIncrement;
  uint8_t cgramPointer, cgramBuffer;
  bool cgramSecondWrite;
  uint8_t oamAdr, oamBuffer;
  bool oamInHigh, oamSecondWrite;
  uint8_t scrollPrev, scrollPrev2, m7prev;
} HmPpuAccess;

typedef struct HmCpuRegs {
  bool nmiEnabled, hIrqEnabled, vIrqEnabled, inIrq, rdnmiPending, autoJoyRead, ppuLatch;
  uint16_t hTimer, vTimer;
  uint8_t multiplyA;
  uint16_t multiplyResult, divideA, divideResult;
  uint32_t ramAdr;
} HmCpuRegs;

struct HmIoState {
  uint8_t regs[PPU_SAVESTATE_REGS_SIZE];          /* inidisp .. cgwsel */
  HmPpuAccess access;
  uint8_t mem[PPU_SAVESTATE_MEM_SIZE];            /* cgram, oam, highOam, vram */
  DmaChannel channel[8];
  uint8_t hdmaen;
  HmCpuRegs cpu;
};

int hm_io_available(void) { return g_snes && g_ppu && g_dma && g_snes->ram == g_cpu.ram; }

HmIoState *hm_io_save(void)
{
  if (!hm_io_available()) return NULL;
  HmIoState *s = calloc(1, sizeof *s);
  if (!s) return NULL;
  memcpy(s->regs, &g_ppu->inidisp, sizeof s->regs);
  memcpy(s->mem, &g_ppu->cgram, sizeof s->mem);
  HmPpuAccess *a = &s->access;
  a->vramPointer = g_ppu->vramPointer;       a->vramReadBuffer = g_ppu->vramReadBuffer;
  a->vramIncrementOnHigh = g_ppu->vramIncrementOnHigh;
  a->vramRemapMode = g_ppu->vramRemapMode;   a->vramIncrement = g_ppu->vramIncrement;
  a->cgramPointer = g_ppu->cgramPointer;     a->cgramBuffer = g_ppu->cgramBuffer;
  a->cgramSecondWrite = g_ppu->cgramSecondWrite;
  a->oamAdr = g_ppu->oamAdr;                 a->oamBuffer = g_ppu->oamBuffer;
  a->oamInHigh = g_ppu->oamInHigh;           a->oamSecondWrite = g_ppu->oamSecondWrite;
  a->scrollPrev = g_ppu->scrollPrev;         a->scrollPrev2 = g_ppu->scrollPrev2;
  a->m7prev = g_ppu->m7prev;
  memcpy(s->channel, g_dma->channel, sizeof s->channel);
  s->hdmaen = g_snesrecomp_last_hdmaen;
  HmCpuRegs *c = &s->cpu;
  c->nmiEnabled = g_snes->nmiEnabled;   c->hIrqEnabled = g_snes->hIrqEnabled;
  c->vIrqEnabled = g_snes->vIrqEnabled; c->inIrq = g_snes->inIrq;
  c->rdnmiPending = g_snes->rdnmiPending;
  c->autoJoyRead = g_snes->autoJoyRead; c->ppuLatch = g_snes->ppuLatch;
  c->hTimer = g_snes->hTimer;           c->vTimer = g_snes->vTimer;
  c->multiplyA = g_snes->multiplyA;     c->multiplyResult = g_snes->multiplyResult;
  c->divideA = g_snes->divideA;         c->divideResult = g_snes->divideResult;
  c->ramAdr = g_snes->ramAdr;
  return s;
}

void hm_io_load(const HmIoState *s)
{
  if (!s || !hm_io_available()) return;
  memcpy(&g_ppu->inidisp, s->regs, sizeof s->regs);
  memcpy(&g_ppu->cgram, s->mem, sizeof s->mem);
  const HmPpuAccess *a = &s->access;
  g_ppu->vramPointer = a->vramPointer;       g_ppu->vramReadBuffer = a->vramReadBuffer;
  g_ppu->vramIncrementOnHigh = a->vramIncrementOnHigh;
  g_ppu->vramRemapMode = a->vramRemapMode;   g_ppu->vramIncrement = a->vramIncrement;
  g_ppu->cgramPointer = a->cgramPointer;     g_ppu->cgramBuffer = a->cgramBuffer;
  g_ppu->cgramSecondWrite = a->cgramSecondWrite;
  g_ppu->oamAdr = a->oamAdr;                 g_ppu->oamBuffer = a->oamBuffer;
  g_ppu->oamInHigh = a->oamInHigh;           g_ppu->oamSecondWrite = a->oamSecondWrite;
  g_ppu->scrollPrev = a->scrollPrev;         g_ppu->scrollPrev2 = a->scrollPrev2;
  g_ppu->m7prev = a->m7prev;
  memcpy(g_dma->channel, s->channel, sizeof s->channel);
  g_snesrecomp_last_hdmaen = s->hdmaen;
  const HmCpuRegs *c = &s->cpu;
  g_snes->nmiEnabled = c->nmiEnabled;   g_snes->hIrqEnabled = c->hIrqEnabled;
  g_snes->vIrqEnabled = c->vIrqEnabled; g_snes->inIrq = c->inIrq;
  g_snes->rdnmiPending = c->rdnmiPending;
  g_snes->autoJoyRead = c->autoJoyRead; g_snes->ppuLatch = c->ppuLatch;
  g_snes->hTimer = c->hTimer;           g_snes->vTimer = c->vTimer;
  g_snes->multiplyA = c->multiplyA;     g_snes->multiplyResult = c->multiplyResult;
  g_snes->divideA = c->divideA;         g_snes->divideResult = c->divideResult;
  g_snes->ramAdr = c->ramAdr;
}

void hm_io_free(HmIoState *s) { free(s); }

/* The first difference, as "what: rewrite value, rom value". 0 = same. */
int hm_io_diff(const HmIoState *rw, const HmIoState *rom, char *why, size_t n)
{
  static const char *const mem_name[] = { "CGRAM", "OAM", "high OAM", "VRAM" };
  static const unsigned mem_at[] = { 0, 0x200, 0x400, 0x420, 0x10420 };
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof rw->regs; i++)
    if (rw->regs[i] != rom->regs[i]) {
      snprintf(why, n, "PPU register byte +%02X = %02X, rom %02X", i, rw->regs[i], rom->regs[i]);
      return 1;
    }
  for (unsigned m = 0; m < 4; m++)
    for (unsigned i = mem_at[m]; i < mem_at[m + 1]; i++)
      if (rw->mem[i] != rom->mem[i]) {
        snprintf(why, n, "%s byte %04X = %02X, rom %02X", mem_name[m], i - mem_at[m], rw->mem[i], rom->mem[i]);
        return 1;
      }
#define FIELD(st, f, what) \
  if ((st)->f != (rom_##st)->f) { \
    snprintf(why, n, "%s %s = %X, rom %X", what, #f, (unsigned)(st)->f, (unsigned)(rom_##st)->f); return 1; }
  const HmPpuAccess *a = &rw->access, *rom_a = &rom->access;
  FIELD(a, vramPointer, "PPU") FIELD(a, vramReadBuffer, "PPU") FIELD(a, vramIncrementOnHigh, "PPU")
  FIELD(a, vramRemapMode, "PPU") FIELD(a, vramIncrement, "PPU") FIELD(a, cgramPointer, "PPU")
  FIELD(a, cgramBuffer, "PPU") FIELD(a, cgramSecondWrite, "PPU") FIELD(a, oamAdr, "PPU")
  FIELD(a, oamBuffer, "PPU") FIELD(a, oamInHigh, "PPU") FIELD(a, oamSecondWrite, "PPU")
  FIELD(a, scrollPrev, "PPU") FIELD(a, scrollPrev2, "PPU") FIELD(a, m7prev, "PPU")
  for (int ch = 0; ch < 8; ch++) {
    const DmaChannel *d = &rw->channel[ch], *rom_d = &rom->channel[ch];
    char what[16];
    snprintf(what, sizeof what, "DMA %d", ch);
    FIELD(d, bAdr, what) FIELD(d, aAdr, what) FIELD(d, aBank, what) FIELD(d, size, what)
    FIELD(d, indBank, what) FIELD(d, tableAdr, what) FIELD(d, repCount, what)
    FIELD(d, unusedByte, what) FIELD(d, dmaActive, what) FIELD(d, hdmaActive, what)
    FIELD(d, mode, what) FIELD(d, fixed, what) FIELD(d, decrement, what) FIELD(d, indirect, what)
    FIELD(d, fromB, what) FIELD(d, unusedBit, what) FIELD(d, doTransfer, what)
    FIELD(d, terminated, what) FIELD(d, offIndex, what)
  }
  if (rw->hdmaen != rom->hdmaen) {
    snprintf(why, n, "HDMAEN = %02X, rom %02X", rw->hdmaen, rom->hdmaen);
    return 1;
  }
  const HmCpuRegs *c = &rw->cpu, *rom_c = &rom->cpu;
  FIELD(c, nmiEnabled, "CPU") FIELD(c, hIrqEnabled, "CPU") FIELD(c, vIrqEnabled, "CPU")
  /* not inIrq / rdnmiPending: the beam sets them, and the original's run
   * moves the beam (WriteReg syncs it, a DMA charges its time) */
  FIELD(c, autoJoyRead, "CPU")
  FIELD(c, ppuLatch, "CPU") FIELD(c, hTimer, "CPU") FIELD(c, vTimer, "CPU") FIELD(c, multiplyA, "CPU")
  FIELD(c, multiplyResult, "CPU") FIELD(c, divideA, "CPU") FIELD(c, divideResult, "CPU")
  FIELD(c, ramAdr, "CPU")
#undef FIELD
  return 0;
}

/* WriteReg's routing, without its clock sync. */
void hm_io_write_live(uint16_t reg, uint8_t v)
{
  if (reg >= 0x2100 && reg < 0x2140) ppu_write(g_ppu, (uint8_t)reg, v);
  else if (reg >= 0x2180 && reg < 0x2184) snes_writeBBus(g_snes, (uint8_t)reg, v);
  else if (reg >= 0x4200 && reg < 0x4220) snes_writeReg(g_snes, reg, v);
  else if (reg >= 0x4300 && reg < 0x4380) dma_write(g_dma, reg, v);
}
uint8_t hm_io_read_live(uint16_t reg)
{
  if (reg >= 0x2100 && reg < 0x2140) return ppu_read(g_ppu, (uint8_t)reg);
  if (reg == 0x2180) return snes_readBBus(g_snes, (uint8_t)reg);
  if (reg >= 0x4200 && reg < 0x4220) return snes_readReg(g_snes, reg);
  if (reg >= 0x4300 && reg < 0x4380) return dma_read(g_dma, reg);
  return 0;
}

/* For the fuzzer: nothing that the beam would do on its own while the
 * original runs (HDMA writing registers on each line, raster IRQs). */
void hm_io_quiet(void)
{
  if (!hm_io_available()) return;
  snes_writeReg(g_snes, 0x420C, 0);
  g_snes->hIrqEnabled = g_snes->vIrqEnabled = false;
  g_snes->inIrq = false;
}

/* For the fuzzer: the beam and its clock anchor, so that every call of an
 * HM_IO routine starts at the same place of the frame (a CPU clock set
 * back behind the anchor makes the next sync jump the beam about). */
struct HmBeam {
  uint8_t tail[sizeof(Snes) - offsetof(Snes, hPos)];
  uint64_t beamMasterLast;
  bool rdnmiPending;
};
HmBeam *hm_beam_save(void)
{
  if (!hm_io_available()) return NULL;
  HmBeam *b = malloc(sizeof *b);
  if (!b) return NULL;
  memcpy(b->tail, &g_snes->hPos, sizeof b->tail);
  b->beamMasterLast = g_snes->beamMasterLast;
  b->rdnmiPending = g_snes->rdnmiPending;
  return b;
}
void hm_beam_load(const HmBeam *b)
{
  if (!b || !hm_io_available()) return;
  memcpy(&g_snes->hPos, b->tail, sizeof b->tail);
  g_snes->beamMasterLast = b->beamMasterLast;
  g_snes->rdnmiPending = b->rdnmiPending;
}
```

`src/hm_regs.h`:

```h
/*
 * hm_regs.h — the console's registers, by their names in the SNES manuals.
 *
 * The routines write them through the bus (hm_bus_wr8(ram, INIDISP, v) ...);
 * the values are the registers' addresses in bank $00 (and its mirrors).
 * Only the registers this code touches are here.
 */
#pragma once

/* ── The picture unit (PPU), $2100-$213F ─────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#define INIDISP      0x2100 /* forced blank (bit 7) and brightness */
#define OBSEL        0x2101 /* sprite sizes and graphics address */
#define OAMADDL      0x2102 /* OAM address (16b) */
#define OAMADDH      0x2103
#define OAMDATA      0x2104 /* OAM data (written twice) */
#define BGMODE       0x2105
#define MOSAIC       0x2106
#define BG1SC        0x2107 /* the backgrounds' tile maps */
#define BG2SC        0x2108
#define BG3SC        0x2109
#define BG4SC        0x210A
#define BG12NBA      0x210B /* the backgrounds' graphics */
#define BG34NBA      0x210C
#define BG1HOFS      0x210D /* BG1 scroll, across (+ 2 per layer) */
#define BG1VOFS      0x210E /* and down */
#define BG2HOFS      0x210F
#define BG2VOFS      0x2110
#define BG3HOFS      0x2111
#define BG3VOFS      0x2112
#define BG4HOFS      0x2113
#define BG4VOFS      0x2114
#define VMAIN        0x2115 /* how the VRAM address moves */
#define VMADDL       0x2116 /* VRAM address (16b) */
#define VMADDH       0x2117
#define VMDATAL      0x2118 /* VRAM data (16b) */
#define VMDATAH      0x2119
#define M7SEL        0x211A /* mode 7 (the matrix and centre written twice) */
#define M7A          0x211B
#define M7B          0x211C
#define M7C          0x211D
#define M7D          0x211E
#define M7X          0x211F
#define M7Y          0x2120
#define CGADD        0x2121 /* CGRAM address */
#define CGDATA       0x2122 /* CGRAM data (written twice) */
#define W12SEL       0x2123 /* the windows */
#define W34SEL       0x2124
#define WOBJSEL      0x2125
#define WH0          0x2126
#define WH1          0x2127
#define WH2          0x2128
#define WH3          0x2129
#define WBGLOG       0x212A
#define WOBJLOG      0x212B
#define TM           0x212C /* main screen layers */
#define TS           0x212D /* sub screen layers */
#define TMW          0x212E
#define TSW          0x212F
#define CGWSEL       0x2130 /* colour math */
#define CGADSUB      0x2131
#define COLDATA      0x2132 /* the fixed colour */
#define SETINI       0x2133
#define MPYL         0x2134 /* read-only from here to $213F */
#define MPYM         0x2135
#define MPYH         0x2136
#define SLHV         0x2137
#define RDOAM        0x2138
#define RDVRAML      0x2139
#define RDVRAMH      0x213A
#define RDCGRAM      0x213B
#define OPHCT        0x213C
#define OPVCT        0x213D
#define STAT77       0x213E
#define STAT78       0x213F

/* ── The sound chip's ports, $2140-$2143 (audio.c) ───────────────────────────────────── */
#define APUIO0       0x2140 /* the sound chip's port 0; ports 1-3 follow */

/* ── The WRAM port, $2180-$2183 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#define WMDATA       0x2180 /* the WRAM port: data */
#define WMADDL       0x2181 /* its address (24b) */
#define WMADDM       0x2182
#define WMADDH       0x2183

/* ── The CPU's registers, $4200-$421F ────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#define NMITIMEN     0x4200 /* NMI, line IRQ and automatic pad reading on / off */
#define WRIO         0x4201 /* the I/O port */
#define WRMPYA       0x4202 /* 8b: the multiplier's first factor */
#define WRMPYB       0x4203 /* 8b: its second factor; writing it starts it */
#define WRDIVL       0x4204 /* 16b: the divider's dividend (WRDIVL/H) */
#define WRDIVH       0x4205
#define WRDIVB       0x4206 /* 8b: the divisor; writing it starts it */
#define HTIMEL       0x4207 /* the IRQ's dot (16b) */
#define HTIMEH       0x4208
#define VTIMEL       0x4209 /* the IRQ's line (16b) */
#define VTIMEH       0x420A
#define MDMAEN       0x420B /* starts the DMA channels (bit = channel) */
#define HDMAEN       0x420C /* the HDMA channels on */
#define MEMSEL       0x420D /* bit 0: FastROM */
#define RDNMI        0x4210 /* read-only from here to $421F */
#define TIMEUP       0x4211 /* the line IRQ's flag (reading it lets the IRQ go) */
#define HVBJOY       0x4212 /* bit 0 = the automatic pad reading is running */
#define RDIO         0x4213
#define RDDIVL       0x4214
#define RDDIVH       0x4215
#define RDMPYL       0x4216
#define RDMPYH       0x4217
#define JOY1L        0x4218 /* 16b: pad 1's buttons */
#define JOY1H        0x4219
#define JOY2L        0x421A /* 16b: pad 2's buttons */
#define JOY2H        0x421B
#define JOY3L        0x421C
#define JOY3H        0x421D
#define JOY4L        0x421E
#define JOY4H        0x421F

/* ── DMA channels: $43n0 + the register, n = the channel (dma.c) ─────────────────────── */
#define DMAP0        0x4300 /* DMA channel 0: mode (+ $10 per channel) */
#define BBAD0        0x4301 /* its destination register ($21xx) */
#define A1T0L        0x4302 /* its source address */
#define A1B0         0x4304 /* its source bank */
#define DAS0L        0x4305 /* its size (16b) */
#define DMAP4        0x4340 /* DMA channel 4: mode */
#define BBAD4        0x4341 /* its destination register ($21xx) */
#define A1T4L        0x4342 /* its source address */
#define A1T4H        0x4343
#define A1B4         0x4344 /* its source bank */
#define DAS4L        0x4345 /* its size (16b) */

/* ── The same registers as a DMA channel's destination (BBADn holds $21xx's low byte) ── */
#define BBAD_OAM     0x04   /* $2104: a copy to OAM */
#define BBAD_VRAM    0x18   /* $2118, the VRAM data register (as in dma.c) */
#define BBAD_CGDATA  0x22   /* $2122: a copy to CGRAM */
```

`src/hm_vars.h`:

```h
/*
 * hm_vars.h — the game's variables that more than one file uses.
 *
 * Each place in RAM that two or more routine files read or write has one
 * name here, so it is called the same everywhere. The names that the
 * recompilation project already gives (the clock, the money, the bags,
 * HM_GAME_STATE ...) are in hm_ram.h and are not repeated. A place only one
 * file uses is named at the top of that file.
 *
 * The values are ram[] offsets, as in hm_ram.h: $7E:xxxx is 0x0xxxx and
 * $7F:xxxx is 0x1xxxx. The routines that read through the data bank or the
 * direct page use them as they are; the bus helpers (hm_bus_rd8 ...) take
 * WRAM_LONG(name), the same place as a 24-bit address.
 *
 * Sizes: 8b one byte, 16b a word, 24b a long pointer or number.
 */
#pragma once

#define WRAM_LONG(a)  (0x7E0000 + (a))   /* a ram[] offset as a bus address */

/* ── Direct page ($00-$FF) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The hm_dp_* helpers take these offsets. Most of the direct page is scratch
 * that each routine uses its own way (those bytes are named in the files);
 * these few keep one meaning everywhere. */
#define HM_TILE_PROPS            0x0D    /* 24b: a long pointer to the map's tile
                                            properties table (the bank in $0F) */
#define HM_TILE_PROPS_BANK       0x0F    /* 8b: its bank */
#define HM_ANIMAL_PTR            0x72    /* 24b $72-$74: an animal's record, as
                                            GetCowPointer / GetChickenPointer leave it */

/* ── Flag words ($7F:1F5A-$7F:1F7B) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The bits known so far, with the file that uses them. $5A-$62 and $74-$76
 * are cleared every day; $64-$72 are the story's and are saved. */
#define HM_FLAGS_5A              0x11F5A /* 16b: bit 0 map $37 seen; 1 a cow is being
                                            bought; $02 a cow comes tomorrow; $04 / $08 a
                                            cow / chicken is sold; $10 the bell calls the
                                            cows; $20 an animal bought today; $40 a tool
                                            was used; $80 the medicine; $0100 the miracle
                                            potion; $0200 the fishing rod; $0400 the
                                            shipping scene runs; $0800 its text; $1000 a
                                            cow was left out; $4000 a text box is open;
                                            $8000 the screen is faded in, a scene can be
                                            skipped */
#define HM_FLAGS_5C              0x11F5C /* 16b: $01 time stopped (and stays so); $02 no
                                            weather layer; $04 the event script is over;
                                            $08 no tile checks; $10 shipping at an
                                            object; $20 no control; $40 shipped; the
                                            horse's requests ($10, $20, $40, $0400,
                                            $0800); the mountain's finds of the day
                                            ($2000-$8000) */
#define HM_FLAGS_5E              0x11F5E /* 16b: bit 0 an item shipped this frame; $02 no
                                            animals, the ending, no map extras; $04 no
                                            breakfast; $40 lets a slot face the player;
                                            $80 / $0100 / $0200 sprite palette $71-$73;
                                            $0800 the long walk to bed; $1000 what it
                                            waits for (a map event); $8000 the music goes
                                            on after 18:00, the ending's slide show */
#define HM_FLAGS_60              0x11F60 /* 16b: bit 0 no feeding (set with
                                            HM_WEATHER_FLAGS bit 4); $02 / $04 block the
                                            player's actions (commands 52 / 53), a child
                                            carried; $08 energy frozen, go to map $3C;
                                            $10 calls the dog; $20 sent home; $40
                                            (without $0100) holds a transition; $80 the
                                            demo is over; $0200 the watch shows text
                                            $046A; $0400 the town's scene; $0800 both
                                            diaries were cleared or failed their check;
                                            $1000 / $2000 a chicken / cow at the
                                            festival; $4000 nothing blocks; $8000 no
                                            tools */
#define HM_FLAGS_62              0x11F62 /* 16b day flags */
#define HM_FLAGS_64              0x11F64 /* 16b story flags: bit 0 / 1 the summer /
                                            winter storm seen; $04 a cow was given the
                                            potion; $08 a calf was born; $10 / $20
                                            today's special days; $40 / $80 the house's
                                            first / second extension */
#define HM_FLAGS_66              0x11F66 /* 16b story flags: bits 0-4 the girl married
                                            (Maria ... Eve, a bit each; palette.c: the
                                            child's stage); $20 -> $40; $80 the house is
                                            being built; $0100 it is done; bits 9-12 the
                                            house painted; $2000 the spring's event seen
                                            today; $4000 / $8000 the festival entries */
#define HM_FLAGS_68              0x11F68 /* 16b story flags: $01 a day went by (the ranch
                                            and the shops are open); $80 a dog; $0100 a
                                            horse; $0800 -> $1000; $8000 the golden
                                            hammer */
#define HM_FLAGS_6A              0x11F6A /* 16b story flags: bits 0-3 the gold tools on
                                            sale; $40 a power berry eaten on map $29; $80
                                            the golden hoe; $0400 -> $0800; visits $1000
                                            / $4000 */
#define HM_FLAGS_6C              0x11F6C /* 16b story flags: visits $01, $04, $10 ($01
                                            also: the exits to map $1C closed); $0080 the
                                            anniversary; $0100 / $0200 the children's
                                            birthdays (they last a day); $1000 the turtle
                                            shell; $4000 a power berry eaten at home */
#define HM_FLAGS_6E              0x11F6E /* 16b story flags: $04 / $08 the second / first
                                            child; $10 no bed; $0200 a fence broke; $2000
                                            an egg is hatching; $4000 the clock; $8000 a
                                            tool back to the shed */
#define HM_FLAGS_70              0x11F70 /* 16b: $02 today's special day
                                            (HM_WEATHER_FLAGS bit 8); $04 the first
                                            spring or summer */
#define HM_FLAGS_72              0x11F72 /* 16b: the last of the story's words */
#define HM_FLAGS_74              0x11F74 /* 16b day flags: bit 5 the festival eggs
                                            vanish, bit 6 one was placed; events seen
                                            (the Starry Night) */
#define HM_FLAGS_76              0x11F76 /* 16b day flags */
#define HM_FLAGS_78              0x11F78 /* 16b: the fence pieces put up, a bit each */
#define HM_FLAGS_7A              0x11F7A /* 16b: the scene flags (SetSceneFlag) */

/* ── Records ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Offsets inside a record (read through a pointer such as HM_ANIMAL_PTR or
 * HM_EVENT_SLOT), so they carry the record's name instead of HM_. */
#define ANIMAL_STATUS            0x00    /* 8b: the first byte of a cow's or a chicken's
                                            record. Cows: bit 0 it exists, 1 newborn, 2
                                            calf, 3 adult, 4 cranky, 5 sick, 6 pregnant,
                                            7 gave birth. Chickens: bit 0 it exists, 1
                                            egg, 2 chick, 3 adult, 4 hungry */
#define COW_DAILY                0x01    /* 8b: a cow's (HM_COW_DATA, 16 bytes each)
                                            flags of the day (bit 7 the potion) */
#define COW_MAP                  0x02    /* 8b: the map it is on */
#define COW_DAYS                 0x03    /* 8b: days as a calf, pregnant, sick or cranky */
#define COW_HAPPINESS            0x04    /* 8b */
#define COW_HITS                 0x05    /* 8b: times hit with a tool (to 10); at 10 it
                                            turns cranky after its meal (animals.c) */
#define COW_X                    0x08    /* 16b: its position */
#define COW_Y                    0x0A    /* 16b */
#define COW_NAME                 0x0C    /* 4 bytes: its name */
#define CHICKEN_MAP              0x01    /* 8b: a chicken's (HM_CHICKEN_DATA, 8 bytes
                                            each) map */
#define CHICKEN_DAYS             0x02    /* 8b: a counter: nights as an egg, as a chick,
                                            hungry */
#define CHICKEN_X                0x04    /* 16b: its position */
#define CHICKEN_Y                0x06    /* 16b */
#define MOBJ_FLAGS               0x00    /* 8b: a map object's (HM_MAP_OBJECTS, 16 bytes
                                            each) flags: bit 0 in use, 1 drawn on the
                                            map, 2 kept off screen */
#define MOBJ_ROUTINE             0x01    /* 8b: its routine (table $81:A58B) */
#define MOBJ_STATE               0x02    /* 8b: its state */
#define MOBJ_ITEM                0x03    /* 8b: the item it is */
#define MOBJ_GOBJ                0x04    /* 16b: its game object */
#define MOBJ_SPRITE              0x06    /* 16b: its sprite */
#define MOBJ_SPRITE_SHOWN        0x08    /* 16b: the sprite shown now */
#define MOBJ_FLIP                0x0A    /* 16b: its flip */
#define MOBJ_X                   0x0C    /* 16b: its position */
#define MOBJ_Y                   0x0E    /* 16b */
#define SLOT_IN_USE              0x00    /* 8b: an event slot's (CC slot, 64 bytes;
                                            events.c) first byte: bit 0 in use, bit 1
                                            passable */
#define SLOT_FLAGS               0x01    /* 8b: bit 0 has a sprite, 1 create the object,
                                            2 the sprite changed, 3 wanders, 4 frozen */
#define SLOT_ANIM_ENTRY          0x02    /* 8b: the entry in its animation table (the way
                                            it faces) */
#define SLOT_STEP_X              0x03    /* 8b signed: its step */
#define SLOT_STEP_Y              0x04    /* 8b signed */
#define SLOT_STEP_DELAY          0x05    /* 8b: frames between steps (StepSlot reloads
                                            SLOT_STEP_TIMER from it) */
#define SLOT_STEP_TIMER          0x06    /* 8b: frames until the next step */
#define SLOT_WALK_STEPS          0x07    /* 8b: steps of a walk */
#define SLOT_STEPS_LEFT          0x08    /* 8b: steps left of this walk */
#define SLOT_RANGE_X             0x09    /* 8b: how far it may wander from home, across */
#define SLOT_RANGE_Y             0x0A    /* 8b: and down */
#define SLOT_WALK_DELAY          0x0B    /* 8b: a walk's frames between steps */
#define SLOT_PRESSED             0x0C    /* 8b: the player pressed A on it / talked to it
                                            (CollideEventObjects) */
#define SLOT_ROLL                0x0D    /* 8b: the last die roll (GetRNG) */
#define SLOT_STATE               0x0E    /* 8b: $E0 being sold, $E1 off the farm, $C2 in
                                            the barn; also the tile type ahead */
#define SLOT_FORCED_DIR          0x0F    /* 8b: the direction the script forces: 1 down,
                                            2 up, 4 right, 8 left */
#define SLOT_FRAMES              0x10    /* 16b: a frame counter (the wait) */
#define SLOT_OBJECT              0x12    /* 16b: its game object */
#define SLOT_ANIMATION           0x14    /* 16b: the object's animation (a byte x 64) */
#define SLOT_SPRITE              0x16    /* 16b: the object's sprite */
#define SLOT_LAST_SPRITE         0x18    /* 16b: the sprite last given to the object */
#define SLOT_X                   0x1A    /* 16b: its position */
#define SLOT_Y                   0x1C    /* 16b */
#define SLOT_HOME_X              0x1E    /* 16b: where its walks start (the middle of its
                                            area) */
#define SLOT_HOME_Y              0x20    /* 16b */
#define SLOT_SCRIPT              0x30    /* 16b: where its script is, */
#define SLOT_SCRIPT_BANK         0x32    /* 8b: and its bank */
#define SLOT_ANIM_TABLE          0x33    /* 16b: its standing animation table, $B3:<word> */
#define SLOT_WALK_TABLE          0x36    /* 16b: its walking animation table */
#define SLOT_NUMBER              0x3F    /* 8b: its own number */
#define COW_SLOT0                0x18    /* the event slot of cow n is $18 + n, */
#define CHICKEN_SLOT0            0x24    /* and chicken n's $24 + n (PlaceAnimalsOnMap,
                                            animals.c) */
#define GOBJ_STATUS              0x00    /* 16b: a game object's (HM_GAME_OBJECTS)
                                            status: GOBJ_IN_USE, or 0 = free */
#define GOBJ_SPRITE              0x02    /* its sprite number */
#define GOBJ_FLIP                0x04    /* its flip: bit 6 across, bit 7 up-down */
#define GOBJ_PARAM               0x06    /* copied from HM_OBJ_PARAM */
#define GOBJ_X                   0x08    /* 16b: its position */
#define GOBJ_Y                   0x0A    /* 16b */
#define GOBJ_FIRST_FRAME         0x0C    /* the sprite's entry: its first frame */
#define GOBJ_NEXT_FRAME          0x0E    /* the frame to show after this one */
#define GOBJ_PIECE_LIST          0x10    /* the address of the frame's piece list */
#define GOBJ_TIMER               0x12    /* 8b: frames left on this frame ($FE free, $FF
                                            for ever) */
#define GOBJ_PIECE_COUNT         0x13    /* 8b: how many pieces */
#define GOBJ_PIECE_SLOTS         0x14    /* 16 bytes: one per piece, its graphics slot
                                            ($FF = queued) */
#define GOBJ_SIZE                0x24    /* the size of a game object's record (36 bytes) */
#define GOBJ_MAX                 0x28    /* how many there are (40) */
#define GOBJ_IN_USE              0x7777  /* GOBJ_STATUS's value for an object in use */

/* ── Tables in the ROM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The bus addresses of ROM tables that several files read (not RAM, so no
 * HM_). The name in HM-Decomp is in brackets. */
#define DMA_CHANNEL_BITS         0x808B3C /* 8 bytes: 1 << the channel */
#define MAPS_GRAPHICS_TABLE      0x80AA7C /* a word per map: its graphics
                                             (Maps_Graphics_Table) */
#define DOOR_TABLE               0x80B6F5 /* the doors: the destination map, the map
                                             animation, when it is shut, where the player
                                             arrives (the DOOR_* fields of
                                             playerstate.c); interact.c reads its opening
                                             hours (Unk_Table13) */
#define SHED_ITEM_TABLE          0x81BE0F /* 8 bytes per item: +6 its byte in
                                             HM_SHED_ITEMS, +7 its bit; also the shed's
                                             list */
#define FEED_BOX_BITS            0x82A571 /* a word per feed box: its bit (1 << n) in
                                             HM_COW_TROUGHS / HM_CHICKEN_TROUGHS
                                             (Cow_Feed_Flags) */
#define PICK_UP_ITEMS            0x82CFB4 /* per tile type x 4 + the season: the item
                                             picked up there (DATA8_82CFB4) */
#define NAME_LETTER_AT           0x82EB4D /* the names screen: the VRAM place of each
                                             letter (DATA16_82EB4D) */
#define CHICKEN_PLACES           0x83CA10 /* 4 bytes per chicken (nest): x, y in the coop
                                             (DATA16_83CA10) */
#define COW_PLACES               0x83CA44 /* 4 bytes per cow: x, y in the barn
                                             (Table_CowsSpawnPos) */

```

`src/interact.c`:

```c
/*
 * interact.c — pressing A in front of something.
 *
 * PressAOnTile ($82:AD0E, JSL, RTL) is called by PlayerKeyA with X = the type
 * of the tile in front (GetTileProperty; 0 when it does not face the
 * player's side). The map's tile property table [$0D] has 4 bytes per type;
 * what pressing A does depends on the type:
 *
 *   $F0-$FF  a door: if byte +1 bit 0, go to place [+0] ($096E; $D2 bit 6
 *            starts the change of map)
 *   $E0-$EF  nothing
 *   $D0-$DF  a sign: show text [+0] (a word)
 *   $C0-$CF  a door with opening hours: [+0] picks a rule of Unk_Table13
 *            ($80:B6F5, 8 bytes each, byte 3 the rule's bits) and [+1] the
 *            text to show when the rule says so (0: never). Rule bits:
 *            $02 from 17:00, $04 before 17:00, $08 Monday-Friday,
 *            $10 Saturday, $20 Sunday, $80 when $0196 bit 4.
 *   below    in autumn and winter tiles $38 $39 $52 $53 $60 $61 $6E $6F
 *            do nothing; if byte +1 bit 7, pick the thing up: item
 *            DATA8_82CFB4[type * 4 + season] in hand ($091D), the tile's
 *            byte +0 in $091F, action 4 (holding it). Otherwise, unless
 *            byte +2 bit 0, look for an event object in front (CollideEventObjects marks
 *            it: that is how the player talks to people and animals).
 */
#include "hm_decomp.h"
#include "hm_ram.h"   /* from the recompilation project */
#include "hm_vars.h"

/* The shared variables (HM_...) are named in hm_vars.h and hm_ram.h. */

/* ROM tables */
#define SONG_INSTRUMENTS    0x80B8CD /* per song, its instrument (- 1) */

/* Direct page */
#define PICK_AT             0x7E     /* 16b: 4 x the tile type (the table offset) */
#define RULE_NUMBER         0x92     /* 8b: the door's opening-hours rule */
#define RULE_TEXT           0x93     /* 8b: the door's text */

static uint32_t db_addr(const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a) { return (uint32_t)r->db << 16 | a; }
static uint16_t dp16(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, unsigned a) { return hm_dp_r16(ram, r, a); }
static void set16(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, unsigned a, uint16_t v) { hm_dp_w16(ram, r, a, v); }
static uint8_t lda8(HmRegs *r, uint8_t v)
{
  r->a = (uint16_t)((r->a & 0xFF00) | v);
  return v;
}
static uint8_t table8(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t y) { return hm_bus_rd8(ram, hm_dp_long(ram, r, HM_TILE_PROPS, y)); }
/* CPX #k: C = X >= k */
static bool below(HmRegs *r, uint16_t k) { r->c = r->x >= k; return !r->c; }

static void show_text(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t text, uint16_t ret)
{
  hm_bus_wr8(ram, db_addr(r, HM_INPUT_STATE), 2);          /* input: a text box */
  hm_bus_wr8(ram, db_addr(r, HM_TEXT_BOX_LINES), 0);
  r->x = text;
  hm_jsl(ram, r, ret, 0x83);
  hm_StartTextBox(ram, r);
  hm_rtl(ram, r);
}

/* the opening-hours rule of a $C0-$CF door: true = show the text */
static bool rule_applies(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t rule)
{
  lda8(r, rule & 0x02);
  if (rule & 0x02) {
    uint8_t h = lda8(r, hm_bus_rd8(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_HOUR)));
    r->c = h >= 0x11;
    if (r->c) return true;
  }
  lda8(r, rule & 0x04);
  if (rule & 0x04) {
    uint8_t h = lda8(r, hm_bus_rd8(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_HOUR)));
    r->c = h >= 0x11;
    if (!r->c) return true;
  }
  lda8(r, rule & 0x08);
  if (rule & 0x08) {
    uint8_t d = lda8(r, hm_bus_rd8(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_WEEKDAY)));
    if (d != 0) {
      r->c = d >= 6;
      if (d != 6) return true;
    }
  }
  lda8(r, rule & 0x10);
  if (rule & 0x10) {
    uint8_t d = lda8(r, hm_bus_rd8(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_WEEKDAY)));
    r->c = d >= 6;
    if (d == 6) return true;
  }
  lda8(r, rule & 0x20);
  if (rule & 0x20) {
    if (lda8(r, hm_bus_rd8(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_WEEKDAY))) == 0) return true;
  }
  lda8(r, rule & 0x80);
  if (!(rule & 0x80)) return false;
  r->a = hm_bus_rd16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS)) & 0x0010;
  return r->a != 0;
}

void hm_PressAOnTile(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint16_t type = r->x;
  uint16_t at = (uint16_t)(type << 2);                     /* TXA; ASL; ASL */

  if (!below(r, 0xF0)) {                                   /* a door */
    r->a = at;
    r->c = (type >> 14) & 1;                               /* ASL's carry */
    r->y = (uint16_t)(at + 1);
    if (!(lda8(r, table8(ram, r, r->y)) & 0x01)) { lda8(r, 0); return; }
    r->y = at;
    hm_bus_wr8(ram, db_addr(r, HM_INTERACTION), lda8(r, table8(ram, r, at)));
    hm_bus_wr8(ram, db_addr(r, HM_INTERACTION_STEP), 0);
    hm_bus_wr8(ram, db_addr(r, HM_INTERACTION_FRAMES), 0);
    set16(ram, r, HM_GAME_STATE, (uint16_t)(dp16(ram, r, HM_GAME_STATE) | 0x0040));
    r->a = 0;
    set16(ram, r, HM_PLAYER_ACTION, 0);
    return;
  }
  if (!below(r, 0xE0)) return;
  if (!below(r, 0xD0)) {                                   /* a sign */
    r->y = at;
    r->c = (type >> 14) & 1;
    uint16_t text = hm_bus_rd16(ram, hm_dp_long(ram, r, HM_TILE_PROPS, at));
    r->a = (uint16_t)((text & 0xFF00) | 0x00);
```
