`src/math.c`:

```c
/*
 * math.c — arithmetic helpers.
 *
 * DivisionUnsigned ($83:8082, JSL, RTL). Divides the 16-bit dividend in $7E
 * by the 16-bit divisor in $80 (direct page). Returns the quotient in A and
 * leaves the remainder in $7E. Always exits with 16-bit A/X/Y, Y = 0, C = 0.
 *
 * Two ways to divide:
 *  - Divisor below 255: the SNES hardware divider ($4204/$4205 dividend,
 *    $4206 divisor, quotient in $4214, remainder in $4216). Only the low
 *    byte of the divisor reaches the hardware. The routine does not check
 *    for 0: the hardware then answers quotient $FFFF, remainder = dividend.
 *  - Divisor 255 and up: long division by hand, 16 rounds of "shift one
 *    bit of the dividend into the remainder; if it fits, subtract and set a
 *    quotient bit". The quotient is built in $82.
 *    Quirk: the running remainder is only 16 bits, so with a divisor above
 *    $8000 its top bit can fall off (ROL) and the result is wrong. Nobody
 *    in the game divides by such numbers; the rewrite copies it anyway.
 *
 * The hand path saves Y on the stack (PHY, Y = 0 there), so two zero bytes
 * are left just below the stack pointer.
 */
#include "hm_decomp.h"
#include "hm_ram.h"   /* from the recompilation project */
#include "hm_regs.h"

/* ── Names of the memory locations used here ────────────────────────────── */

/* Direct page */
#define DIVIDEND   0x7E   /* 16b; the remainder ends up here too */
#define DIVISOR    0x80   /* 16b */
#define QUOTIENT   0x82   /* 16b: only used (and written) by the hand path */
#define MUL_FACTOR 0x7E   /* 16b: Multiply16's second factor (the same word as
                             DIVIDEND, named by its role there) */

/* WRAM of the data bank: MultiplicationUnsigned / Multiply16 */
#define MUL_A      0x011A /* 8b: MultiplicationUnsigned's first factor */
#define MUL_B      0x011B /* 8b: its second factor */
#define MUL16_IN   0x011C /* 16b: Multiply16's A at the entry */
#define MUL16_LOW  0x011E /* 16b: low x low */
#define MUL16_HIGH_A 0x0120 /* 16b: (A's high x low) << 8 */
#define MUL16_HIGH_B 0x0122 /* 16b: (low x $7E's high) << 8 */

void hm_DivisionUnsigned(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint16_t dividend = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, DIVIDEND);
  uint16_t divisor = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, DIVISOR);
  r->y = 0;

  if (divisor < 0xFF) {
    /* Hardware divider: 16-bit dividend / 8-bit divisor. */
    uint8_t d = (uint8_t)divisor;
    hm_bus_wr16(ram, WRDIVL, dividend);  /* WRDIVL/H */
    hm_bus_wr8(ram, WRDIVB, d);          /* WRDIVB: starts it */
    uint16_t quotient = d ? (uint16_t)(dividend / d) : 0xFFFF;
    uint16_t remainder = d ? (uint16_t)(dividend % d) : dividend;
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, DIVIDEND, remainder);
    r->a = quotient;
  } else {
    hm_push8(ram, r, 0);                 /* PHY (Y = 0): high byte, then low */
    hm_push8(ram, r, 0);
    uint16_t quotient = 0, remainder = 0, bits = dividend;
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
      quotient = (uint16_t)(quotient << 1);
      remainder = (uint16_t)(remainder << 1 | bits >> 15);   /* top bit may fall off */
      bits = (uint16_t)(bits << 1);
      if (remainder >= divisor) {
        remainder = (uint16_t)(remainder - divisor);
        quotient++;
      }
    }
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, QUOTIENT, quotient);
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, DIVIDEND, remainder);
    hm_pull8(ram, r);                    /* PLA */
    hm_pull8(ram, r);
    r->a = quotient;
  }
  r->c = 0;                              /* TYA / PLA of 0, then LSR */
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * DivisionSigned ($83:80D0, JSL, RTL): the same with signs. Dividend and
 * divisor are made positive first (Y counts how many were negative), the
 * division is as above, and the quotient is negated when Y is odd. The
 * remainder in $7E stays positive. Leftovers: Y = that count on the
 * hardware path, 0 on the hand path (its loop counter); C = Y & 1.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_DivisionSigned(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint16_t negatives = 0;
  uint16_t dividend = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, DIVIDEND);
  if (dividend & 0x8000) {
    dividend = (uint16_t)(~dividend + 1);
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, DIVIDEND, dividend);
    negatives++;
  }
  uint16_t divisor = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, DIVISOR);
  if (divisor & 0x8000) {
    divisor = (uint16_t)(~divisor + 1);
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, DIVISOR, divisor);
    negatives++;
  }
  uint16_t quotient;
  if (divisor < 0xFF) {
    uint8_t d = (uint8_t)divisor;
    quotient = d ? (uint16_t)(dividend / d) : 0xFFFF;
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, DIVIDEND, d ? (uint16_t)(dividend % d) : dividend);
    r->y = negatives;
  } else {
    hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)(negatives >> 8));        /* PHY */
    hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)negatives);
    uint16_t remainder = 0, bits = dividend;
    quotient = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
      quotient = (uint16_t)(quotient << 1);
      remainder = (uint16_t)(remainder << 1 | bits >> 15);
      bits = (uint16_t)(bits << 1);
      if (remainder >= divisor) {
        remainder = (uint16_t)(remainder - divisor);
        quotient++;
      }
    }
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, QUOTIENT, quotient);
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, DIVIDEND, remainder);
    hm_pull8(ram, r);                                   /* PLA */
    hm_pull8(ram, r);
    r->y = 0;
  }
  r->c = negatives & 1;                                 /* TYA / PLA; LSR */
  r->a = r->c ? (uint16_t)(~quotient + 1) : quotient;
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * MultiplicationUnsigned ($83:8067, JSR, RTS): A = $011A x $011B (two
 * bytes, a 16-bit product), with the console's multiplier ($4202/$4203,
 * the answer in $4216 after a few cycles: the four NOPs). Nothing else
 * changes but the multiplier's registers (compared by the chip checks).
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_MultiplicationUnsigned(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t a = hm_bus_rd8(ram, (uint32_t)r->db << 16 | MUL_A);
  hm_bus_wr8(ram, WRMPYA, a);                           /* WRMPYA */
  uint8_t b = hm_bus_rd8(ram, (uint32_t)r->db << 16 | MUL_B);
  hm_bus_wr8(ram, WRMPYB, b);                           /* WRMPYB: starts it */
  r->a = (uint16_t)(a * b);                             /* RDMPY ($4216) */
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Multiply16 ($83:8000, JSL, RTL; a multiplication, despite its name):
 * A = A x $7E (16-bit, the high part lost), with three 8 x 8 products of
 * MultiplicationUnsigned: low x low, plus (high x low) << 8 and
 * (low x high) << 8 (only the low byte of each counts). Each is skipped
 * when its high byte is 0. Leftovers: $011C = A in, $011E / $0120 / $0122 =
 * the three parts, $011A / $011B = the last factors; X, Y and the flags
 * as they were (PHP / PLP).
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#define RET_23_LOW   0x801B
#define RET_23_HIGHA 0x8031
#define RET_23_HIGHB 0x8050

static uint32_t m_db(const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a) { return (uint32_t)r->db << 16 | a; }
static void m_wr16(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a, uint16_t v) { hm_bus_wr16(ram, m_db(r, a), v); }
static uint16_t m_rd16(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a) { return hm_bus_rd16(ram, m_db(r, a)); }
static void m_wr8(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a, uint8_t v) { hm_bus_wr8(ram, m_db(r, a), v); }
/* JSR MultiplicationUnsigned: A = $011A x $011B */
static uint16_t times(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t ret)
{
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)(ret >> 8));
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)ret);
  hm_MultiplicationUnsigned(ram, r);
  hm_pull8(ram, r); hm_pull8(ram, r);
  return r->a;
}

void hm_Multiply16(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  hm_push8(ram, r, r->p);                                     /* PHP */
  uint16_t a = r->a, b = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, MUL_FACTOR);
  m_wr16(ram, r, MUL16_IN, a);
  m_wr16(ram, r, MUL16_LOW, 0);
  m_wr16(ram, r, MUL16_HIGH_A, 0);
  m_wr16(ram, r, MUL16_HIGH_B, 0);
  m_wr8(ram, r, MUL_A, (uint8_t)a);
  m_wr8(ram, r, MUL_B, (uint8_t)b);
  m_wr16(ram, r, MUL16_LOW, times(ram, r, RET_23_LOW));
  if (a & 0xFF00) {
    m_wr8(ram, r, MUL_A, (uint8_t)(a >> 8));
    m_wr16(ram, r, MUL16_HIGH_A, (uint16_t)((times(ram, r, RET_23_HIGHA) & 0xFF) << 8));
  }
  if (b & 0xFF00) {
    m_wr8(ram, r, MUL_B, (uint8_t)(b >> 8));
    m_wr8(ram, r, MUL_A, (uint8_t)a);
    m_wr16(ram, r, MUL16_HIGH_B, (uint16_t)((times(ram, r, RET_23_HIGHB) & 0xFF) << 8));
  }
  r->a = (uint16_t)(m_rd16(ram, r, MUL16_LOW) + m_rd16(ram, r, MUL16_HIGH_A) + m_rd16(ram, r, MUL16_HIGH_B));
  hm_pull8(ram, r);                                           /* PLP */
}

```

`src/menus.c`:

```c
/*
 * menus.c — the buttons in menus (bank $84).
 *
 * InputTypeSelector ($84:C034) reads the input mode $019A each frame:
 * 1 walking, 2 no movement, 3 a list in a text box, 4 menus, 5 the name
 * screen, 6 another. In mode 4, MenuInputs looks at the menu $95:
 *   1    playing (the player's buttons, and Start opens the pause menu)
 *   2, 3 (Start: $95 = 6)
 *   5    the title menu: three options in $098D (0 load, 1 save..., 2 ...)
 *   7    choose a slot to save: $098E = the slot
 *   8    choose a slot to load: only a slot with a game can be taken
 * Each answer is in $94 (1 = B, cancel; 2 = A, accept). Every move makes a
 * sound effect (3, 6, $0A: move; 1: accept; 2: refused).
 *
 * Buttons (Joy1, $0128 = pressed this frame, $012C = with auto-repeat):
 * $8000 B, $1000 Start, $0800 up, $0400 down, $0200 left, $0100 right,
 * $0080 A.
 */
#include "hm_decomp.h"
#include "hm_ram.h"   /* from the recompilation project */
#include "hm_vars.h"

#define BTN_B       0x8000
#define BTN_START   0x1000
#define BTN_UP      0x0800
#define BTN_DOWN    0x0400
#define BTN_LEFT    0x0200
#define BTN_RIGHT   0x0100
#define BTN_A       0x0080
#define LIST_TEXTS  0x839467   /* DATA8_839467: the text of each of 11 places */

/* ── Names of the memory locations used here ──────────────────────────────
 * The shared variables (HM_...) are named in hm_vars.h and hm_ram.h. */

/* Direct page */
#define GRID_PTR          0x72   /* 24b $72-$74: the name page's grid */
#define GRID_PTR_BANK     0x74   /* 8b: GRID_PTR's bank */
#define CELL_BYTE         0x7E   /* 16b: ReadNameCursorCell: which byte + 2 (not read) */
#define MENU_ANSWER       0x94   /* 8b: the menu's answer: 1 = B, cancel; 2 = A, accept */

/* WRAM of the data bank (through db_addr / rd8 / wr8) */
#define SAVE_SLOT         0x098E   /* 8b: the diary slot chosen (0 or 1) */

/* ROM */
#define NAME_GRID_0       0xEBF8   /* $82:EBF8: the name screen's page 0, 8 bytes a cell */
#define NAME_GRID_1       0xEE30   /* $82:EE30: page 1 */
#define NAME_GRID_2       0xF0D0   /* $82:F0D0: page 2 */

static uint32_t db_addr(const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a) { return (uint32_t)r->db << 16 | a; }
static uint8_t rd8(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a) { return hm_bus_rd8(ram, db_addr(r, a)); }
static uint16_t rd16(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a) { return hm_bus_rd16(ram, db_addr(r, a)); }
static void wr8(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a, uint8_t v) { hm_bus_wr8(ram, db_addr(r, a), v); }
static void set_a8(HmRegs *r, uint8_t v) { r->a = (uint16_t)((r->a & 0xFF00) | v); }
static void jsl83(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t ret, void (*fn)(uint8_t *, HmRegs *))
{
  hm_jsl(ram, r, ret, 0x83);
  fn(ram, r);
  hm_rtl(ram, r);
}
/* $0114 = sound, $0115 = 6, PlaySoundEffect0A (effect sound, 6, $0A) */
static void beep(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t sound, uint16_t ret)
{
  wr8(ram, r, HM_SOUND_EFFECT, sound);
  set_a8(r, 6);
  wr8(ram, r, HM_SOUND_BANK, 6);
  jsl83(ram, r, ret, hm_PlaySoundEffect0A);
}
/* LDA Joy; BIT #button (A = the buttons) */
static bool pressed(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t at, uint16_t button)
{
  r->a = rd16(ram, r, at);
  return r->a & button;
}
/* the slot menus: up or down switch the slot ($098E 0 <-> 1), $97 = 1
 * (redraw) */
static void other_slot(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t ret)
{
  wr8(ram, r, SAVE_SLOT, (uint8_t)(rd8(ram, r, SAVE_SLOT) ^ 0x01));
  set_a8(r, 1);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_MENU_REDRAW) = 1;
  beep(ram, r, 3, ret);
}
static void answer(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t which, uint8_t sound, uint16_t ret)
{
  set_a8(r, which);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, MENU_ANSWER) = which;
  beep(ram, r, sound, ret);
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * SaveSlotMenuInputs ($84:C2FE, RTL; CODE_84C2FE, menu 7): up / down
 * change the slot, B cancels ($94 = 1), A accepts ($94 = 2).
 * Leftovers: A = the buttons if none was pressed; otherwise those of
 * PlaySoundEffect0A.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_SaveSlotMenuInputs(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_DOWN) || pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_UP)) other_slot(ram, r, 0xC34C);
  else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_B)) answer(ram, r, 1, 3, 0xC365);
  else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_A)) answer(ram, r, 2, 1, 0xC37E);
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * LoadSlotMenuInputs ($84:C380, RTL; CODE_84C380, menu 8): the same, but
 * A only accepts a slot with a game in it (LoadGameSlotResume answers
 * X = 1); an empty one gives the "refused" sound (2).
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_LoadSlotMenuInputs(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_DOWN) || pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_UP)) { other_slot(ram, r, 0xC3CE); return; }
  if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_B)) { answer(ram, r, 1, 3, 0xC3E7); return; }
  if (!pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_A)) return;
  r->a = rd8(ram, r, SAVE_SLOT);                      /* LDA #0; XBA; LDA $098E */
  jsl83(ram, r, 0xC3F4, hm_LoadGameSlotResume);
  r->c = 1;                                           /* CPX #0 */
  if (r->x != 0) answer(ram, r, 2, 1, 0xC413);
  else beep(ram, r, 2, 0xC426);
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * StartMenuInputs ($84:C428, RTL; CODE_84C428, menus 2 and 3): with
 * $7F1F5A bit $8000, Start goes to menu 6.
 * Leftovers: A = $7F1F5A & $8000 or the buttons; else PlaySoundEffect0A's.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_StartMenuInputs(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  r->a = hm_bus_rd16(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_FLAGS_5A)) & 0x8000;
  if (!r->a) return;
  if (!pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_START)) return;
  set_a8(r, 6);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_INTRO_STAGE) = 6;
  beep(ram, r, 3, 0xC456);
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * TitleMenuInputs ($84:C458, RTL; CODE_84C458, menu 5): three options in
 * $098D; down / up move (wrapping around), $90 = 0, $97 = 1 (redraw). A
 * opens the next menu: option 0 -> 8 (load a game), 1 -> 7, 2 -> $0A.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_TitleMenuInputs(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_DOWN)) {
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, HM_MENU_FRAMES, 0);
    uint8_t at = rd8(ram, r, HM_TITLE_CURSOR);
    r->c = at >= 2;                                   /* CMP #2 */
    uint8_t next = at == 2 ? 0 : (uint8_t)(at + 1);
    wr8(ram, r, HM_TITLE_CURSOR, next);
    set_a8(r, 1);
    *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_MENU_REDRAW) = 1;
    beep(ram, r, 3, at == 2 ? 0xC4C2 : 0xC4A2);
  } else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_UP)) {
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, HM_MENU_FRAMES, 0);
    uint8_t at = rd8(ram, r, HM_TITLE_CURSOR);
    wr8(ram, r, HM_TITLE_CURSOR, at == 0 ? 2 : (uint8_t)(at - 1));
    set_a8(r, 1);
    *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_MENU_REDRAW) = 1;
    beep(ram, r, 3, at == 0 ? 0xC50A : 0xC4E8);
  } else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_A)) {
    uint8_t at = rd8(ram, r, HM_TITLE_CURSOR);
    if (at != 0) r->c = at >= 1;                      /* CMP #1 */
    uint8_t menu = at == 0 ? 0x08 : at == 1 ? 0x07 : 0x0A;
    set_a8(r, menu);
    *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_INTRO_STAGE) = menu;
    beep(ram, r, 1, 0xC53E);
  }
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * ListInputs ($84:C540, RTL; CODE_84C540, input mode 3): a list of 22
 * places in a text box, two columns of 11 ($018A = the place; the arrow is
 * drawn at it). Down / up move in the column (wrapping 0 <-> 10), right /
 * left jump 11 (to the other column); these use the auto-repeat and first
 * erase the arrow (DrawTextBoxArrow frame 1). A closes the list: in the
 * first column it starts that place's text (DATA8_839467) in a box of
 * one line and goes back to "no movement" (mode 2); in the second it
 * just erases the arrow and goes back to walking (mode 1). Either way
 * BG2 scrolls back ($0142 = $100).
 * Note: the second column only works with right / left; up / down do
 * nothing there.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
static bool erase_arrow_if(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, bool first_column, uint16_t ret)
{
  uint8_t at = rd8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_PLACE);
  set_a8(r, at);
  r->c = at >= 0x0B;
  if (first_column ? at >= 0x0B : at < 0x0B) return false;
  r->a = 1;
  jsl83(ram, r, ret, hm_DrawTextBoxArrow);
  return true;
}
static void moved(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t to)
{
  wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_PLACE, to);
  set_a8(r, to);
  wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK, 0);
}

void hm_ListInputs(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_REPEAT, BTN_DOWN)) {
    beep(ram, r, 3, 0xC5E2);
    if (!erase_arrow_if(ram, r, true, 0xC5F4)) return;
    uint8_t at = rd8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_PLACE);
    r->c = at >= 0x0A;
    if (at == 0x0A) { set_a8(r, 0); wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_PLACE, 0); }
    else moved(ram, r, (uint8_t)(at + 1));
  } else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_REPEAT, BTN_UP)) {
    beep(ram, r, 3, 0xC623);
    if (!erase_arrow_if(ram, r, true, 0xC635)) return;
    uint8_t at = rd8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_PLACE);
    if (at == 0) { set_a8(r, 0x0A); wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_PLACE, 0x0A); }
    else moved(ram, r, (uint8_t)(at - 1));
  } else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_REPEAT, BTN_RIGHT)) {
    beep(ram, r, 3, 0xC662);
    if (!erase_arrow_if(ram, r, true, 0xC674)) return;
    r->c = 0;                                         /* CLC; ADC #$0B */
    moved(ram, r, (uint8_t)(rd8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_PLACE) + 0x0B));
  } else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_REPEAT, BTN_LEFT)) {
    beep(ram, r, 3, 0xC695);
    if (!erase_arrow_if(ram, r, false, 0xC6A7)) return;
    r->c = 1;                                         /* SEC; SBC #$0B */
    moved(ram, r, (uint8_t)(rd8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_PLACE) - 0x0B));
  } else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_A)) {
    beep(ram, r, 1, 0xC58B);
    wr8(ram, r, HM_TEXT_BOX_STATE, 0);
    wr8(ram, r, HM_INPUT_STATE, 2);
    uint8_t at = rd8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_PLACE);
    r->a = at;                                        /* LDA #0; XBA; LDA $018A */
    r->c = at >= 0x0B;
    if (at >= 0x0B) {
      wr8(ram, r, HM_INPUT_STATE, 1);
      r->a = 1;
      jsl83(ram, r, 0xC5B1, hm_DrawTextBoxArrow);
    } else {
      r->x = hm_bus_rd16(ram, LIST_TEXTS + 2u * at);
      r->a = (uint16_t)(r->x & 0xFF00);               /* LDA.L ...; TAX; SEP; LDA #0 */
      wr8(ram, r, HM_TEXT_BOX_LINES, 0);
      jsl83(ram, r, 0xC5C7, hm_StartTextBox);
    }
    r->a = 0x0100;
    hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_BG2_Y), 0x0100);
  }
}

/* ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 * ImmobileInputs ($84:CF05, RTL; input mode 2): the buttons while a text
 * box is open ($019B says in which state):
 *   bit 1, printing: holding A ($0124, "held") makes the next letter come
 *          at once ($0189 = 4);
 *   bit 2 (the end) or bit 5 (the arrow): A closes the box and the player
 *          can walk again (mode 1); the A press is used up ($0128 bit 7
 *          cleared);
 *   bit 3, waiting: A wipes the box and goes on with the next code (the
 *          cursor back to VRAM $5010, bit 3 cleared);
 *   bit 4, a choice: $018F = the option, $018E = the last one. The options
 *          are in two columns of three (0-2, 3-5); down / up move in the
 *          column, right / left jump to the other one; A closes the box.
 *          Before moving, the cursor is erased (letter $B1 at $0185).
 * ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */

static void erase_cursor(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t ret)
{
  r->x = 1;
  r->a = 0x00B1;
  jsl83(ram, r, ret, hm_DrawLetter);
}
static void choose(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t option)
{
  wr8(ram, r, HM_ANSWER, option);
  set_a8(r, option);
}

static void choice_down(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  beep(ram, r, 3, 0xCFFB);
  erase_cursor(ram, r, 0xD007);
  uint8_t at = rd8(ram, r, HM_ANSWER), last = rd8(ram, r, HM_LAST_OPTION);
  set_a8(r, at);
  r->c = at >= 3;
  if (at >= 3) {
    r->c = at >= last;
    choose(ram, r, at == last ? (uint8_t)(at - 1) : (uint8_t)(at + 1));
  } else {
    r->c = at >= last;
    if (at != last) r->c = at >= 2;
    if (at == last || at == 2) wr8(ram, r, HM_ANSWER, 0);
    else choose(ram, r, (uint8_t)(at + 1));
  }
  wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK, 0);
}

static void choice_up(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  beep(ram, r, 3, 0xD04B);
  erase_cursor(ram, r, 0xD057);
  uint8_t at = rd8(ram, r, HM_ANSWER), last = rd8(ram, r, HM_LAST_OPTION);
  set_a8(r, at);
  if (at == 0) {                                     /* to the bottom of the column */
    set_a8(r, last);
    r->c = last >= 3;
    choose(ram, r, last >= 3 ? 2 : last);
  } else if (at == 3) {
    r->c = 1;
    set_a8(r, last);
    r->c = last >= 3;
    if (last != 3) choose(ram, r, 4);                /* LDA $018F; INC */
  } else {
    r->c = at >= 3;
    choose(ram, r, (uint8_t)(at - 1));
  }
  wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK, 0);
}

static void choice_across(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t ret_beep, uint16_t ret_erase)
{
  beep(ram, r, 3, ret_beep);
  uint8_t last = rd8(ram, r, HM_LAST_OPTION);
  set_a8(r, last);
  r->c = last >= 3;
  if (last >= 3) {
    uint8_t at = rd8(ram, r, HM_ANSWER);
    set_a8(r, at);
    r->c = at >= 2;
    if (at != 2) {
      erase_cursor(ram, r, ret_erase);
      at = rd8(ram, r, HM_ANSWER);
      set_a8(r, at);
      r->c = at >= 2;
      if (at >= 2) { r->c = at >= 3; choose(ram, r, (uint8_t)(at - 3)); }
      else if (at == 1) {
        r->c = 1;
        set_a8(r, last);
        r->c = last >= 3;
        if (last != 3) { r->c = 0; choose(ram, r, 4); }
      } else {
        r->c = 0;
        choose(ram, r, 3);
      }
    }
  }
  wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK, 0);
}

void hm_ImmobileInputs(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t box = rd8(ram, r, HM_TEXT_BOX_STATE);
  set_a8(r, box & 0x02);
  if (box & 0x02) {                                   /* printing: A held = faster */
    if (!pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_HELD, BTN_A)) return;
    set_a8(r, 4);
    wr8(ram, r, HM_TEXT_TICK, 4);
    return;
  }
  set_a8(r, box & 0x04);
  bool close = box & 0x04;
  if (!close) {
    set_a8(r, box & 0x08);
    if (box & 0x08) {                                 /* waiting: A = go on */
      if (!pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_A)) return;
      jsl83(ram, r, 0xCF70, hm_ClearTextBox);
      hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_TEXT_CODE_AT), (uint16_t)(rd16(ram, r, HM_TEXT_CODE_AT) + 1));
      hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_TEXT_X), 0x5010);
      r->c = 0;                                       /* CLC; ADC #$10 */
      wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK, 0);
      uint8_t flags = (uint8_t)(rd8(ram, r, HM_TEXT_BOX_STATE) & 0xF7);
      wr8(ram, r, HM_TEXT_BOX_STATE, flags);
      r->a = (uint16_t)(0x5000 | flags);
      wr8(ram, r, HM_TEXT_TICK, 0);
      return;
    }
    set_a8(r, box & 0x10);
    if (box & 0x10) {                                 /* a choice */
      if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_DOWN))       choice_down(ram, r);
      else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_UP))    choice_up(ram, r);
      else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_RIGHT)) choice_across(ram, r, 0xD09F, 0xD0BB);
      else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_LEFT))  choice_across(ram, r, 0xD105, 0xD121);
      else if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_A)) {
        beep(ram, r, 1, 0xCFDD);
        jsl83(ram, r, 0xCFE1, hm_CloseTextBox);
        set_a8(r, 1);
        wr8(ram, r, HM_INPUT_STATE, 1);
      }
      return;
    }
    set_a8(r, box & 0x20);
    close = box & 0x20;
    if (!close) return;
  }
  if (!pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_A)) return;   /* the end: A closes */
  jsl83(ram, r, 0xCF4E, hm_CloseTextBox);
  set_a8(r, 1);
  wr8(ram, r, HM_INPUT_STATE, 1);
  r->a = (uint16_t)(rd16(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW) & 0xFF7F);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_PAD1_NEW), r->a);
}

/* ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 * The name screen (input mode 5). The letters are a grid; ReadNameCursorCell
 * reads the cell under the cursor ($0991) in the grid of the page shown
 * ($0993: 0 $82:EBF8, 1 $82:EE30, else $82:F0D0). Each cell has 8 bytes:
 * x, y, the cell reached with each arrow (down, up, and the two others),
 * the letter, and a code: 1-3 switch to page 0-2, 4 "done".
 * The name being typed is at $0885 (4 letters, $B1 = empty), $0994 how many.
 * ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */

/* ReadNameCursorCell ($82:EBAC, JSL, RTL): A = which byte of the cell (0-5:
 * the arrows, the letter, the code) -> A = that byte. */
void hm_ReadNameCursorCell(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint16_t which = r->a;
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)(which >> 8));                 /* PHA */
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)which);
  uint16_t grid = NAME_GRID_0;
  uint8_t page = rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_PAGE);
  r->a = (uint16_t)((0xEB00) | page);                      /* LDA #$82 ... LDA $0993 */
  if (page != 0) {
    r->c = page >= 1;
    grid = page == 1 ? NAME_GRID_1 : NAME_GRID_2;
  }
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, GRID_PTR, grid);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, GRID_PTR_BANK) = 0x82;
  uint16_t lo = hm_pull8(ram, r);
  which = (uint16_t)(lo | hm_pull8(ram, r) << 8);
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, CELL_BYTE, (uint16_t)(which + 2));
  uint32_t s = (uint32_t)(uint16_t)(rd16(ram, r, HM_NAME_CELL) << 3) + (uint16_t)(which + 2);
  r->c = s > 0xFFFF;
  r->y = (uint16_t)s;
  r->a = hm_bus_rd8(ram, hm_dp_long(ram, r, GRID_PTR, r->y)); /* LDA #0; XBA; LDA [$72],Y */
}

/* NameCursorPosition ($82:EB57, JSL, RTL): the cursor's place on the name screen:
 * the first two bytes of the current cell (x, y) into $099B / $099D.
 * Leftovers: $72-$74 = the page's grid, A = y, Y = 8 x cell + 1, C = bit
 * 13 of the cell number (the last ASL). */
void hm_NameCursorPosition(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint16_t grid = NAME_GRID_0;
  uint8_t page = rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_PAGE);
  if (page != 0) grid = page == 1 ? NAME_GRID_1 : NAME_GRID_2;
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, GRID_PTR, grid);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, GRID_PTR_BANK) = 0x82;
  uint16_t cell = rd16(ram, r, HM_NAME_CELL);
  r->c = (cell >> 13) & 1;                                 /* ASL x 3 */
  r->y = (uint16_t)(cell << 3);
  r->a = hm_bus_rd8(ram, hm_dp_long(ram, r, GRID_PTR, r->y));
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_NAME_CURSOR_X), r->a);
  r->y++;
  r->a = hm_bus_rd8(ram, hm_dp_long(ram, r, GRID_PTR, r->y));
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_NAME_CURSOR_Y), r->a);
}

/* DrawNameLetter ($82:EA60, JSL, RTL): draw letter A at the name's place
 * $0994 (the letter cursor $0185 from DATA16_82EB4D: $5010, $5020...). */
void hm_DrawNameLetter(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint16_t letter = r->a;
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)(letter >> 8));
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)letter);
  uint16_t i = rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT);
  r->c = (i << 1) > 0xFFFF;
  r->x = (uint16_t)(i << 1);
  r->a = hm_bus_rd16(ram, NAME_LETTER_AT + r->x);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, 0x800000 | HM_TEXT_X, r->a);
  uint16_t lo = hm_pull8(ram, r);
  r->a = (uint16_t)(lo | hm_pull8(ram, r) << 8);
  r->x = 0x0001;
  hm_jsl(ram, r, 0xEA7E, 0x83);
  hm_DrawLetter(ram, r);
  hm_rtl(ram, r);
}

/* the arrows: move the cursor to the cell the grid says */
static void name_move(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t which, uint16_t ret1, uint16_t ret2)
{
  r->a = which;
  hm_jsl(ram, r, ret1, 0x82);
  hm_ReadNameCursorCell(ram, r);
  hm_rtl(ram, r);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_NAME_CELL), r->a);
  beep(ram, r, 3, ret2);
}
void hm_NameMenuKeyDown(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)  { name_move(ram, r, 0, 0xC20C, 0xC223); }
void hm_NameMenuKeyUp(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)    { name_move(ram, r, 1, 0xC22D, 0xC244); }
void hm_NameMenuKeyLeft(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)  { name_move(ram, r, 2, 0xC24E, 0xC265); }
void hm_NameMenuKeyRight(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r) { name_move(ram, r, 3, 0xC26F, 0xC286); }

/* NameMenuKeyB ($84:C0AB): erase the last letter (with 4 letters there is
 * no cursor to clear first). */
void hm_NameMenuKeyB(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t n = rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT);
  set_a8(r, n);
  if (n) {
    r->c = n >= 4;
    if (n != 4) {
      r->a = 0x00A8;                                       /* the cursor's place: blank */
      hm_jsl(ram, r, 0xC0BE, 0x82);
      hm_DrawNameLetter(ram, r);
      hm_rtl(ram, r);
    }
    r->a = (uint8_t)(rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT) - 1);      /* LDA #0; XBA; LDA; DEC */
    r->x = r->a;
    set_a8(r, 0xB1);
    wr8(ram, r, (uint16_t)(HM_NAME_TYPED + r->x), 0xB1);
    n = (uint8_t)(rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT) - 1);
    set_a8(r, n);
    wr8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT, n);
  }
  beep(ram, r, 2, 0xC0EC);
}

/* NameMenuKeyA ($84:C0EE): the cell's code: switch page (the BG1 scroll
 * shows it), "done" (only with a letter at least: $0993 = 3), or add the
 * letter (up to 4). */
void hm_NameMenuKeyA(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  static const struct { uint16_t bg_x, bg_y, ret; } PAGE[3] = {
    { 0x0000, 0x0000, 0xC17C }, { 0x0100, 0x0000, 0xC1A6 }, { 0x0000, 0x0100, 0xC1D0 },
  };
  r->a = 5;
  hm_jsl(ram, r, 0xC0F6, 0x82);
  hm_ReadNameCursorCell(ram, r);
  hm_rtl(ram, r);
  uint16_t code = r->a;
  for (uint16_t k = 1; k <= 4; k++) {
    r->c = code >= k;
    if (code != k) continue;
    if (k == 4) {                                          /* done */
      uint8_t n = rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT);
      set_a8(r, n);
      if (!n) { beep(ram, r, 2, 0xC202); return; }
      set_a8(r, 3);
      wr8(ram, r, HM_NAME_PAGE, 3);
      beep(ram, r, 1, 0xC1EF);
      return;
    }
    set_a8(r, (uint8_t)(k - 1));
    wr8(ram, r, HM_NAME_PAGE, (uint8_t)(k - 1));
    r->a = PAGE[k - 1].bg_x;
    hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_CAM_X), PAGE[k - 1].bg_x);
    hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_CAM_Y), PAGE[k - 1].bg_y);
    if (k == 3) r->a = 0x0100;
    hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_NAME_CELL), 0);
    beep(ram, r, 1, PAGE[k - 1].ret);
    return;
  }
  uint8_t n = rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT);
  set_a8(r, n);
  r->c = n >= 4;
  if (n != 4) {                                            /* add the letter */
    r->a = 4;
    hm_jsl(ram, r, 0xC124, 0x82);
    hm_ReadNameCursorCell(ram, r);
    hm_rtl(ram, r);
    uint8_t letter = (uint8_t)r->a;
    hm_push8(ram, r, letter);                              /* PHA */
    r->x = rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT);                     /* LDA #0; XBA; LDA; TAX */
    r->a = (uint16_t)(hm_pull8(ram, r));                   /* PLA (A high = 0) */
    wr8(ram, r, (uint16_t)(HM_NAME_TYPED + r->x), letter);
    hm_jsl(ram, r, 0xC13A, 0x82);
    hm_DrawNameLetter(ram, r);
    hm_rtl(ram, r);
    n = (uint8_t)(rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT) + 1);
    set_a8(r, n);
    wr8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT, n);
  }
  beep(ram, r, 1, 0xC155);
}

/* NameMenuInputs ($84:C066): the arrows with auto-repeat, then B, then A */
void hm_NameMenuInputs(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  static const struct { uint16_t at, button; void (*fn)(uint8_t *, HmRegs *); } K[] = {
    { HM_PAD1_REPEAT, BTN_DOWN, hm_NameMenuKeyDown }, { HM_PAD1_REPEAT, BTN_UP, hm_NameMenuKeyUp },
    { HM_PAD1_REPEAT, BTN_RIGHT, hm_NameMenuKeyLeft }, { HM_PAD1_REPEAT, BTN_LEFT, hm_NameMenuKeyRight },
    { HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_B, hm_NameMenuKeyB }, { HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_A, hm_NameMenuKeyA },
  };
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof K / sizeof K[0]; i++)
    if (pressed(ram, r, K[i].at, K[i].button)) { K[i].fn(ram, r); return; }
}

/* ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 * Menu 1 (MenuEventPad): the player moved by an event's pad (unless in the
 * air); with $7F1F5A bit $8000, Start skips: menu 9 (SkipEventScene, which
 * also sets $7F1F5C bit 2).
 * ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
void hm_SkipEventScene(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  set_a8(r, 9);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_INTRO_STAGE) = 9;
  beep(ram, r, 3, 0xC2EF);
  r->a = (uint16_t)(hm_bus_rd16(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_FLAGS_5C)) | 0x0004);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_FLAGS_5C), r->a);
}
void hm_MenuEventPad(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  r->a = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, HM_PLAYER_ACTION);
  r->c = r->a >= 3;
  if (r->a != 3) {
    hm_jsl(ram, r, 0xC2C0, 0x84);
    hm_ReadEventPad(ram, r);
    hm_rtl(ram, r);
  }
  r->a = hm_bus_rd16(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_FLAGS_5A)) & 0x8000;
  if (!r->a) return;
  if (pressed(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW, BTN_START)) hm_SkipEventScene(ram, r);
}

/* MenuInputs ($84:C288): by the menu number $95 */
void hm_MenuInputs(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  static const struct { uint8_t menu; void (*fn)(uint8_t *, HmRegs *); } M[] = {
    { 1, hm_MenuEventPad }, { 2, hm_StartMenuInputs }, { 3, hm_StartMenuInputs },
    { 5, hm_TitleMenuInputs }, { 7, hm_SaveSlotMenuInputs }, { 8, hm_LoadSlotMenuInputs },
  };
  uint8_t m = *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_INTRO_STAGE);
  set_a8(r, m);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof M / sizeof M[0]; i++) {
    r->c = m >= M[i].menu;
    if (m == M[i].menu) { M[i].fn(ram, r); return; }
  }
}

/* TextBoxAutoClose ($84:CED2, input mode 6): with $019B bit 2, after 120 frames
 * close the text box and go back to walking (and forget a pressed A). */
void hm_TextBoxAutoClose(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t box = rd8(ram, r, HM_TEXT_BOX_STATE);
  set_a8(r, box & 0x04);
  if (!(box & 0x04)) return;
  r->a = (uint16_t)(rd16(ram, r, HM_TEXT_AUTO_CLOSE_TIMER) + 1);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_TEXT_AUTO_CLOSE_TIMER), r->a);
  r->c = r->a >= 0x78;
  if (r->a != 0x78) return;
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_TEXT_AUTO_CLOSE_TIMER), 0);
  hm_jsl(ram, r, 0xCEF1, 0x83);
  hm_CloseTextBox(ram, r);
  hm_rtl(ram, r);
  set_a8(r, 1);
  wr8(ram, r, HM_INPUT_STATE, 1);
  r->a = rd16(ram, r, HM_PAD1_NEW) & 0xFF7F;
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, db_addr(r, HM_PAD1_NEW), r->a);
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * InputTypeSelector ($84:C034): by the input mode $019A.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_InputTypeSelector(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  static void (*const mode[])(uint8_t *, HmRegs *) = {
    hm_PlayerMovementInputs, hm_ImmobileInputs, hm_ListInputs, hm_MenuInputs,
    hm_NameMenuInputs, hm_TextBoxAutoClose,
  };
  uint8_t m = rd8(ram, r, HM_INPUT_STATE);
  set_a8(r, m);
  for (uint8_t k = 1; k <= 6; k++) {
    r->c = m >= k;
    if (m == k) { mode[k - 1](ram, r); return; }
  }
}
```

`src/names.c`:

```c
/*
 * names.c — after a name was written in the names screen (NamesScreen):
 * the name goes where it belongs, and the game goes on.
 *
 * The four letters typed are at $0885-$0888. Each routine fades the
 * screen out (from 15, 3 frames a level, to 1), blanks it, clears VRAM
 * and CGRAM, keeps the name, asks for a map to be entered ($0196 bit 14,
 * which SetScreenTransition sees), puts BG3 back ($0146 = $100), the
 * controls back to the player ($019A = 1), and jumps into the game loop
 * (GameLoop, $80:8083), which never comes back: the check stops there
 * (HM_TOLOOP).
 * Each name is kept twice: one byte a letter, and one word a letter (the
 * text routines use the words).
 */
#include "hm_decomp.h"
#include "hm_ram.h"   /* from the recompilation project */
#include "hm_vars.h"

typedef void Fn(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r);

/* ── Names of the memory locations used here ──────────────────────────────
 * The shared variables (HM_...) are named in hm_vars.h and hm_ram.h. */

/* Direct page */
#define NMI_STATUS      0x00   /* 8b: set by the NMI, cleared by the loop */
#define DMA_CHANNEL     0x27   /* 8b: AddProgrammedDMA's channel (dma.c) */
#define DMA_B_ADDRESS   0x29   /* 8b: its destination register ($22 = CGRAM data) */
#define DMA_SOURCE      0x72   /* 24b $72-$74: its source */
#define DMA_SOURCE_BANK 0x74   /* 8b: the source's bank */
#define DRIFT_FRAME     0x96   /* 8b: the background drifts when it is 1 (0 / 1) */

/* WRAM of the data bank */
#define CURSOR_GOBJ     0x0995 /* 16b: the cursor's game object */
#define CURSOR_SPRITE   0x0997 /* 16b: the cursor's sprite, kept */
#define CURSOR_FLIP     0x0999 /* 16b: its flip */

/* ROM: the names screen's colours, in bank $A9 */
#define NAME_COLOURS_1  0x8C00   /* $A9:8C00, $100 bytes */
#define NAME_COLOURS_2  0xDE00   /* $A9:DE00, $100 bytes */

static uint32_t db(const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a) { return (uint32_t)r->db << 16 | a; }
static uint8_t rd8(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a) { return hm_bus_rd8(ram, db(r, a)); }
static uint16_t rd16(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a) { return hm_bus_rd16(ram, db(r, a)); }
static void wr8(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a, uint8_t v) { hm_bus_wr8(ram, db(r, a), v); }
static void wr16(uint8_t *ram, const HmRegs *r, uint16_t a, uint16_t v) { hm_bus_wr16(ram, db(r, a), v); }
static void set_a8(HmRegs *r, uint8_t v) { r->a = (uint16_t)((r->a & 0xFF00) | v); }

/* JSL at `at` (bank 80 unless said): the fade saves the flags (PHP):
 * r->p carries the carry, 8-bit A, 16-bit indexes, D and I of the entry
 * (N, Z and V are not followed: HM_LOOSE) */
static void jsl(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t at, uint8_t bank, Fn *fn)
{
  uint8_t keep = r->p;
  r->p = (uint8_t)((keep & 0x0C) | 0x20 | (r->c & 1));
  hm_jsl(ram, r, (uint16_t)(at + 3), bank);
  fn(ram, r);
  hm_rtl(ram, r);
  r->p = keep;
}
/* the fade out and the cleared screen; the JSLs from `at` */
static void dark(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t at)
{
  set_a8(r, 0x0F); *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_FROM) = 0x0F;    /* SEP #$20; REP #$10 */
  set_a8(r, 0x03); *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_FRAMES) = 0x03;
  set_a8(r, 0x01); *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_TO) = 0x01;
  jsl(ram, r, at, 0x80, hm_ScreenFadeOut);
  jsl(ram, r, (uint16_t)(at + 4), 0x80, hm_ForceBlank);
  jsl(ram, r, (uint16_t)(at + 8), 0x80, hm_ZeroesVRAM);
  jsl(ram, r, (uint16_t)(at + 12), 0x80, hm_ZeroesCGRAM);
}
/* the four letters to `bytes` (one byte each, a full address) and `words`
 * (one word each) */
static void keep_name(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint32_t bytes, uint16_t words)
{
  for (uint16_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) {                       /* LDA #0; XBA: A's top 0 */
    uint8_t letter = rd8(ram, r, (uint16_t)(HM_NAME_TYPED + i));
    r->a = letter;
    hm_bus_wr8(ram, bytes + i, letter);
    wr16(ram, r, (uint16_t)(words + 2 * i), letter);
  }
}
/* a new cow (AddNewCow: A = 0 bought, 1 born) and its name at +0C-+0F */
static void new_cow(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t born, uint16_t at)
{
  r->a = born;                                             /* REP #$20 */
  jsl(ram, r, at, 0x83, hm_AddNewCow);
  for (uint16_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) {                       /* SEP #$20; REP #$10 */
    r->y = (uint16_t)(COW_NAME + i);
    set_a8(r, rd8(ram, r, (uint16_t)(HM_NAME_TYPED + i)));
    hm_bus_wr8(ram, hm_dp_long(ram, r, HM_ANIMAL_PTR, r->y), (uint8_t)r->a);
  }
}
/* $0196 bit 14 is already set by the flag lines; BG3 and the controls */
static void back_to_game(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  r->a = 0x0100;                                           /* REP #$20 */
  wr16(ram, r, HM_BG3_Y, 0x0100);
  set_a8(r, 0x01);                                         /* SEP #$20 */
  wr8(ram, r, HM_INPUT_STATE, 0x01);
  g_hm_next = 0x808083;
  /* JMP GameLoop: the check stops here (HM_TOLOOP) */
}
static void go_to_map(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  r->a = (uint16_t)(rd16(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS) | 0x4000); /* REP #$20 */
  wr16(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS, r->a);
}
static void flag_off(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint32_t addr, uint16_t bits)
{
  r->a = (uint16_t)(hm_bus_rd16(ram, addr) & ~bits);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, addr, r->a);
}

/* SetPlayerName ($80:80ED): $0881-$0884 and $08D5-$08DB */
void hm_SetPlayerName(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  dark(ram, r, 0x80FD);
  keep_name(ram, r, db(r, HM_PLAYER_NAME), HM_PLAYER_NAME_WORDS);
  go_to_map(ram, r);
  back_to_game(ram, r);
}
/* SetCowNameBought ($80:815F): a bought cow; $7F1F5A bit 1 (buying it)
 * off */
void hm_SetCowNameBought(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  dark(ram, r, 0x816F);
  new_cow(ram, r, 0, 0x8184);
  go_to_map(ram, r);
  flag_off(ram, r, WRAM_LONG(HM_FLAGS_5A), 0x0002);
  back_to_game(ram, r);
}
/* SetCowNameBorn ($80:81D2): a calf; $7F1F64 bits 2 and 3 (the birth)
 * off */
void hm_SetCowNameBorn(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  dark(ram, r, 0x81E2);
  new_cow(ram, r, 1, 0x81F7);
  flag_off(ram, r, WRAM_LONG(HM_FLAGS_64), 0x0004);
  flag_off(ram, r, WRAM_LONG(HM_FLAGS_64), 0x0008);
  go_to_map(ram, r);
  back_to_game(ram, r);
}
/* SetDogName ($80:8254): $0899-$089C and $08DD-$08E3 */
void hm_SetDogName(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  dark(ram, r, 0x8264);
  keep_name(ram, r, db(r, HM_DOG_NAME), HM_DOG_NAME_WORDS);
  go_to_map(ram, r);
  back_to_game(ram, r);
}
/* SetHorseName ($80:82C6): $089D-$08A0 and $08E5-$08EB */
void hm_SetHorseName(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  dark(ram, r, 0x82D6);
  keep_name(ram, r, db(r, HM_HORSE_NAME), HM_HORSE_NAME_WORDS);
  go_to_map(ram, r);
  back_to_game(ram, r);
}
/* SetKid1Name ($80:8338): $7F1F3D-$7F1F40 (the save's) and $08ED-$08F3 */
void hm_SetKid1Name(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  dark(ram, r, 0x8348);
  keep_name(ram, r, WRAM_LONG(HM_KID1_NAME), HM_KID1_NAME_WORDS);
  go_to_map(ram, r);
  back_to_game(ram, r);
}
/* SetKid2Name ($80:83AE): $7F1F41-$7F1F44 and $08F5-$08FB */
void hm_SetKid2Name(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  dark(ram, r, 0x83BE);
  keep_name(ram, r, WRAM_LONG(HM_KID2_NAME), HM_KID2_NAME_WORDS);
  go_to_map(ram, r);
  back_to_game(ram, r);
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * NamesScreen ($82:E80C; GameLoop jumps here, JML, with $0196 bit 13):
 * the names screen.
 *  - The setup: the music of map $5F (PickMapMusic, FadeOutSongSlowly), the
 *    screen faded out (from 15, 3 frames a level, to 1) and blanked, VRAM
 *    cleared, the colour cycles, sprites and objects stopped
 *    (StopAllColourAnimations, ClearSpriteDataTables, InitializeOBJs); $0196 kept
 *    in $0198 and cleared, no player object ($0905 = 0), the controls to
 *    the names screen ($019A = 5); its graphics (preset 4,
 *    BackgroundsManager), its colours (palette $6F), two blocks of $100
 *    bytes from $A9:8C00 and $A9:DE00 to CGRAM; ClearItemRecords; the
 *    cursor's sprite (CreateGameObject at (40, 68), animation $219, kept
 *    in $0995-$099D); the frames of the name (DrawScreenBar, DrawNameEntryBlanks); the
 *    scrolls at 0; the music changes (FadeOutSong, 20, 22); the screen lit
 *    and faded in (from 3, 3 frames a level, to 15); page 0, cell 0, no
 *    letters ($0885-$0888 = $B1, blank).
 *  - Then a frame at a time (from $82:E95F): wait for the NMI; the cursor
 *    of the name blinks (every $14 frames, local $82:EA15); the joypad
 *    (InputTypeSelector); unless the name is done ($0993 = 3), the cursor
 *    moves (NameCursorPosition), the background drifts one pixel every other frame
 *    (BG2 x + 1, y - 1), the cursor's sprite is drawn (MoveGameObject,
 *    AnimateGameObjects, LoadQueuedSpritePieces, PrepareOAMData); and round again.
 *  - Done: $0196 back, and on to where the name goes ($099F: 0 the player,
 *    1 a cow bought, 2 a calf, 3 the dog, 4 the horse, 5 / 6 the
 *    children: SetPlayerName... SetKid2Name, JML; any other value would go
 *    round for ever).
 * Bug: DrawScreenBar ends with RTS but is called with JSL, so a byte (the
 * bank, $82) stays on the stack from there on. Nothing returns from here,
 * so it does no harm; the check's stop takes it off before its RTL.
 * The check stops after the first frame (the JML back to $82:E95F), or at
 * the JML to the name's routine (HM_TOLOOP); NamesScreenFrame checks a
 * frame on its own.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
static void zero16_all(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t from, uint16_t to)
{
  for (uint16_t a = from; a <= to; a += 2) wr16(ram, r, a, 0);
}
/* two blocks of colours to CGRAM ($27 the channel, $29 = $22) */
static void colours(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t channel, uint16_t to, uint16_t from, uint16_t at)
{
  set_a8(r, channel);                                      /* SEP #$20; REP #$10 */
  *hm_dp(ram, r, DMA_CHANNEL) = channel;
  set_a8(r, 0x22);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, DMA_B_ADDRESS) = 0x22;
  r->y = 0x0100;                                           /* REP #$20 */
  r->x = to;
  r->a = from;
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, DMA_SOURCE, from);
  set_a8(r, 0xA9);                                         /* SEP #$20 */
  *hm_dp(ram, r, DMA_SOURCE_BANK) = 0xA9;
  jsl(ram, r, at, 0x80, hm_AddProgrammedDMA);
}
/* the four numbers of the cursor's sprite: to the direct page and kept */
static const struct { uint8_t dp; uint16_t keep; } CURSOR[4] = {
  { HM_OBJ_SPRITE, CURSOR_SPRITE }, { HM_OBJ_FLIP, CURSOR_FLIP },
  { HM_OBJ_X, HM_NAME_CURSOR_X }, { HM_OBJ_Y, HM_NAME_CURSOR_Y },
};

/* $82:EA15 (JSR): the name's cursor blinks: unless the name is full, every
 * $14 counts ($018B, bit 7 the phase) the phase turns; the cursor is drawn
 * ($A8) or blanked ($B1) at the name's place (DrawNameLetter) */
static void name_cursor(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t n = rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT);                  /* SEP #$20; REP #$10 */
  set_a8(r, n);
  r->c = n >= 4;
  if (n == 4) return;
  r->a = (uint16_t)(rd16(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK) & 0x007F); /* REP #$20 */
  r->c = r->a >= 0x0014;
  if (r->a == 0x0014) {
    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)((rd8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK) & 0x80) ^ 0x80); /* SEP #$20 */
    set_a8(r, v);
    wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK, v);
  }
  uint8_t phase = (uint8_t)(rd8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK) & 0x80);
  set_a8(r, phase);
  if (!phase) { r->a = 0x00A8; jsl(ram, r, 0xEA47, 0x82, hm_DrawNameLetter); }
  else        { r->a = 0x00B1; jsl(ram, r, 0xEA52, 0x82, hm_DrawNameLetter); }
  uint8_t c = (uint8_t)(rd8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK) + 1);  /* SEP #$20 */
  set_a8(r, c);
  wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK, c);
}

/* the done name: $0196 back, and the JML to its routine (the check stops
 * there: not followed) */
static void name_done(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  r->a = rd16(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS_KEPT);              /* REP #$20 */
  wr16(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS, r->a);
  uint8_t to = rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_FOR);                   /* SEP #$20 */
  set_a8(r, to);
  static const uint32_t SET_NAME[7] = { 0x8080ED, 0x80815F, 0x8081D2, 0x808254, 0x8082C6, 0x808338, 0x8083AE };
  for (uint8_t k = 0; k <= 6; k++) {
    r->c = to >= k;
    if (to == k) { g_hm_next = SET_NAME[k]; return; }     /* JML Set...Name */
  }
  for (;;) { }                                             /* BRA: round for ever */
}

/* one frame of the names screen ($82:E95F); false once the name is done */
static bool name_frame(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t entry)
{
  for (;;) {                                               /* SEP #$20; LDA $00; BEQ */
    uint8_t ready = *hm_dp(ram, r, NMI_STATUS);
    set_a8(r, ready);
    if (ready) break;
    hm_nmi(ram, r, 0xE961, (uint8_t)(entry | 0x20));
  }
  r->a = 0x1800;                                           /* REP #$20 */
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, HM_LOAD_BUDGET, 0x1800);
  hm_push8(ram, r, 0xE9); hm_push8(ram, r, 0x6E);          /* JSR $EA15 */
  name_cursor(ram, r);
  hm_pull8(ram, r); hm_pull8(ram, r);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE96F, 0x84, hm_InputTypeSelector);
  uint8_t page = rd8(ram, r, HM_NAME_PAGE);                /* SEP #$20 */
  set_a8(r, page);
  r->c = page >= 3;
  if (page == 3) { name_done(ram, r); return false; }
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE97F, 0x82, hm_NameCursorPosition);
  uint8_t drift = *hm_dp(ram, r, DRIFT_FRAME);             /* SEP #$20 */
  set_a8(r, drift);
  r->c = drift >= 1;
  if (drift == 1) {
    *hm_dp(ram, r, DRIFT_FRAME) = 0;
    wr16(ram, r, HM_BG2_X, (uint16_t)(rd16(ram, r, HM_BG2_X) + 1)); /* REP #$20 */
    wr16(ram, r, HM_BG2_Y, (uint16_t)(rd16(ram, r, HM_BG2_Y) - 1));
  } else {
    *hm_dp(ram, r, DRIFT_FRAME) = (uint8_t)(drift + 1);
  }
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {                            /* REP #$20 */
    r->a = rd16(ram, r, CURSOR[i].keep);
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, CURSOR[i].dp, r->a);
  }
  r->a = rd16(ram, r, CURSOR_GOBJ);
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_NUMBER, r->a);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE9B6, 0x85, hm_MoveGameObject);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE9BA, 0x85, hm_AnimateGameObjects);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE9BE, 0x85, hm_LoadQueuedSpritePieces);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE9C2, 0x85, hm_PrepareOAMData);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, NMI_STATUS) = 0;                          /* SEP #$20; STZ $00 */
  g_hm_next = 0x82E95F;
  return true;                                             /* JML $82:E95F */
}

void hm_NamesScreen(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t entry = r->p;
  set_a8(r, 0x5F);                                         /* SEP #$20 */
  *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_MAP_ID) = 0x5F;
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE812, 0x80, hm_PickMapMusic);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE816, 0x83, hm_FadeOutSongSlowly);
  set_a8(r, 0x0F); *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_FROM) = 0x0F;    /* SEP #$20 */
  set_a8(r, 0x03); *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_FRAMES) = 0x03;
  set_a8(r, 0x01); *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_TO) = 0x01;
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE828, 0x80, hm_ScreenFadeOut);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE82C, 0x80, hm_ForceBlank);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE830, 0x80, hm_ZeroesVRAM);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE834, 0x80, hm_StopAllColourAnimations);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE838, 0x85, hm_ClearSpriteDataTables);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE83C, 0x85, hm_InitializeOBJs);
  r->a = rd16(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS);                   /* REP #$20 */
  wr16(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS_KEPT, r->a);
  wr16(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS, 0);
  wr16(ram, r, HM_PLAYER_GOBJ, 0);
  set_a8(r, 0x05);                                         /* SEP #$20 */
  wr8(ram, r, HM_INPUT_STATE, 0x05);
  set_a8(r, 0x04);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE859, 0x80, hm_ManageGraphicPresets);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE85D, 0x80, hm_BackgroundsManager);
  r->a = 0x006F;                                           /* REP #$20 */
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE866, 0x80, hm_LoadFirstHalfPaletteToWRAM);
  colours(ram, r, 0, 0x0000, NAME_COLOURS_1, 0xE889);
  colours(ram, r, 1, 0x0080, NAME_COLOURS_2, 0xE8AC);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE8B0, 0x80, hm_StartProgrammedDMA);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE8B4, 0x81, hm_ClearItemRecords);
  static const uint16_t start[4] = { 0x0219, 0x0000, 0x0028, 0x0044 };
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {                            /* REP #$20 */
    r->a = start[i];
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, CURSOR[i].dp, start[i]);
    wr16(ram, r, CURSOR[i].keep, start[i]);
  }
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_PARAM, 0);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE8DC, 0x85, hm_CreateGameObject);
  r->a = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_NUMBER);                 /* REP #$20 */
  wr16(ram, r, CURSOR_GOBJ, r->a);
  hm_jsl(ram, r, 0xE8EA, 0x82);                            /* JSL ... */
  hm_DrawScreenBar(ram, r);
  hm_pull8(ram, r); hm_pull8(ram, r);                      /* ... RTS: the bank stays */
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE8EB, 0x82, hm_DrawNameEntryBlanks);
  zero16_all(ram, r, HM_CAM_X, HM_BG3_Y);                  /* REP #$20: the scrolls */
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE903, 0x83, hm_FadeOutSong);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE907, 0x83, hm_SetSong);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE90B, 0x83, hm_StartSong);
  uint8_t song = rd8(ram, r, HM_WANTED_SONG);              /* SEP #$20 */
  set_a8(r, song);
  wr8(ram, r, HM_PLAYING_SONG, song);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE917, 0x80, hm_ResetForceBlank);
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE91B, 0x80, hm_WaitForNMI);
  set_a8(r, 0x03); *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_FROM) = 0x03;    /* SEP #$20 */
  set_a8(r, 0x03); *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_FRAMES) = 0x03;
  set_a8(r, 0x0F); *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_TO) = 0x0F;
  jsl(ram, r, 0xE92D, 0x80, hm_ScreenFadeIn);
  wr16(ram, r, HM_NAME_CELL, 0);                           /* REP #$20 */
  set_a8(r, 0x00);                                         /* SEP #$20 */
  wr8(ram, r, HM_NAME_PAGE, 0);
  wr8(ram, r, HM_NAME_COUNT, 0);
  wr8(ram, r, HM_ARROW_BLINK, 0);
  set_a8(r, 0xB1);
  for (uint16_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) wr8(ram, r, (uint16_t)(HM_NAME_TYPED + i), 0xB1);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_TO) = 0;
  *hm_dp(ram, r, DRIFT_FRAME) = 0;
  *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_MENU_REDRAW) = 0;
  name_frame(ram, r, entry);
  hm_pull8(ram, r);   /* the check stops after the first frame, and takes the stray byte off */
}

/* $82:E95F: one frame of the names screen on its own (entered as the
 * JML back to it does) */
void hm_NamesScreenFrame(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  name_frame(ram, r, r->p);
}

```

`src/nmi.c`:

```c
/*
 * nmi.c — the interrupts and the waits for the next frame.
 *
 * Every frame the picture chip raises the NMI at the start of the vertical
 * blank. The CPU then pushes the bank, the address it was at and the flags,
 * sets I, clears decimal mode and runs the handler of the vector $FFEA in
 * bank $00 (NMI_Interrupt, $00:867B); the handler's RTI takes all three
 * back. The game's main loop and anything that waits a frame (the fades,
 * the sound commands) stop in WaitForNMI: clear $00 and loop until the
 * handler sets it again (UpdateGraphics does, at its end).
 *
 * In the recompiled game the wait is where the compiled code hands control
 * to the frame scheduler, so a live call never completes and the live
 * check skips it; the fuzzer runs these routines in the interpreter and,
 * when the original reaches the wait loop with $00 = 0, makes the NMI
 * happen right there (HM_WAIT in hm_decomp.h). hm_nmi below is the same on
 * the C side: the rewrites wait by running the handler at that point.
 */
#include "hm_decomp.h"
#include "hm_ram.h"   /* from the recompilation project */
#include "hm_vars.h"
#include "hm_regs.h"

/* ── Names of the memory locations used here ────────────────────────────── */

/* Direct page */
#define NMI_STATUS      0x00   /* 8b: set by the NMI (UpdateGraphics) */
#define FADE_BRIGHTNESS 0x25   /* 8b: the fades' brightness now */
#define FADE_FRAME      0x26   /* 8b: the fades' frames left at this level */

/* The CPU's registers */
#define NMI_ON          0xA1

static void push16(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t v)
{
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)(v >> 8));
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)v);
}
static uint16_t pull16(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t lo = hm_pull8(ram, r);
  return (uint16_t)(lo | hm_pull8(ram, r) << 8);
}
static void set_a8(HmRegs *r, uint8_t v) { r->a = (uint16_t)((r->a & 0xFF00) | v); }
/* RTI and PLP: the flags back; with 8-bit indexes their high bytes are 0 */
static void flags_back(HmRegs *r, uint8_t p)
{
  r->c = p & 1;
  r->n = (uint8_t)((p >> 7) & 1);
  if (p & 0x10) { r->x &= 0x00FF; r->y &= 0x00FF; }
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * NMI_Interrupt ($80:867B, the NMI vector; RTI): saves A, X, Y (16-bit),
 * D and the data bank, keeps the NMI on ($4200 = $A1), lets the line IRQ
 * in (CLI) and runs UpdateGraphics (JSR) with the interrupted code's direct
 * page and data bank; then takes everything back and returns (RTI).
 * Inside, A = $00A1 (LDA #0; XBA; LDA #$A1) and the flags UpdateGraphics
 * saves are N and M set, the rest clear but V and C.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_NMI_Interrupt(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  push16(ram, r, r->a);                                    /* REP #$30; PHA PHX PHY PHD PHB */
  push16(ram, r, r->x);
  push16(ram, r, r->y);
  push16(ram, r, r->d);
  hm_push8(ram, r, r->db);
  r->a = 0x00A1;
  hm_bus_wr8(ram, NMITIMEN, NMI_ON);
  uint8_t p_in = r->p;                                     /* CLI */
  r->p = (uint8_t)((p_in & 0x41) | 0xA0);
  r->n = 1;
  hm_push8(ram, r, 0x86); hm_push8(ram, r, 0x90);          /* JSR UpdateGraphics at $868E */
  hm_UpdateGraphics(ram, r);
  hm_pull8(ram, r); hm_pull8(ram, r);
  r->p = p_in;
  r->db = hm_pull8(ram, r);                                /* REP #$30; PLB PLD PLY PLX PLA */
  r->d = pull16(ram, r);
  r->y = pull16(ram, r);
  r->x = pull16(ram, r);
  r->a = pull16(ram, r);
  uint8_t p = hm_pull8(ram, r);                            /* RTI */
  hm_pull8(ram, r);
  hm_pull8(ram, r);
  r->pb = hm_pull8(ram, r);
  flags_back(r, p);
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * COP_Interrupt ($80:8699, the IRQ vector despite HM-Decomp's name; RTI):
 * the line IRQ. Saves the data bank, A, X, Y, reads TIMEUP ($4211, which
 * lets the IRQ go) and calls a routine that only returns (COP_Return, JSR);
 * then takes them back. The COP and BRK vectors point at the RTI at the end
 * of NMI_Interrupt ($80:8698).
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_COP_Interrupt(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  hm_push8(ram, r, r->db);                                 /* REP #$30; PHB PHA PHX PHY */
  push16(ram, r, r->a);
  push16(ram, r, r->x);
  push16(ram, r, r->y);
  r->a = (uint16_t)(r->a >> 8);                            /* LDA #0; XBA */
  set_a8(r, hm_bus_rd8(ram, (uint32_t)r->db << 16 | TIMEUP));
  hm_push8(ram, r, 0x86); hm_push8(ram, r, 0xA9);          /* JSR COP_Return at $86A7 */
  hm_pull8(ram, r); hm_pull8(ram, r);
  r->y = pull16(ram, r);                                   /* REP #$30; PLY PLX PLA PLB */
  r->x = pull16(ram, r);
  r->a = pull16(ram, r);
  r->db = hm_pull8(ram, r);
  uint8_t p = hm_pull8(ram, r);                            /* RTI */
  hm_pull8(ram, r);
  hm_pull8(ram, r);
  r->pb = hm_pull8(ram, r);
  flags_back(r, p);
}

uint32_t g_hm_next;
void (*g_hm_frame_hook)(uint8_t *ram);
uint16_t g_hm_oam_right = 0x0100, g_hm_oam_left = 0xFFF0;
int g_hm_no_ending;
int g_hm_crops_passable;
int g_hm_single_seed;
int g_hm_bag_on, g_hm_bag_take;
int g_hm_wife_on;
uint16_t g_hm_wife_until;
uint8_t g_hm_bag[9];
uint8_t g_hm_seeds_used[5];
uint16_t (*g_hm_year_suffix)(uint16_t x, uint16_t rom_value);

/* The NMI arriving at `pc` with the flags `p` (hm_decomp.h). */
void hm_nmi(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t pc, uint8_t p)
{
  if (g_hm_frame_hook) g_hm_frame_hook(ram);
  uint8_t keep = r->p;
  hm_push8(ram, r, r->pb);
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)(pc >> 8));
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)pc);
  hm_push8(ram, r, p);
  r->pb = 0x00;
  r->p = (uint8_t)((p | 0x04) & ~0x08);
  hm_NMI_Interrupt(ram, r);
  r->p = keep;
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * WaitForNMI ($80:8645, JSL, RTL): waits for the next frame. Saves the
 * flags and A, turns the NMI on ($4200 = $A1), lets interrupts in (CLI),
 * clears $00 and loops (LDA $00 at $80:8654) until the NMI has set it.
 * Leftovers: A and the flags as they were (PHA / PLA, PHP / PLP).
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_WaitForNMI(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t p = r->p;
  hm_push8(ram, r, p);                                     /* PHP */
  push16(ram, r, r->a);                                    /* REP #$20; PHA */
  set_a8(r, NMI_ON);                                       /* SEP #$20; LDA #$A1 */
  hm_bus_wr8(ram, NMITIMEN, NMI_ON);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, NMI_STATUS) = 0;                          /* CLI; STZ $00 */
  hm_nmi(ram, r, 0x8654, (uint8_t)((p & ~0x06) | 0xA0));
  set_a8(r, *hm_dp(ram, r, NMI_STATUS));                   /* LDA $00: set */
  r->a = pull16(ram, r);                                   /* REP #$20; PLA; PLP */
  flags_back(r, hm_pull8(ram, r));
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * WaitForNMIATimes ($80:865D, JSL, RTL): the same A times (16-bit; 0 would
 * mean 65536). From the second wait on, the carry is 1 (CMP #0).
 * Leftovers: A = 0, the flags as they were (PHP / PLP).
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_WaitForNMIATimes(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t p = r->p, c = p & 1;
  hm_push8(ram, r, p);                                     /* PHP */
  do {
    push16(ram, r, r->a);                                  /* REP #$20; PHA */
    set_a8(r, NMI_ON);
    hm_bus_wr8(ram, NMITIMEN, NMI_ON);
    *hm_dp(ram, r, NMI_STATUS) = 0;
    hm_nmi(ram, r, 0x866C, (uint8_t)((p & ~0x07) | 0xA0 | c));
    set_a8(r, *hm_dp(ram, r, NMI_STATUS));
    r->a = (uint16_t)(pull16(ram, r) - 1);                 /* REP #$20; PLA; DEC A */
    r->c = c = 1;                                          /* CMP #0 */
  } while (r->a);
  flags_back(r, hm_pull8(ram, r));                         /* PLP */
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * ScreenFadeIn ($80:87CE) and ScreenFadeOut ($80:880A) (JSL, RTL): the
 * brightness goes, one level at a time, from $92 (or, if $92 = $FF, from
 * where it is, $25) to $94, up or down, $93 frames per level
 * (SetBrightness, then WaitForNMI $93 times; $26 counts them). At the end
 * bit 15 of $7F1F5A is set (faded in) or cleared (faded out).
 * The flags are followed exactly (`p`), since SetBrightness and
 * WaitForNMI save them (PHP) and the NMI pushes them.
 * Leftovers: A = the new $7F1F5A (16-bit), C = 1, X and Y 8-bit.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
static uint8_t nz8(uint8_t p, uint8_t v) { return (uint8_t)((p & ~0x82) | (v & 0x80) | (v ? 0 : 0x02)); }
static uint8_t lda8(HmRegs *r, uint8_t p, uint8_t v) { set_a8(r, v); return nz8(p, v); }
static uint8_t cmp8(HmRegs *r, uint8_t p, uint8_t a, uint8_t m)
{
  r->c = a >= m;
  return (uint8_t)((nz8(p, (uint8_t)(a - m)) & ~0x01) | r->c);
}
static void call_with_flags(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t p, uint16_t at,
                            void (*fn)(uint8_t *, HmRegs *))
{
  r->p = p;
  hm_jsl(ram, r, (uint16_t)(at + 3), 0x80);
  fn(ram, r);
  hm_rtl(ram, r);
}

static void fade(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, int up)
{
  uint8_t entry = r->p;
  uint8_t p = (uint8_t)(r->p | 0x30);                      /* SEP #$30 */
  r->x &= 0x00FF; r->y &= 0x00FF;
  uint16_t at = up ? 0x87CE : 0x880A;                      /* the routine's start */
  p = lda8(r, p, *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_FROM));
  p = cmp8(r, p, (uint8_t)r->a, 0xFF);
  if ((uint8_t)r->a != 0xFF) {
    p = lda8(r, p, *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_FROM));
    *hm_dp(ram, r, FADE_BRIGHTNESS) = (uint8_t)r->a;
  }
  p = lda8(r, p, *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_FRAMES));
  *hm_dp(ram, r, FADE_FRAME) = (uint8_t)r->a;
  for (;;) {
    p = lda8(r, p, *hm_dp(ram, r, FADE_BRIGHTNESS));
    call_with_flags(ram, r, p, (uint16_t)(at + 0x12), hm_SetBrightness);
    p = lda8(r, p, *hm_dp(ram, r, FADE_BRIGHTNESS));
    p = cmp8(r, p, (uint8_t)r->a, *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_TO));
    if ((uint8_t)r->a == *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_TO)) break;
    uint8_t b = (uint8_t)(*hm_dp(ram, r, FADE_BRIGHTNESS) + (up ? 1 : -1));
    *hm_dp(ram, r, FADE_BRIGHTNESS) = b;                   /* INC / DEC $25 */
    p = nz8(p, b);
    do {
      call_with_flags(ram, r, p, (uint16_t)(at + 0x1E), hm_WaitForNMI);
      uint8_t f = (uint8_t)(*hm_dp(ram, r, FADE_FRAME) - 1);
      *hm_dp(ram, r, FADE_FRAME) = f;                      /* DEC $26; LDA $26 */
      p = lda8(r, p, f);
    } while (*hm_dp(ram, r, FADE_FRAME));
    p = lda8(r, p, *hm_dp(ram, r, HM_FADE_FRAMES));
    *hm_dp(ram, r, FADE_FRAME) = (uint8_t)r->a;
  }
  uint16_t v = hm_bus_rd16(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_FLAGS_5A));   /* REP #$20 */
  v = up ? (uint16_t)(v | 0x8000) : (uint16_t)(v & 0x7FFF);
  r->a = v;
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, WRAM_LONG(HM_FLAGS_5A), v);
  r->n = (uint8_t)(v >> 15);
  r->p = entry;
}
void hm_ScreenFadeIn(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r) { fade(ram, r, 1); }
void hm_ScreenFadeOut(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r) { fade(ram, r, 0); }

```

`src/objects.c`:

```c
/*
 * objects.c — objects with a sprite: the "game objects" the screen is made
 * of (people, animals, the tools' effects...) and the "map objects" the
 * tools leave on the map (cut grass, a splash...).
 *
 * Game objects ("gobj" in HM-Decomp): up to 40 records of $24 bytes at
 * $019C (data bank):
 *   +00 $7777 = in use, 0 = free     +02 sprite number    +04 flip
 *   +06 (copied from $A3)            +08 X                +0A Y
 *   +0C entry of the sprite table    +0E the same + 3
 *   +10 address of the sprite's piece list   +12 a byte of the sprite entry
 *   +13 number of pieces             +14... one byte per piece: the
 *                                           graphics slot it is in ($FF =
 *                                           queued, not loaded yet)
 * Sprites 0-$261 are described in bank $86 (table $86:8080), $262-$44F in
 * bank $87 (table $87:8080). A sprite's piece list is a count and then 5
 * bytes per piece (the first word is the piece's graphics number).
 *
 * Direct page: inputs $9B/$9D position, $9F flip, $A1 sprite, $A3; outputs
 * $A5 record number, $A7 0 = created / $FFFF = no room, $A9 record offset.
 * $DC counts the records handed out so far (it only grows, up to 40).
 *
 * Graphics of the pieces: $7F:0F00 + piece says in which slot (of the
 * sprite graphics in VRAM) it already is, $FF = not loaded; $7E:A320 +
 * 4 slot counts the pieces using the slot. Pieces not loaded go into a ring
 * queue of 64 entries of 4 bytes at $7E:A220 (piece, address of the byte
 * that will receive the slot): $BD is where the next one goes, $BB where
 * the loader (LoadQueuedSpritePieces, run at the NMI) takes them out.
 *
 * Map objects: 10 records of 16 bytes at $7E:B4E6:
 *   +0 flags (bit 0 = in use)   +1 its routine (table $81:A58B)   +2, +3
 *   +4 its game object number   +6 sprite   +8 sprite shown now
 *   +A flip   +C X   +E Y
 * RunItemsOnMap ($81:A383) moves them every frame.
 */
#include "hm_decomp.h"
#include "hm_ram.h"   /* from the recompilation project */
#include "hm_vars.h"
#include "hm_regs.h"

#define SPRITES_86       0x868080   /* ROM: sprite -> its entry, bank $86 */
#define SPRITES_87       0x878080   /* ROM: the same for sprites $262+ */
#define FIRST_SPRITE_87  0x0262
#define PIECE_SLOT       0x7F0F00   /* piece -> graphics slot ($FF = none) */
#define PIECE_QUEUE      0x7EA220   /* 64 x (piece, where to put the slot) */
#define SLOT_USERS       0x7EA320   /* slot * 4 -> how many pieces use it */
#define MAP_OBJECT_SIZE  0x10
#define MAP_OBJECTS_MAX  10

/* A sprite's entry: a list of frames */
#define FRAME_PIECES      0      /* word: the frame's piece list (0 = back to the first) */
#define FRAME_LASTS       2      /* byte: how many frames it lasts */
#define FRAME_SIZE        3
/* A piece in a piece list (after the count byte) */
#define PIECE_DX          2      /* signed byte: its offset across in the sprite */
#define PIECE_DY          3      /* signed byte: its offset down */
#define PIECE_ATTR        4      /* palette (bits 0-2) and flip (bits 4-5) */
#define PIECE_ENTRY_SIZE  5

/* Other tables */
#define GOBJ_OFFSETS     0x858BE0   /* ROM: Table_GameOBJIndexes, object -> record offset */
#define HIGH_X_BITS      0x858BD0   /* ROM: words, the X high bit of each sprite of a high-table word */
#define PIECE_GRAPHICS   0x868000   /* ROM: words, 2 x the index (same table as SLOT_TILES) */
#define SLOT_TILES       0x868000   /* 2 x slot: the slot's first tile */
#define PLAYER_ANIMS     0x81D210   /* ROM: DATA8_81D210, per animation 3 bytes:
                                     * the sprite and the flip / 64 */
#define QUEUE_SLOT_AT    2          /* in a PIECE_QUEUE entry: where to write the slot */
#define SLOT_PIECE       2          /* in a SLOT_USERS entry: the piece loaded in it
                                     * ($FFFF = none) */
#define COPY_BANK        2          /* in a HM_LOAD_COPIES entry: the source's bank */
#define COPY_VRAM        4          /* in a HM_LOAD_COPIES entry: the VRAM address */
#define COPY_SIZE        6
#define OAM_Y_BYTE       1          /* in a sprite's 4 bytes (X is byte 0) */
#define OAM_TILE_BYTE    2
#define OAM_ATTR_BYTE    3

/* Data-bank variables */
#define GOBJ_CLEAR_AT    0x0086     /* DB (absolute, not direct page): the record
                                     * InitializeOBJs is clearing */
#define UNKNOWN_00B7     0x00B7     /* DB (absolute): ClearOAMCopy sets it to 1 */
#define POSTPONED_FREES  0x0740     /* DB: destructions refused (a piece still queued) */
#define QUEUE_LEFT       0x0742     /* DB: entries still in the piece queue */
#define NEW_SLOTS        0x0846     /* DB: slots handed out so far (to $40) */
#define SEARCH_FROM      0x0848     /* DB: where the search for a free slot starts (1-$40) */
#define DRAW_ORDER       0x084C     /* DB: the drawing order, one byte per object */
/* $0901 is HM_ANIM_REQUEST (hm_ram.h): the player's animation */
#define PLAYER_ANIM_SHOWN 0x0903    /* DB: the animation the player's object shows */

/* Direct page. The game object routines' arguments and results: */
#define OBJ_OFFSET       0xA9   /* the record's offset (36 x the number) */
#define OBJ_INDEX        0xAB   /* loops: the number of the object worked on
                                 * (PrepareOAMData: its place in DRAW_ORDER) */
/* The sprite and its pieces: */
#define MAP_OBJ_PTR      0x07   /* long $07-$09: the map object worked on */
#define MAP_OBJ_PTR_BANK 0x09
#define SPRITE_ENTRY     0x75   /* long $75-$77: the sprite's entry / the frame */
#define SPRITE_ENTRY_BANK 0x77
#define PIECE_LIST       0x78   /* long $78-$7A: the piece list / the piece */
#define PIECE_LIST_BANK  0x7A
#define PIECES_LEFT      0xAD   /* pieces still to do */
#define PIECE_NUM        0xB3   /* in: a piece's graphics number; out: its slot
                                 * ($FFFF = queued). ReleaseSpriteSlot: the slot */
#define PIECE_SLOT_AT    0xB5   /* where the piece's slot is to be written */
#define QUEUE_OUT        0xBB   /* PIECE_QUEUE: where the loader takes the next one */
#define QUEUE_IN         0xBD   /* PIECE_QUEUE: where the next one goes */
/* $AF means a different thing in each routine: */
#define SLOT_BYTE_AT     0xAF   /* LoadGameObjectComponents: where the next slot goes */
#define PIECES_QUEUED    0xAF   /* CheckSpritePiecesLoaded: 0 all loaded, $FFFF not */
#define ORDER_BACK       0xAF   /* GetOBJOrderToDraw: the next place from the end */
#define OAM_USED         0xAF   /* PrepareOAMData: bytes of HM_OAM_COPY filled so far */
/* GetOBJOrderToDraw's own uses: */
#define ORDER_PLAYER_Y   0xA9   /* the player's Y (OBJ_OFFSET elsewhere) */
#define ORDER_FRONT      0xAD   /* the next place from the start (PIECES_LEFT elsewhere) */
/* LoadQueuedSpritePieces's own uses: */
#define LOAD_VRAM        0x75   /* the slot's VRAM address */
#define LOAD_SLOT_AT     0x78   /* long $78-$7A: where the slot is written (bank $80) */
#define LOAD_SLOT_AT_BANK 0x7A
#define COPY_AT          0xBF   /* the next free HM_LOAD_COPIES entry (offset) */
#define LOAD_PIECE       0xC1   /* the piece, then its graphics' offset */
#define LOAD_SLOT4       0xC3   /* 4 x the slot, then the graphics' address */
#define LOAD_SLOT        0xC5   /* the slot, then the graphics' bank */
/* PrepareOAMData's own uses: */
#define OAM_PIECE_AT     0x75   /* the piece's byte in GOBJ_PIECE_SLOTS (offset) */
#define SCREEN_X         0xBF   /* the piece's place on the screen */
#define SCREEN_Y         0xC1
#define OAM_HIGH_BITS    0xC3   /* the word of HM_OAM_COPY_HIGH being changed */
#define TEMP_C5          0xC5   /* set to 3, not read here */
#define OAM_PALETTE      0xB1   /* the piece's palette x 2 */
#define OAM_FLIP_BITS    0xB2   /* the piece's flip bits */
/* Scratch: */
#define TEMP_7E          0x7E   /* a temporary (a multiplier, a part of a number...) */
#define TEMP_80          0x80   /* another one (PrepareOAMData) */
/* Others: */
#define NMI_DMA_CHANNELS 0x9A   /* the DMA channels the NMI starts (bit 4 = the OAM) */

static void push16(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint16_t v)
{
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)(v >> 8));
  hm_push8(ram, r, (uint8_t)v);
}
static uint16_t pull16(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t lo = hm_pull8(ram, r);
  return (uint16_t)(lo | hm_pull8(ram, r) << 8);
}
/* `addr,X` with the data bank: may run on into the next bank */
static uint32_t abs_x(const HmRegs *r, uint16_t addr, uint16_t x)
{
  return (((uint32_t)r->db << 16 | addr) + x) & 0xFFFFFF;
}
static uint32_t abs_db(const HmRegs *r, uint16_t addr)
{
  return (uint32_t)r->db << 16 | addr;
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * LoadSpriteComponent ($85:8C30, JSR, RTS; CODE_858C30 in HM-Decomp).
 * $B3 = a piece's graphics number, $B5 = where its slot will be written.
 * Already loaded: one more user of its slot; $B3 = A = Y = the slot.
 * Not loaded: queued for the loader; $B3 = A = $FFFF, X = the queue entry.
 * If the queue is full the original waits ("CMP $BB; BEQ" to itself) for
 * the NMI to empty a place; the rewrite cannot wait (the fuzz never fills
 * the queue).
 * C: in the queue case, the new $BD >= $BB; otherwise 0.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
void hm_LoadSpriteComponent(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint16_t piece = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, PIECE_NUM);
  uint8_t slot = hm_bus_rd8(ram, (PIECE_SLOT + piece) & 0xFFFFFF);
  r->y = slot;
  if (slot != 0xFF) {
    r->x = (uint16_t)(slot << 2);
    uint32_t users = (SLOT_USERS + r->x) & 0xFFFFFF;
    hm_bus_wr16(ram, users, (uint16_t)(hm_bus_rd16(ram, users) + 1));
    r->a = slot;
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, PIECE_NUM, slot);
    r->c = 0;                                            /* CPY #$FF: Y < $FF */
    return;
  }
  uint16_t at = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, QUEUE_IN);
  uint16_t next = (uint16_t)(at + 4);
  if (next == 0x0100) next = 0;                          /* 64 entries, then wrap */
  r->c = next >= hm_dp_r16(ram, r, QUEUE_OUT);           /* the CMP $BB of the wait */
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, QUEUE_IN, next);
  r->x = at;
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, (PIECE_QUEUE + at) & 0xFFFFFF, piece);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, (PIECE_QUEUE + QUEUE_SLOT_AT + at) & 0xFFFFFF, hm_dp_r16(ram, r, PIECE_SLOT_AT));
  r->a = 0xFFFF;
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, PIECE_NUM, 0xFFFF);
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * LoadGameObjectComponents ($85:8AE5, JSR, RTS; CODE_858AE5 in HM-Decomp).
 * For the game object at offset $A9: reads its piece list ($78-$7A = the
 * list, bank $86/$87 already in $7A), stores the count at +13, and loads
 * every piece (LoadSpriteComponent), writing its slot at +14 + n.
 * Leftovers: $AD = 0, $AF = the byte after the last piece, $B3/$B5 of the
 * last piece; A = 0, X = $A9, Y = 1 + 5 pieces, C from the last ADC.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#define RET_AE5_PIECE 0x8B1E   /* JSR LoadSpriteComponent at $85:8B1C */

void hm_LoadGameObjectComponents(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint16_t obj = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, OBJ_OFFSET);
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, PIECE_LIST, hm_bus_rd16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_PIECE_LIST, obj)));
  uint8_t pieces = hm_bus_rd8(ram, hm_dp_long(ram, r, PIECE_LIST, 0));
  *hm_dp(ram, r, PIECES_LEFT) = pieces;
  hm_bus_wr8(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_PIECE_COUNT, obj), pieces);
  *hm_dp(ram, r, PIECES_LEFT + 1) = 0;
  uint16_t first = (uint16_t)(obj + HM_GAME_OBJECTS);    /* CLC; ADC #$019C */
  r->c = (uint32_t)first + GOBJ_PIECE_SLOTS > 0xFFFF;    /* CLC; ADC #$0014 */
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, SLOT_BYTE_AT, (uint16_t)(first + GOBJ_PIECE_SLOTS));

  uint16_t x = obj, y = 1;
  while (hm_dp_r16(ram, r, PIECES_LEFT) != 0) {
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, PIECE_NUM, hm_bus_rd16(ram, hm_dp_long(ram, r, PIECE_LIST, y)));
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, PIECE_SLOT_AT, hm_dp_r16(ram, r, SLOT_BYTE_AT));
    push16(ram, r, x);                                   /* PHX; PHY */
    push16(ram, r, y);
    push16(ram, r, RET_AE5_PIECE);                       /* JSR */
    hm_LoadSpriteComponent(ram, r);
    pull16(ram, r);                                      /* RTS */
    y = pull16(ram, r);                                  /* PLY; PLX */
    x = pull16(ram, r);
    hm_bus_wr8(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_PIECE_SLOTS, x), (uint8_t)hm_dp_r16(ram, r, PIECE_NUM));
    x++;
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, SLOT_BYTE_AT, (uint16_t)(hm_dp_r16(ram, r, SLOT_BYTE_AT) + 1));
    r->c = (uint32_t)y + PIECE_ENTRY_SIZE > 0xFFFF;
    y = (uint16_t)(y + PIECE_ENTRY_SIZE);
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, PIECES_LEFT, (uint16_t)(hm_dp_r16(ram, r, PIECES_LEFT) - 1));
  }
  r->a = 0;
  r->x = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, OBJ_OFFSET);
  r->y = y;
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * CreateGameObject ($85:8000, JSL, RTL; CODE_858000 in HM-Decomp). Takes a
 * free game object (one more of the 40 if not all are handed out yet, then
 * the first free one) and fills it from $A1 (sprite), $9F, $A3, $9B/$9D;
 * looks up the sprite's entry and loads its pieces.
 * $A7 = 0 and $A5 / $A9 = the object; or $A7 = $FFFF if none is free.
 * Leftovers: $75 the sprite's entry, $77 / $7A its bank. Created: as
 * LoadGameObjectComponents, then A = 0. No room: A = $FFFF, X = $24 n,
 * Y = n (n = $DC), C = 1.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#define RET_8000_PIECES 0x80B0   /* JSR LoadGameObjectComponents at $85:80AE */

void hm_CreateGameObject(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint16_t sprite = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_SPRITE);
  uint8_t bank = sprite >= FIRST_SPRITE_87 ? 0x87 : 0x86;
  *hm_dp(ram, r, SPRITE_ENTRY_BANK) = bank;
  *hm_dp(ram, r, PIECE_LIST_BANK) = bank;

  uint16_t handed_out = hm_dp_r16(ram, r, HM_GOBJ_COUNT);
  if (handed_out != GOBJ_MAX) {
    handed_out++;
    hm_dp_w16(ram, r, HM_GOBJ_COUNT, handed_out);
  }
  uint16_t x = 0, y = 0;
  while (hm_bus_rd16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS, x)) != 0) {
    x = (uint16_t)(x + GOBJ_SIZE);
    y++;
    if (y == hm_dp_r16(ram, r, HM_GOBJ_COUNT)) {         /* none free */
      r->c = 1;                                          /* CPY: equal */
      r->a = 0xFFFF;
      hm_dp_w16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_RESULT, 0xFFFF);
      r->x = x; r->y = y;
      return;
    }
  }

  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_NUMBER, y);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_STATUS, x), GOBJ_IN_USE);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_SPRITE, x), sprite);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_FLIP, x), hm_dp_r16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_FLIP));
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_PARAM, x), hm_dp_r16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_PARAM));
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_X, x), hm_dp_r16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_X));
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_Y, x), hm_dp_r16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_Y));
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, OBJ_OFFSET, x);

  uint16_t number = hm_bus_rd16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_SPRITE, x));
  uint32_t table = SPRITES_86;
  if (hm_dp_r16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_SPRITE) >= FIRST_SPRITE_87) {
    number = (uint16_t)(number - FIRST_SPRITE_87);
    table = SPRITES_87;
  }
  uint16_t entry = hm_bus_rd16(ram, (table + (uint16_t)(number << 1)) & 0xFFFFFF);
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, SPRITE_ENTRY, entry);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_FIRST_FRAME, x), entry);
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_NEXT_FRAME, x), (uint16_t)(entry + FRAME_SIZE));
  hm_bus_wr16(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_PIECE_LIST, x), hm_bus_rd16(ram, hm_dp_long(ram, r, SPRITE_ENTRY, FRAME_PIECES)));
  hm_bus_wr8(ram, abs_x(r, HM_GAME_OBJECTS + GOBJ_TIMER, x), hm_bus_rd8(ram, hm_dp_long(ram, r, SPRITE_ENTRY, FRAME_LASTS)));

  r->x = x; r->y = 2;
  push16(ram, r, RET_8000_PIECES);                       /* JSR */
  hm_LoadGameObjectComponents(ram, r);
  pull16(ram, r);                                        /* RTS */
  r->a = 0;
  hm_dp_w16(ram, r, HM_OBJ_RESULT, 0);
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * SpawnMapObject ($81:A500, JSL, RTL; CODE_81A500 in HM-Decomp). Takes the
 * first free map object ($07-$09 = it) and fills it from $0974-$0976,
```
