```c
  uint8_t weather = ram[HM_WEATHER_TOMORROW];
  uint8_t season = ram[HM_SEASON];
  hm_wr16(ram, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS, 0);
  r->a = weather;                                /* LDA #0; XBA; LDA weather */
  r->c = 1;                                      /* CMP #n with weather >= n */

  switch (weather) {
  case HM_WEATHER_SUNNY:
    r->a = season;
    r->c = season >= SUMMER;
    if (season == SUMMER) {                      /* no LDX here: X untouched */
      r->a = kWeatherFlagTable[0];
      hm_wr16(ram, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS, r->a);
    }
    break;
  case HM_WEATHER_RAIN:
    r->c = season >= WINTER;
    set_weather_flag(ram, r, season == WINTER ? 2 : 1);
    break;
  case HM_WEATHER_SNOW:
    set_weather_flag(ram, r, season == SPRING ? 1 : 2);
    break;
  case HM_WEATHER_HURRICANE:
    set_weather_flag(ram, r, 3);
    break;
  case HM_WEATHER_FAIR_STORY:
    set_weather_flag(ram, r, 4);
    mark_story_storm(ram, r, 0x0002, 0x0100);
    break;
  case HM_WEATHER_THUNDER:
    set_weather_flag(ram, r, 5);
    mark_story_storm(ram, r, 0x0001, 0x0080);
    break;
  default:                                       /* festivals: no flag */
    break;
  }
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * WeatherTomorrow ($82:8CF9, JSL, RTL). Runs at night with TODAY's date.
 *
 * 1. Festival eves: tomorrow is the festival.
 *      Spring 22 -> flower festival      Fall 11   -> harvest festival
 *      Fall 19   -> egg festival         Winter 9  -> thanksgiving
 *      Winter 23 -> star night           Winter 30 -> new year
 * 2. First year only, once each:
 *      Winter: guaranteed storm on day 8 (decided on the 7th), before that
 *              1 chance in 8 every night.          (code 4, flag 64 bit 1)
 *      Summer: guaranteed storm on day 30 (decided on the 29th), before
 *              that 1 chance in 30 every night.    (code 5, flag 64 bit 0)
 * 3. Summer hurricane (any year, not decided on day 30): 1 in 30, or
 *    1 in 60 if the player has the turtle shell.
 * 4. Rain: 1 in 6 in spring, 1 in 10 in summer and fall, never in winter.
 * 5. Snow (only winter): 1 in 3.
 * 6. Otherwise sunny.
 * "1 in n" is RNGReturn0toA(n) == 0, which is slightly more likely than
 * 1/n (see rng.c).
 *
 * Quirks: the first-year winter storm is checked on any winter night that
 * is not a festival eve, but the guaranteed one only on day 7; on the 29th
 * of summer the summer storm skips the dice. A season above 3 (never
 * happens) reads past the chance tables, here as in the original.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
/* The chance tables, one byte per season, read from the ROM (a season
 * above 3, which the game never has, reads on past them, as the
 * original does) */
#define kHurricaneChance 0x828EB2u   /* 0, 30, 0, 0 */
#define kRainChance      0x828EB6u   /* 6, 10, 10, 0 */
#define kSnowChance      0x828EBAu   /* 0, 0, 0, 3 */
#define kThunderChance   0x828EBEu   /* 0, 30, 0, 0 */
#define kSnowstormChance 0x828EC2u   /* 0, 0, 0, 8 */
static uint8_t chance(uint8_t *ram, uint32_t table, uint8_t season) { return hm_bus_rd8(ram, table + season); }

/* Where each JSL RNGReturn0toA returns to (its frame stays on the stack). */
#define RET_SNOWSTORM  0x8DCD
#define RET_THUNDER    0x8E11
#define RET_HURRICANE  0x8E58
#define RET_RAIN       0x8E7B
#define RET_SNOW       0x8E9E

/* JSL RNGReturn0toA with `faces` in A; true when it rolled 0. */
static bool roll_zero(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t faces, uint16_t ret)
{
  r->a = faces;
  hm_jsl(ram, r, ret, 0x80);                     /* JSL.L $80:89F9 */
  hm_RNGReturn0toA(ram, r);
  hm_rtl(ram, r);
  return r->a == 0;
}

/* "1 chance in table[season]": LDA #0; XBA; LDA season; TAX; LDA table,X */
static bool one_in(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint32_t table, uint16_t ret)
{
  uint8_t season = ram[HM_SEASON];
  r->x = season;
  uint8_t n = chance(ram, table, season);
  r->a = n;
  if (n == 0)
    return false;
  return roll_zero(ram, r, n, ret);
}

static void set_weather(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t code, uint16_t a)
{
  ram[HM_WEATHER_TOMORROW] = code;
  r->a = a;
}

/* Festival eves keep A's high byte from the caller (8-bit LDA #code). */
static void set_festival(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r, uint8_t code)
{
  set_weather(ram, r, code, (uint16_t)((r->a & 0xFF00) | code));
  r->c = 1;                                      /* CMP #day matched */
}

static void normal_day(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  if (one_in(ram, r, kRainChance, RET_RAIN))
    set_weather(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_RAIN, HM_WEATHER_RAIN);
  else if (one_in(ram, r, kSnowChance, RET_SNOW))
    set_weather(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_SNOW, HM_WEATHER_SNOW);
  else
    set_weather(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_SUNNY, HM_WEATHER_SUNNY);
}

static void summer_night(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t day = ram[HM_DAY];
  r->c = 0;                                      /* CMP #3 with season 1 */

  /* First-year summer storm. */
  if (ram[HM_YEAR] == 0 && !(hm_rd16(ram, HM_FLAGS_64) & 0x0001)) {
    r->c = day >= 29;
    if (day == 29) {
      set_weather(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_THUNDER, HM_WEATHER_THUNDER);
      return;
    }
    if (one_in(ram, r, kThunderChance, RET_THUNDER)) {
      set_weather(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_THUNDER, HM_WEATHER_THUNDER);
      return;
    }
  }

  /* Hurricane: not decided on the last day of summer. */
  r->c = day >= 30;
  if (day == 30) {
    normal_day(ram, r);
    return;
  }
  uint8_t season = ram[HM_SEASON];
  r->x = season;
  r->a = chance(ram, kHurricaneChance, season);
  if (chance(ram, kHurricaneChance, season) != 0) {
    uint16_t faces = chance(ram, kHurricaneChance, season);
    if (hm_rd16(ram, HM_FLAGS_6C) & HAS_TURTLE_SHELL)
      faces = (uint16_t)(faces << 1);            /* the shell halves the chance */
    r->y = faces;
    if (roll_zero(ram, r, (uint8_t)faces, RET_HURRICANE)) {
      set_weather(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_HURRICANE, HM_WEATHER_HURRICANE);
      return;
    }
  }
  normal_day(ram, r);
}

static void winter_night(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t day = ram[HM_DAY];
  if (day == 9)  { set_festival(ram, r, WEATHER_THANKSGIVING); return; }
  if (day == 23) { set_festival(ram, r, WEATHER_STAR_NIGHT); return; }
  if (day == 30) { set_festival(ram, r, WEATHER_NEW_YEAR); return; }
  r->c = day >= 30;

  /* First-year winter storm. */
  if (ram[HM_YEAR] == 0 && !(hm_rd16(ram, HM_FLAGS_64) & 0x0002)) {
    r->c = day >= 7;
    if (day == 7) {
      set_weather(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_FAIR_STORY, HM_WEATHER_FAIR_STORY);
      return;
    }
    if (one_in(ram, r, kSnowstormChance, RET_SNOWSTORM)) {
      set_weather(ram, r, HM_WEATHER_FAIR_STORY, HM_WEATHER_FAIR_STORY);
      return;
    }
  }
  normal_day(ram, r);
}

void hm_WeatherTomorrow(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  uint8_t season = ram[HM_SEASON], day = ram[HM_DAY];

  switch (season) {
  case SPRING:
    r->c = day >= 22;
    if (day == 22) set_festival(ram, r, WEATHER_FLOWER_FESTIVAL);
    else normal_day(ram, r);
    return;
  case FALL:
    if (day == 11) { set_festival(ram, r, WEATHER_HARVEST_FESTIVAL); return; }
    r->c = day >= 19;
    if (day == 19) { set_festival(ram, r, WEATHER_EGG_FESTIVAL); return; }
    normal_day(ram, r);
    return;
  case WINTER:
    winter_night(ram, r);
    return;
  default:
    summer_night(ram, r);
    return;
  }
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * TvWeatherForecast ($82:81C0, JSL, RTL): the TV weather report. $0990 = what the
 * forecast shows (the TV code at $81:D9xx picks the text with it and the
 * season): table $82:81FD maps tomorrow's code (0-3 as they are, the two
 * scripted storms as 0, festivals 6..0B as 5..0A), then a hurricane day
 * shows 0B and the winter storm 4 (from today's flags $0196).
 * The table is read as the game does, even past its 12 entries.
 * Leftovers: X = tomorrow's code; A = 0, or the value just stored;
 * C untouched.
 * ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
#define TV_FORECAST_MAP  0x8281FD   /* ROM: tomorrow's code -> the forecast */

void hm_TvWeatherForecast(uint8_t *ram, HmRegs *r)
{
  r->x = ram[HM_WEATHER_TOMORROW];
  ram[HM_TV_FORECAST] = hm_bus_rd8(ram, TV_FORECAST_MAP + r->x);
  uint16_t flags = hm_rd16(ram, HM_WEATHER_FLAGS);
  if (flags & 0x0010) {
    ram[HM_TV_FORECAST] = 0x0B;
    r->a = 0x000B;
  } else if (flags & 0x0200) {
    ram[HM_TV_FORECAST] = 0x04;
    r->a = 0x0204;
  } else {
    r->a = 0;
  }
}
```

`tools/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the decompilation's test executable.
#
#   tools/build.sh [--rom /path/to/rom.sfc]
#
# The decompilation does not have its own copy of the game: it builds the
# RECOMPILATION project (../HarvestMoonSNESRecomp, or HM_RECOMP=...) with
#   1. its own copy of the generated code (build/gen), produced from your ROM
#      with the recompilation's configuration,
#   2. the HM-Decomp names and the check wrappers applied to that copy
#      (tools/decomp_overrides.py),
#   3. the rewritten routines in src/ compiled in (HM_EXTRA_SOURCES).
# The recompilation project's own files are never modified.
#
# Result: build/game/HarvestMoonSNESRecomp(.exe). It plays exactly like the
# normal game; HM_DECOMP_CHECK=1 / HM_DECOMP_FUZZ=... turn the checks on.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
RECOMP="$(cd "${HM_RECOMP:-$ROOT/../HarvestMoonSNESRecomp}" && pwd)"
PYTHON=${PYTHON:-python3}
ROM=""
EXTRA_CMAKE=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --rom) ROM=$2; shift 2 ;;
    -D*) EXTRA_CMAKE+=("$1"); shift ;;
    *) echo "build.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
CLI="$RECOMP/snesrecomp/snesrecomp_cli.py"
B="$ROOT/build"
mkdir -p "$B"
export RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=${RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN:-stable}

RESOLVE=(resolve-rom --project-root "$RECOMP" --name rom.sfc --name harvestmoon.sfc --name harvestmoon.smc)
[ -n "$ROM" ] && RESOLVE+=(--rom "$ROM")
ROM=$("$PYTHON" "$CLI" "${RESOLVE[@]}"); ROM=${ROM%$'\r'}
IDENT="$RECOMP/snesrecomp/tools/rom_identity.py"
CRC=$("$PYTHON" "$IDENT" "$RECOMP/rom_identity.txt" --get expected_crc32)
SHA=$("$PYTHON" "$IDENT" "$RECOMP/rom_identity.txt" --get expected_sha256)

echo "== 1/3 Generating code from $ROM (recompilation config) =="
GEN_ARGS=(--rom "$ROM" --cfg-dir "$RECOMP/recomp" --out-dir "$B/gen" --funcs-h "$B/funcs.h"
          --project-root "$RECOMP" --expected-crc32 "$CRC" --expected-sha256 "$SHA")
for p in "$RECOMP"/recomp/profiles/*.json "$RECOMP"/recomp/profiles/*.jsonl; do
  [ -f "$p" ] && GEN_ARGS+=(--profile-manifest "$p")
done
rm -f "$B/gen/.snesrecomp-cache.json"
"$PYTHON" "$CLI" generate "${GEN_ARGS[@]}" | grep -E "analysis:|v2_emit: [0-9]+ roots|postprocess|apply_overrides|error" || true
# The generated files `#include "funcs.h"`; next to them it is found first,
# before any (possibly stale) copy in the recompilation's src/.
cp "$B/funcs.h" "$B/gen/funcs.h"

echo "== 2/3 Names and check wrappers =="
"$PYTHON" "$ROOT/tools/decomp_overrides.py" --gen-dir "$B/gen" \
  --names "$ROOT/data/decomp_names.tsv" --decomp "$ROOT/src/hm_decomp.c"

echo "== 3/3 Building the test executable =="
SOURCES=$(ls "$ROOT"/src/*.c | tr '\n' ';')
cmake -S "$RECOMP" -B "$B/game" -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DHM_GEN_DIR="$B/gen" -DHM_EXTRA_SOURCES="$SOURCES" \
  -DHM_EXTRA_INCLUDE_DIRS="$RECOMP/src;$ROOT/src" "${EXTRA_CMAKE[@]}" >/dev/null
cmake --build "$B/game" | tail -1
echo "Done: $B/game"

```

`tools/calls.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""List the JSR / JSL call sites of a routine, with their return addresses.

    python3 tools/calls.py --rom rom.sfc 82:9328 [82:9460 ...] [--m 1 --x 0]

A linear disassembly from the entry (LoROM, no copier header or with one),
following REP / SEP to know the width of immediates, until the first
RTS / RTL / RTI that is not followed by more code of the routine (pass
--end to give the end address explicitly). The return address a JSR / JSL
pushes is the address of its own last byte, which is what the rewrites
pass to hm_jsl / push for the frame (never computed by hand).
"""
import argparse
import sys

def length(op, m, x):
    """Total length in bytes of the instruction `op` (m / x = 1: 8-bit)."""
    hi, lo = op >> 4, op & 0xF
    if lo == 0:
        if hi & 1:
            return 2                                   # branches
        return {0x0: 2, 0x2: 3, 0x4: 1, 0x6: 1, 0x8: 2}.get(hi, 2 if x else 3)
    if lo == 2:
        return {0x2: 4, 0x6: 3, 0x8: 3}.get(hi, 2 if hi != 0xA else (2 if x else 3))
    if lo in (1, 3, 5, 6, 7):
        return 2
    if lo == 4:
        return 3 if op in (0x44, 0x54, 0xF4) else 2
    if lo in (8, 0xA, 0xB):
        return 1
    if lo == 9:
        return 3 if hi & 1 else (2 if m else 3)
    if lo == 0xC:
        return 4 if op == 0x5C else 3
    if lo in (0xD, 0xE):
        return 3
    return 4                                           # lo == F: long


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--rom", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--m", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--x", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--end", default=None, help="bank:addr where to stop")
    ap.add_argument("entries", nargs="+")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    rom = open(a.rom, "rb").read()
    if len(rom) % 0x8000 == 512:
        rom = rom[512:]

    def rd(addr):
        return rom[((addr >> 16) & 0x3F) << 15 | (addr & 0x7FFF)]

    def parse(s):
        b, ad = s.split(":")
        return int(b, 16) << 16 | int(ad, 16)

    for e in a.entries:
        pc = parse(e)
        end = parse(a.end) if a.end else None
        m, x = a.m, a.x
        print(f"{e}:")
        while True:
            op = rd(pc)
            n = length(op, m, x)
            if op == 0xC2:      # REP
                v = rd(pc + 1); m = 0 if v & 0x20 else m; x = 0 if v & 0x10 else x
            elif op == 0xE2:    # SEP
                v = rd(pc + 1); m = 1 if v & 0x20 else m; x = 1 if v & 0x10 else x
            if op in (0x20, 0xFC):   # JSR abs / JSR (abs,X)
                t = rd(pc + 1) | rd(pc + 2) << 8
                kind = "JSR" if op == 0x20 else "JSR (,X)"
                print(f"  {pc >> 16:02X}:{pc & 0xFFFF:04X} {kind} {pc >> 16:02X}:{t:04X}  ret {(pc + 2) & 0xFFFF:04X}")
            elif op == 0x22:
                t = rd(pc + 1) | rd(pc + 2) << 8 | rd(pc + 3) << 16
                print(f"  {pc >> 16:02X}:{pc & 0xFFFF:04X} JSL {t >> 16:02X}:{t & 0xFFFF:04X}  ret {(pc + 3) & 0xFFFF:04X}")
            pc += n
            if end is not None:
                if pc >= end:
                    break
            elif op in (0x60, 0x6B, 0x40):
                break
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

`tools/candidates.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Which routines to decompile next.

    python3 tools/candidates.py --decomp ../HM-Decomp [-n 40]

For every routine of HM-Decomp not yet registered in src/hm_decomp.c, lists
its size (instructions, as tools/progress.py counts them), the routines it
calls (JSL / JSR to a label) that are still to do, and whether it touches
hardware registers ($21xx PPU / APU, $42xx, $43xx DMA) or waits for the
NMI, which the checker cannot compare. The "ready" ones (every callee
done, no hardware) come first, biggest first.
"""
import argparse
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import progress  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CALL = re.compile(r"\bJS[LR](?:\.[LW])?\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)")
HW = re.compile(r"\$(?:21[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}|42[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}|43[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})\b|!APUIO|!(?:INI|NMI|HDMA|MDMA|VMAIN|VMADD|CGADD|OAMADD|INIDISP)|WaitForNMI")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--decomp", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "..", "HM-Decomp"))
    ap.add_argument("-n", type=int, default=40)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    found, lines = progress.parse(a.decomp)
    all_r = progress.routines(a.decomp)
    done = progress.registered(os.path.join(ROOT, "src", "hm_decomp.c"))
    done_names = set(done.values())
    # names of everything (HM-Decomp label -> key) and the code of each block
    name_of = {k: n for k, (n, _) in found.items()}
    label_key = {n: k for k, n in name_of.items()}
    for pc, (label, name, *_) in progress.LOCAL.items():
        label_key[label.lstrip(".")] = pc
        label_key[name] = pc
    code = {}
    for rows in lines.values():
        for owner, c in rows:
            if owner is not None:
                code.setdefault(owner, []).append(c)

    def is_done(callee):
        k = label_key.get(callee)
        return callee in done_names or (k is not None and k in done)

    rows = []
    for k, (name, n) in all_r.items():
        if k in done:
            continue
        text = "\n".join(code.get(k, []))
        callees = sorted({c for c in CALL.findall(text) if not c.startswith(".")})
        todo = [c for c in callees if not is_done(c) and c != name]
        hw = bool(HW.search(text))
        rows.append((not todo and not hw, n, name, k, todo, hw))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (not r[0], -r[1]))
    for ready, n, name, k, todo, hw in rows[: a.n]:
        where = f"{k:06X}" if isinstance(k, int) else "------"
        flags = ("ready" if ready else "") + (" HW" if hw else "")
        print(f"{where} {n:5d} {name:32s} {flags:6s} {' '.join(todo[:6])}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/check.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the decompilation checks headlessly.
#
#   tools/check.sh [iterations] [seeds]
#
# 1. Fuzz: from frame 1500 of the attract demo, one rewritten routine per
#    frame is called <iterations> times (default 2000) with random inputs;
#    each call is compared with the original byte for byte, then the machine
#    is restored.
#    Repeated with <seeds> different random seeds (default 3).
# 2. Live: a new game is played by script with every real call checked.
# 3. Nights: the same new game, then ten nights forced (poke 0973 02) on
#    chosen dates (festival eves, first-year storm days...), checked live.
# Exits non-zero on any mismatch.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
GAME="$ROOT/build/game"
N=${1:-2000}
SEEDS=${2:-3}
OUT="$ROOT/build/check"; rm -rf "$OUT"; mkdir -p "$OUT"
EXE="$GAME/HarvestMoonSNESRecomp"; [ -x "$EXE" ] || EXE="$EXE.exe"
# HM_ROM=/path/rom.sfc passes the ROM explicitly (otherwise the game uses the
# ROM it remembers from a previous run, rom.cfg).
ROMARG=(); [ -n "${HM_ROM:-}" ] && ROMARG=(--rom "$(cd "$(dirname "$HM_ROM")" && pwd)/$(basename "$HM_ROM")")
run() {  # name script env...
  local name=$1 script=$2; shift 2
  (cd "$GAME" && env "$@" SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy SNESRECOMP_NO_LAUNCHER=1 \
     "$EXE" "${ROMARG[@]}" --no-launcher --script "$script" > "$OUT/$name.log" 2>&1) || true
  echo "-- $name"; grep "^\[decomp-check\]  \|MISMATCH" "$OUT/$name.log" || echo "(no report: see $OUT/$name.log)"
}
for s in $(seq 1 "$SEEDS"); do
  run fuzz$s "$ROOT/scripts/demo.txt" HM_DECOMP_FUZZ=1500:$N HM_DECOMP_FUZZ_SEED=$s
done
run live "$ROOT/scripts/newgame.txt" HM_DECOMP_CHECK=1
run nights "$ROOT/scripts/nights.txt" HM_DECOMP_CHECK=1
! grep -q "MISMATCH=[1-9]\|MISMATCH " "$OUT"/*.log

```

`tools/decomp_overrides.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the recompilation's generated C into the decompilation's test build.

    python3 tools/decomp_overrides.py --gen-dir build/gen \
        --names data/decomp_names.tsv --decomp src/hm_decomp.c

Runs on a COPY of the generated code (build/gen), never on the
recompilation project's own src/gen.

1. Names. Every compiled routine that HM-Decomp names is renamed from
   `bank_BB_AAAA_MmXx` to `Name_MmXx` (data/decomp_names.tsv, written by
   tools/import_decomp_names.py). Identifiers only: the program is unchanged.

2. Checks. Every routine registered in src/hm_decomp.c gets a wrapper: its
   compiled body is renamed `Name_MmXx__rom` and a new `Name_MmXx` calls it,
   and with HM_DECOMP_CHECK=1 (or during HM_DECOMP_FUZZ) also runs the
   hand-written rewrite on a snapshot and compares (src/hm_decomp.h).
"""
import argparse
import glob
import os
import re
import sys

FUNC_ID = re.compile(r"\bbank_([0-9a-f]{2})_([0-9A-F]{4})_(M[01]X[01])\b")


def load_names(path):
    names = {}
    if path and os.path.exists(path):
        for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):
            line = line.strip()
            if line and not line.startswith("#"):
                pc, name = line.split("\t")
                names[int(pc, 16)] = name
    return names


def rename(gen_dir, names):
    if not names:
        return 0
    def sub(m):
        name = names.get(int(m.group(1), 16) << 16 | int(m.group(2), 16))
        return f"{name}_{m.group(3)}" if name else m.group(0)
    count = 0
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(gen_dir, "*.c")) + glob.glob(os.path.join(gen_dir, "*.h"))):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            text = f.read()
        new = FUNC_ID.sub(sub, text)
        if new != text:
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(new)
            count += 1
    return count


WRAP_DECL = """
/* hm decomp wrappers (tools/apply_overrides.py) */
extern int g_hm_decomp_check;
extern int g_hm_wait_sim;
int hm_decomp_wait_interp(struct CpuState *cpu, const char *name, RecompReturn *ret);
void *hm_decomp_check_begin(const struct CpuState *cpu, const char *name);
void hm_decomp_check_end(const char *name, void *snapshot, const struct CpuState *cpu, int completed);
"""
WRAPPER = """
RecompReturn {fn}(CpuState *cpu) {{
  RecompReturn _w;
  if (g_hm_wait_sim && hm_decomp_wait_interp(cpu, "{name}", &_w)) return _w;
  if (!g_hm_decomp_check) return {fn}__rom(cpu);
  void *_snap = hm_decomp_check_begin(cpu, "{name}");
  RecompReturn _r = {fn}__rom(cpu);
  hm_decomp_check_end("{name}", _snap, cpu, _r == RECOMP_RETURN_NORMAL);
  return _r;
}}
"""


def decomp_registry(path):
    if not path or not os.path.exists(path):
        return []
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    # Entries flagged HM_INTERP have no compiled body at their address (the
    # fuzzer runs them in the interpreter; see src/hm_decomp.h), but the game
    # may still run a compiled copy from the bank $00-$3F mirror (Name_lo):
    # those are wrapped too, so live calls are checked.
    return [(name, "HM_INTERP" in flags) for name, flags in
            re.findall(r'\{\s*"([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)",\s*hm_\w+,\s*([^,]*),', text)]


def wrap(gen_dir, routines):
    wrapped = 0
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(gen_dir, "bank*_v2.c"))):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            text = f.read()
        if "__rom(CpuState *cpu)" in text:
            continue                                    # already wrapped
        tail = []
        for name, _ in routines:
            pat = re.compile(r"^RecompReturn ((?:%s|%s_lo)_M[01]X[01])\(CpuState \*cpu\) \{" % (name, name), re.M)
            for fn in sorted(set(pat.findall(text))):
                text = text.replace("RecompReturn %s(CpuState *cpu) {" % fn,
                                    "RecompReturn %s__rom(CpuState *cpu) {" % fn, 1)
                text = text.replace('#include "funcs.h"\n',
                                    '#include "funcs.h"\nRecompReturn %s__rom(CpuState *cpu);\n' % fn, 1)
                tail.append(WRAPPER.format(fn=fn, name=name))
                wrapped += 1
        if tail:
            text = text.replace('#include "funcs.h"\n', '#include "funcs.h"\n' + WRAP_DECL, 1)
            text += "".join(tail)
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(text)
    return wrapped


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--gen-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--names", required=True, help="data/decomp_names.tsv")
    ap.add_argument("--decomp", required=True, help="src/hm_decomp.c (registry)")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    names = load_names(args.names)
    n = rename(args.gen_dir, names)
    print("decomp_overrides: %d names applied in %d files" % (len(names), n))
    routines = decomp_registry(args.decomp)
    w = wrap(args.gen_dir, routines)
    print("decomp_overrides: %d rewritten routines, %d compiled variants wrapped" % (len(routines), w))
    missing = [r for r, interp in routines if not interp and r not in names.values()]
    if missing:
        print("decomp_overrides: rewritten routines with no compiled body: %s" % ", ".join(missing),
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/import_decomp_names.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Name the recompiled functions after the HM-Decomp disassembly.

    python3 tools/import_decomp_names.py --decomp ../HM-Decomp --gen build/gen

Reads every routine label with an address comment in HM-Decomp's code banks
(`GetRNG: ;838138`) and, for each one the recompiler compiles ahead of time
(a `bank_BB_AAAA_MmXx` body exists in the generated code), writes
`BBAAAA<TAB>Name` to data/decomp_names.tsv. tools/decomp_overrides.py then
renames those functions in the decompilation's copy of the generated C, so
it reads `GetRNG_M1X0` instead of `bank_83_8138_M1X0`.

This is a rename of C identifiers and nothing else. Declaring the names to
the analyzer instead (symbols.toml func roots) was tried and rejected: the
extra function boundaries changed how 31 bodies were split and moved work
between frames. The rename leaves the program byte-for-byte the same.

HM-Decomp addresses are in the FastROM mirror ($80-$87); the game also runs
code from the $00-$07 mirror, which the recompiler compiles separately. Those
copies get the same name with a `_lo` suffix.
"""

import glob
import os
import re
import sys

LABEL = re.compile(r"^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*):\s*;\s*([0-9A-Fa-f]{6})\b", re.M)
# Every compiled body announces itself; works before and after the rename.
BODY = re.compile(r'cpu_trace_func_entry\(cpu, 0x([0-9a-fA-F]{6}), "[A-Za-z_0-9]*_M([01])X([01])"\)')


# Routines HM-Decomp only has as a local label inside another routine (so

MANUAL = {

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--decomp", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--gen", default="build/gen")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/decomp_names.tsv")
    ap.add_argument("--skip-prefix", default="CODE_",
                    help="comma list of label prefixes that are not routines")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    labels = {}
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(a.decomp, "src", "code_banks", "*.asm"))):
        for m in LABEL.finditer(open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()):
            name, pc = m.group(1), int(m.group(2), 16)
            if any(name.startswith(p) for p in a.skip_prefix.split(",") if p):
                continue
            labels.setdefault(pc, name)

    for pc, name in MANUAL.items():
        labels[pc] = name           # our name wins (HM-Decomp may have a placeholder)

    variants = {}          # pc24 -> sorted list of (m, x)
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(a.gen, "bank*_v2.c")):
        for m in BODY.finditer(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()):
            variants.setdefault(int(m.group(1), 16), set()).add((int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))))

    taken = set()
    rows = []
    for pc, name in sorted(labels.items()):
        hi = pc | 0x800000
        for bank_pc, cname in ((hi, name), (hi & 0x7FFFFF, name + "_lo")):
            if bank_pc not in variants or cname in taken:
                continue
            taken.add(cname)
            rows.append(f"{bank_pc:06X}\t{cname}")
    with open(a.out, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        f.write("# pc24<TAB>name -- generated by tools/import_decomp_names.py from HM-Decomp labels\n")
        f.write("\n".join(rows) + "\n")
    named = len(rows)
    print(f"import_decomp_names: {len(labels)} decomp labels, {named} compiled routines named")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/progress.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""How much of the game is decompiled.

    python3 tools/progress.py --decomp ../HM-Decomp [--update-readme]

Measures against the HM-Decomp disassembly (no ROM needed, so anyone can
recompute it):

  * Routines: every top-level label in HM-Decomp's code banks whose body has
    instructions: the ones with an address comment (`GetRNG: ;838138`) and
    the ones without (`CODE_81A500:`). Data tables (`db`/`dw`/`dl` only)
    are not counted.
  * Instructions: the 65816 instructions inside them (one per line of the
    disassembly, labelled or not). This is the headline percentage: a
    4096-tile loop weighs more than a three-line helper.

A routine counts as decompiled when it is registered in src/hm_decomp.c
(written in C and verified against the original).

With --update-readme the block between <!-- progress --> and
<!-- /progress --> in README.md (English) and README.es.md (Spanish) is
rewritten.
"""
import argparse
import glob
import os
import re
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
LABEL = re.compile(r"^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*):\s*;\s*([0-9A-Fa-f]{6})\b")
ANY_TOP_LABEL = re.compile(r"^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*):")
# An instruction: a mnemonic (3 letters, optional .B/.W/.L) or a %Set8bit /
# %Set16bit macro (one REP/SEP each), maybe after a label on the same line.
INSN = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-+]\s+)?(?:\.?[A-Za-z0-9_]+:\s*)?"
                  r"(?:([A-Z]{3})(?:\.[BWL])?\b|%Set(?:8|16)bit)")
DATA = {"DB", "DW", "DL", "DD"}

# Routines HM-Decomp only has as a label inside a bigger block (a local
# `.label`, an indented `CODE_xxxxxx:`, or a top-level label with no
# address comment). Each counts as a routine of its own, from its label to
# the first RTL/RTS, and those instructions are taken out of the block it is
# written in, so nothing is counted twice. Same list as MANUAL in
# tools/import_decomp_names.py.

    0x80D934: ("SUB_80D934", "SUB_80D934"),
    0x80D96B: ("SUB_80D96B", "SUB_80D96B"),
    0x80D9A2: ("SUB_80D9A2", "SUB_80D9A2"),
    0x80D9D9: ("SUB_80D9D9", "SUB_80D9D9"),
    0x80DA10: ("SUB_80DA10", "SUB_80DA10"),
    0x80DA47: ("SUB_80DA47", "SUB_80DA47"),
    0x80DAB4: ("SUB_80DAB4", "SUB_80DAB4"),
    0x80DB06: ("SUB_80DB06", "SUB_80DB06"),
    0x80DC30: ("SUB_80DC30", "SUB_80DC30"),
    0x80DD09: ("SUB_80DD09", "SUB_80DD09"),
    0x84BC9C: ("@84BC9C", "Event_Cmd51", "@84BD44"),
    0x84BD44: ("@84BD44", "Event_Cmd52", "@84BE0D"),
    0x84BE0D: ("@84BE0D", "Event_Cmd53", "@84BED6"),
    0x84BED6: ("@84BED6", "Event_Cmd54", "@84BF20"),
    0x84BF20: ("@84BF20", "Event_Cmd55", "@84BF81"),
    0x84BF81: ("@84BF81", "Event_Cmd56", "@84BFA0"),
    0x84BFA0: ("@84BFA0", "Event_Cmd57", "@84BFBF"),
    0x84BFBF: ("@84BFBF", "Event_Cmd58", "@84C000"),
    0x84C000: ("@84C000", "Event_Cmd59", "@84C014"),
    0x829999: ("ToolUsedCornSeeds", "ToolUsedCornSeeds"),   # ";82A9999" in HM-Decomp
}


def is_insn(code):
    m = INSN.match(code)
    return bool(m) and (m.group(1) or "").upper() not in DATA


def parse(decomp_dir):
    """(routines, lines): routines = {key: [name, instructions]}, key = the
    pc for labels with an address, ("noaddr", name) otherwise; lines = for
    every file, a list of (owner key, code) per line."""
    routines, lines = {}, {}
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(decomp_dir, "src", "code_banks", "*.asm"))):
        current, out = None, []
        for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read().split("\n"):
            a = ADDR.search(line)
            if a:
                ADDRESSES.setdefault((path, a.group(1).upper()), len(out))
            m = LABEL.match(line)
            code = line.split(";", 1)[0]
            if m:
                current = int(m.group(2), 16)
                routines.setdefault(current, [m.group(1), 0])
                code = m.group(1) + ":"     # kept so LOCAL can find the label
            else:
                t = ANY_TOP_LABEL.match(code)
                if t:
                    current = ("noaddr", t.group(1))
                    routines.setdefault(current, [t.group(1), 0])
            if current is not None and is_insn(code):
                routines[current][1] += 1
            out.append((current, code))
        lines[path] = out
    return routines, lines


# where each address comment is (";84BC9C;"): LOCAL entries may start or
# end at an address ("@84BC9C") for routines HM-Decomp gives no label
ADDR = re.compile(r";\s*([0-9A-Fa-f]{6})\s*;")
ADDRESSES = {}


def find_start(path, rows, label):
    if label.startswith("@"):
        return ADDRESSES.get((path, label[1:].upper()))
    return next((i for i, (_, c) in enumerate(rows)
                 if c.strip() == label + ":" or c.strip().startswith(label + ":")), None)


def split_locals(routines, lines, carved=None):
    carved = carved or {}
    for pc, entry in LOCAL.items():
        label, name = entry[0], entry[1]
        end = entry[2] if len(entry) > 2 else None     # up to this label, not the first RTL
        for path, rows in lines.items():
            start = find_start(path, rows, label)
            if start is None:
                continue
            stop = ADDRESSES.get((path, end[1:].upper())) if end and end.startswith("@") else None
            # each instruction is taken out of the block that owns its line
            # (the routine may end in another top-level label: `return85: RTL`)
            n = 0
            for j, (owner, code) in enumerate(rows[start:]):
                if stop is not None and start + j >= stop:
                    break
                if end and stop is None and j and code.strip().startswith(end + ":"):
                    break
                if is_insn(code):
                    # a line split_called already carved out (a routine
                    # called with JSL from elsewhere) stays in that routine
                    if (path, start + j) in carved:
                        continue
                    n += 1
                    routines[owner][1] -= 1
                    if not end and re.search(r"\bRT[LS]\b", code):
                        break
            routines[pc] = [name, n]
            break
    return routines


CALL = re.compile(r"\bJS[LR](?:\.[LW])?\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\b")
CODE_NAME = re.compile(r"^(?:CODE|SUB)_([0-9A-Fa-f]{6})$")


def split_called(routines, lines):
    """A label inside a block that is called (JSL / JSR) from another block
    is a routine of its own: HM-Decomp often writes several routines under
    one top-level label. Each is carved out, from its label to its first
    RTL / RTS, into a routine keyed by its address (CODE_xxxxxx) or name."""
    local_labels = {entry[0] for entry in LOCAL.values()}
    carved = {}
    callers = {}
    for rows in lines.values():
        for owner, code in rows:
            for target in CALL.findall(code):
                callers.setdefault(target, set()).add(owner)
    for path, rows in lines.items():
        for i, (owner, code) in enumerate(rows):
            m = re.match(r"^\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*):", code)
            if not m or m.group(1) in local_labels:
                continue
            name = m.group(1)
            if not (callers.get(name, set()) - {owner}):
                continue                      # only called from its own block
            k = CODE_NAME.match(name)
            key = int(k.group(1), 16) if k else ("split", name)
            if key in routines:
                continue
            n = 0
            for j, (own2, code2) in enumerate(rows[i:]):
                if j and ANY_TOP_LABEL.match(code2):
                    break
                if is_insn(code2):
                    n += 1
                    routines[own2][1] -= 1
                    carved[(path, i + j)] = key
                    if re.search(r"\bRT[LS]\b", code2):
                        break
            routines[key] = [name, n]
    return routines, carved


def routines_of(decomp_dir):
    found, lines = parse(decomp_dir)
    found, carved = split_called(found, lines)
    found = split_locals(found, lines, carved)
    return {k: (name, n) for k, (name, n) in found.items() if n > 0}


routines = routines_of


# Routines HM-Decomp shows as data (`dw` lines): rewritten and verified, but
# not counted, since the measure is HM-Decomp's own code.
NOT_IN_DECOMP = {0x81B121, 0x81B1CF, 0x81B21E,   # ReplaceTilesCoop, MountainCave, ElfTunnel
                 # extra checks of a part of a routine counted whole (a loop's
                 # frame entered on its own): Unk_NamesInput's, the intro's
                 0x82E95F, 0x82D80D, 0x82D93F, 0x82E0EB, 0x82E337}


def registered(path):
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    names = re.findall(r'\{\s*"([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)",\s*hm_\w+,[^{]*?0x([0-9A-Fa-f]{6})\b', text)
    return {int(pc, 16): name for name, pc in names if int(pc, 16) not in NOT_IN_DECOMP}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--decomp", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "..", "HM-Decomp"))
    ap.add_argument("--update-readme", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    all_r = routines(a.decomp)
    done = registered(os.path.join(ROOT, "src", "hm_decomp.c"))
    missing = [n for pc, n in done.items() if pc not in all_r]
    if missing:
        print("progress: not found in HM-Decomp: " + ", ".join(missing), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    total_insn = sum(n for _, n in all_r.values())
    done_insn = sum(all_r[pc][1] for pc in done)
    pct = 100.0 * done_insn / total_insn
    pct_r = 100.0 * len(done) / len(all_r)
    summary = (f"{pct:.2f}% of the code ({done_insn} of {total_insn} instructions), "
               f"{len(done)} of {len(all_r)} routines ({pct_r:.1f}%)")
    print(summary)

    if a.update_readme:
        blocks = {
            "README.md": (
                f"![Rewritten in C: {pct:.2f}%](https://img.shields.io/badge/rewritten%20in%20C-{pct:.2f}%25-2f855a)\n\n"
                f"**{pct:.2f}%** of the game's code rewritten in C and verified: "
                f"{done_insn} of {total_insn} instructions, "
                f"{len(done)} of {len(all_r)} routines ({pct_r:.1f}%).\n"
                f"Computed with `python3 tools/progress.py --decomp ../HM-Decomp` "
                f"over the HM-Decomp disassembly."),
            "README.es.md": (
                f"![Reescrito en C: {pct:.2f}%](https://img.shields.io/badge/reescrito%20en%20C-{pct:.2f}%25-2f855a)\n\n"
                f"**{pct:.2f}%** del código del juego reescrito en C y verificado: "
                f"{done_insn} de {total_insn} instrucciones, "
                f"{len(done)} de {len(all_r)} rutinas ({pct_r:.1f}%).\n"
                f"Se calcula con `python3 tools/progress.py --decomp ../HM-Decomp` "
                f"sobre el desensamblado de HM-Decomp."),
        }
        for fname, body in blocks.items():
            path = os.path.join(ROOT, fname)
            text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
            block = "<!-- progress -->\n" + body + "\n<!-- /progress -->"
            new, n = re.subn(r"<!-- progress -->.*?<!-- /progress -->", lambda m: block, text, flags=re.S)
            if not n:
                print(f"progress: {fname} has no <!-- progress --> block", file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(new)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
